Are you gonna do this thing for me? Dwight? [David knocks on Michael's door and opens door] Hey David, how are you? Good to see you. Nice surprise. Dwight and I were just having a very unfortunate conversation.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: That's too bad.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Yes it is, but it had to be done, didn't it?

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Hopefully, nothing that can't be undone because Dwight I owe you an apology. The head of Blue Cross just called. They were so excited about the golden ticket discount that they have decided to make Dunder Mifflin their exclusive provider of all office supplies. Congratulations Dwight. [holds out hand for handshake]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: David… you're welcome. [Dwight and David shake hands and make exclamations]

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: I just want to say that this golden ticket idea is one of the most brilliant signs of initiative I have ever seen at this company and how about a big round of applause for Mr. Dwight Schrute? [everyone starts clapping]

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Alright Dwight. This is huge.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: That's what she said! [David laughs]

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Hey, Dwight, great idea. Dwight, Dwight, great idea. How'd you come up with that idea?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Inspiration.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Really? How did– how are you inspired? How did it pop into your head Dwight?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [same time as Michael] You never know when it's gonna strike. Just… boom.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Give me the details of how that happened.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: You, you are taking about Dwight Schrute. The biggest Wonka fan I know. I mean, you've been talking about that movie for years.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: What?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: And you know what? I even made fun of you when you dressed up as Willy Wonka to pitch this idea and for that I apologize.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Apology rejected.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: [going up to give Dwight a hug] Thanks for much for helping the company, Dwight.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh Pam.

scenes.speaker: Creed
scenes.line: Good work, kid.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Thanks old man.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: This, this is great. OH, OK, look I want to get you on the horn with the marketing people in New York. The should meet you.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Pam, could you set up a call in there in about 15 minutes, please?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Sure.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: David? David?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [same time as Michael] 'Cause I've got this idea…

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: David?

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Yeah?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Could I be a part of the meeting also?

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: You probably have too much to do around here. I don't want to uh, take up your time with another meeting.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yeah, let's face it. This meeting sounds like it's Wonka fans only. He's never seen the movie. [David laughs]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Alright.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: [on speakerphone] Hey guys, I have with me Dwight Schrute. Dwight, take it away.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: OK guys, listen up. Here's the deal. I love candy. Sweet sugary candy from the second it touches my tongue to the moment it's metabolized by my stomach acids, so naturally I liked Willy Wonka.

scenes.speaker: Man on phone
scenes.line: Wait, do you guys hear that? There's not a dog listening in, is there? [cut to show Michael on the other line] I hear panting.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: No. No dogs.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: So I love Willy Wonka. That golden ticket scene is so inspiring to me that that's where I cam up with that idea [Michael comes into conference room].

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: There is no movie called Willy Wonka. It's called Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: It's actually based on a book called Charlie and the Chocolate Factory.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Pam…

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I can't… vouch for that. But I do know this. He is a liar. He has taken my idea.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: That is my idea.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: [on phone] We are gonna call you back guys. [to Michael] What is going on here?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: OK, here's what happened, David. It was all my idea. You called me and you were really angry at me and I got scared, so I had Dwight take the fall, but now, it turns out that it's a great idea and Dwight will not confess. Can you believe that?

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: No, no.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: It is my idea.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh how dare you.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: It is my idea. I'm filled with good ideas. Thousands of good ideas.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: You are? Good ideas, huh? Hey, did you come up with toilet buddy? It's a net, circular net, that you put inside the toilet to catch all of your change and your wallet from falling into the toilet? Formally known as toilet guard?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Horse Boat.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh please.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: A canoe built around your horse so you can go from riding to water travel without slowing down. Horse Boat!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Toilet sponge. It's a hollowed out sponge…

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh give me a break.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: …that is more absorbent, and softer than toilet paper. I have a lot of toilet ideas.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: That's because they're easy!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: They're not easy. Everybody has to go to the bathroom.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [same time as Michael] Women's urinals… uh…

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: [same time as Michael and Dwight] Guys, guys. OK, enough. Please, enough. What, is this true, Dwight? I mean, is this true?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Yes, it's Michael's idea that he forced on me on threat of death.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Thank You!

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: What, I don't — what do you want me to do now, Michael? What am I supposed to do now?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well David, I will be honest with you. I do want the credit without any of the blame.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: OK, uhh… I am going back to New York. Pam, do me a favor, don't send me those notes.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: OK.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: I am gone.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: When they look back on this day in the history books all that will be remembered is that I had a good idea. And that's what I am going to write down in my diary. That is what I want you to write down in yours.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh I am. In my own words.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I want to see it.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: No.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I want to see it. [Michael gets up to try to see Dwight's diary]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: No, Michael.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Give me… Give me the diary.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: No! [Michael struggles to take Dwight's diary from his hand]

scenes.speaker: Lynn
scenes.line: Hi.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Lynn, I'm just gonna say to you everything that I am thinking.

scenes.speaker: Lynn
scenes.line: OK.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: I think you have the best smile. I'd like to take you out to dinner and a movie.

scenes.speaker: Lynn
scenes.line: OK.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Nice. [Both laugh] Boobs. [Lynn blushes]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Well, it's uh, his funeral. So… neh!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Ding dong.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Who is it?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: KGB.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Alright. I just got out of the shower, I'll be one second.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [in accent] When you are done, open the door. … Hello in there?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yeah, I'm late for work, so I have to brush my teeth, it's a whole routine.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: We have more houses to visit.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: If you want to come back then, that'll be fine.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: We will come back at… how is [looks at watch] 4:45?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I get back from work around 6.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: How about 5:15?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: You can try. That, that might work.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Very well, we will come back at 5:15.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Alright.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Michael, since it is your fifteenth anniversary at the company, I thought it might be appropriate to begin the festivities with a fifteen-minute round of applause.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I like it.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Followed by a fifteen minute moment of silence.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [wearing a tuxedo] I don't know. Is it classy enough?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Jim! Enough with the classy, ok?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I just feel like after fifteen years at this company, bravo by the way, that we should celebrate with a very classy event, a night to remember.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I think you're right. This party has to have all the excitement, drama and intrigue of my time here.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: And of course, classy.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: And classy, yeah.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Michael, you're just agreeing with him because he's wearing a tux. Don't you see what he's doing here?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Last week, Dwight sent out a memo about the dress code. So, this is me showing him that I'm taking it very seriously.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh, here's one:

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Hi, can I help you?

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Yeah, I'm Charles Miner, here to see Michael Scott.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Sure. Just one second. Please have a seat.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [on speakerphone] Yes?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Michael, there's a Charles Miner here to see you.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Miner? I hardly know her!… Hello?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Yeah, are you coming out now?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Uh-huh. [comes out of office] Well, well, well, who have we here? Ah, it is Prince Charles Miner. [shakes Charles' hand] At your service. Everybody, this is Sir Charles Miner and he is the new VP for the Northeast region. So, just give it up for this big guy, right? Give it up. [leads round of applause] Here he is.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: I-I was-

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Wow! Hold that thought. I want everybody to go into the break room. I have a little surprise for you. Go ahead. You too. Dwight, would you escort our guest in there? C'mon, here we go, don't be shy, don't be shy, you're one of us . [whispers] Dwight, stall him a little, I have to get the fish.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Really wish you would have told me the new boss was coming today.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: What? No, I didn't want to make everybody nervous.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Nope. I mean, I could have brought a change of clothes, or-

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: You look dynamite. What are you talking about? Very slick. Ok, get the fish.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Originally founded in 1866, Scranton quickly became one of Pennsylvania's largest anthracite coal-mining communities.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Surprise, there is nothing in here. The real surprise is in the conference room. Let's go! [swings arm above head for everyone to come, hits doorframe] Oh! God! Ok, come on, come on!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: We'll finish it up later, but essentially what we're talking about is…

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Surprise! [unveils bagels sitting on table] As you can see, I turned the bagels from O's into C's, for Charles.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Thank you.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Took me all night.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: This is what you did last night?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I met this guy at corporate last week and we were just digging each other's vibe. I was totally grooving on him and vice-versa. And besides, the last two people to have his job were Jan and Ryan. The former was my lover, and the latter my best friend. So, who knows? I do. [in British cockney accent] It's gonna be mental! It's going to be mental.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: My god, he's like a black George Clooney.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: Really? I don't see it. I mean, he's ok, he's not unattractive, it's. . .

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey, how you doing? Jim Halpert, sales. Just wanted to say, if you need anything, let me know.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Why are you wearing a tuxedo?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I didn't think you'd notice. [laughs nervously] Uh, it's funny actually, there's another salesman out here, Dwight Schrute, and he sent out this memo, as he always does, and, uh, it was about professionalism in the workplace. Of course, he singled me out. So I just had to mess with him.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Uh.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh, you'd understand if you read the memo which I should probably get you, there's probably one in a drawer… uh. It was pretty crazy. But, uh, not more crazy than wearing a tux, at work, I grant you that… so, uh.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Your name is Jim?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Jim Halpert, yep. So, um, just going to let you get back to it… [being pulled away by Pam]

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: He just had to wear his tux today.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I thought it'd be funny.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Took him 40 minutes to get ready.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: All right, let me introduce you to some of the troops. Accounting, front and center. Come on up here. I'd like you to meet somebody. This is the accounting department.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Hey, I come from accounting, too.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh, nerd alert!

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Ni-

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: This is Oscar Martinez. He is Latino. And he just got out of a long-term relationship with a man, Gil, who broke his heart. But he didn't bring any of that into work, it did not affect his job performance whatsoever and I am very proud of him for that.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Hey, Oscar, it's good to meet you.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: This little hell-raiser is Angela. She has slept with a bunch of different guys in the office. One over there, in the orange [points to Andy]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Hey-o!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: There you go! Where's the other?

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: You know, Michael, I don't need to know everyone's sexual history.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well, perfect, because we have now arrived at Kevin and he has no sexual history.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Hey!

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: How about I just say hi to everyone at one time?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Good. Good, good, good. Everyone, please give it up for Charles Miner. [claps]

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Thank you, Michael. Thank you for the C-shaped bagels.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh! Well…

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: That's great.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Above and beyond.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Hey, you know we're in tough times and we're not immune to this economy.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: That's true.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: But the goal is to, you know, fight our way through this.

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: [clears throat, raises his hand] Stanley Hudson. Are there gonna be layoffs?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No. Absolutely not.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Uh, hold on, Michael, thank you. Uh, Stanley, you know, we can't make any promises, but we'll try everything in our power to avoid that.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Do you have specifics?

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Sp-Well, um, Michael should have filled you in last week.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well, due to the economy, there is a lot of worry going around. I didn't want to worry people.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: You didn't tell them.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well, why don't-

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Yeah, I will. What I told Michael last week-

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Charles is going to tell you.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Is that we are cutting three percent across the board, which means we will no longer be matching 401k contributions. All overtime requests will need to come through the corporate office.

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: Fantastic.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well, it's not official.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: It is official. It is official. And actually, guys, I'm encouraging branches to consider a freeze on discretionary spending.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Such as salary, benefits, etc, etc. Insurance.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: No, no, not salaries. Petty cash, supplies, and uh, you know, parties.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well-

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: What about your party?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Ok, ok, you know what? I think this has been great. I think this gives us a lot to think about, doesn't it? Charles Miner, ladies and gentlemen. [starts round of applause] He has a long trip home. Thank you for coming in. We have to get back to work.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Michael, I'm going to stay for the day.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh no, no, no. You don't have to do that. I've got this covered. This was just a meet-and-greet.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: No, it's a little bit more than that. I'm going to set up in here, ok?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I am thrilled that the new boss has taken such an active interest in all of the responsibilities that I'm supposed to have. Thrilled.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [on speakerphone] David, it was my understanding that I was not going to be managed.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: What gave you that idea?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: It was my understanding.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: I see.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Listen, why don't we just leave that position vacant? Truth be told, I think I thrive under a lack of accountability.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Look, Michael, Charles is very qualified. Get to know him. I really think the two of you are going to make a great team.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: But the branch is still mine?

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: You're still the branch manager, yes, and if you need anything else at all, just let Charles know.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Ask him about the party.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh, right. David, are you coming to my fifteenth anniversary party?

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: I'll give it my best shot, Michael.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: No the other thing.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh, ok. If we hire Cirque de Soleil as salaried employees, will that help us with year-end tax stuff? [several seconds of silence]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: He hung up?

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: No.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I just got off the horn with David Wallace, and he said that you and I should try to get to know each other better. And I agree, so what I would like you to do is tell me something that you've never told anybody before.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: No.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Come on. What's your wife's name? Where did you work before you came here?

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Saticoy Steel.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Beautiful. See, African-Americans have such a rich history of unusual names.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: No, I worked at a company called Saticoy Steel.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: You're not from paper?

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: No.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Does David know this?

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Yeah, he knows. He just wants a good manager.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well that, actually, is an excellent segue into really what is my only point-

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: And what is that?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: And that- I-I don't need to be managed, Charles. And if you want pick up some tips, observing here, and take them to the other branches, it's all good. But Jan would mostly come by when she was super horny, and Ryan would come by to visit his parents and do laundry, so… Are we clear?

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: That's not how I plan on doing things.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Ok, alright, well I'll just bounce that off David, see what comes back.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: I'll tell David what he needs to know. Sorry. David wants it this way.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Whatever David wants.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Ok.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [on phone] Michael Scott calling for David. Well, just tell him to call me ASAP as possible. Thanks.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh, Michael, come on, no. You have to charm 'em. [calls back on speakerphone]

scenes.speaker: Stephanie
scenes.line: David Wallace's office.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Hey there, gorgeous. How you doing today?

scenes.speaker: Stephanie
scenes.line: Good. Thank you.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: How's it hanging?

scenes.speaker: Stephanie
scenes.line: Alright. . .

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Good. Listen, my name is, uh, Michael… Scotch. And, uh, I just wanted to say that, uh, I've got David Wallace's son in the trunk of my car. If he doesn't get on this phone in 5 seconds-

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No! You idiot! [hangs up] Idiot, idiot, idiot! What are you doing? God! Oh my god. [redials]

scenes.speaker: Stephanie
scenes.line: David Wallace's office.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Hi Stephanie, it's Michael Scott again. I just spoke with Michael Scotch and the son's going to be returned, everything's fine.

scenes.speaker: Stephanie
scenes.line: Michael…

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: And I really really need to talk to David.

scenes.speaker: Stephanie
scenes.line: Please hold.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: [on cell phone] Charles Miner. Hello? Hello, who is this? Who is this?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I was never given a name. [hangs up, he and Dwight sigh in relief]

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: [to delivery men] Uh, hi, can I help you? I don't think anyone here-

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Oh, uh, Pam? Hey everyone, lunch is on me today.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: That is so unnecessary!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Are you kidding me with this? On the day that I bring in breakfast?

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: It's no big deal.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I wish you had told us sooner, because I was going to go to the vending machine and get an egg salad.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: You still have that option. [Michael sighs]

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: Thanks again, Charles.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: Thank you.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Nobody thanked me.

scenes.speaker: Jim

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: We can't help you if you don't just tell us what happened.

scenes.speaker: Michael

scenes.line: Hey, Jim.

scenes.line: Yeah, well, with you it's different, okay? Cause I just- I just suck. I just- I suck!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Tuna, be nice to my friend Jim, ok?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Why? When I look in the mirror, I don't like the face that looks back.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Well, so what? Your body's a ten.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Forget it.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Jim.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I said forget it. [drop kicks lunch across room, stomps on it]

scenes.line: [on phone] Dwight Schrute.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Hello, traitor.

scenes.line: I think you have the wrong number, Michael.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I want you to listen to me, friend, and I want you to listen to me good. I am going to come at you, and I am going to come at you hard. I am going to steal all of your clients, and then I am going to kill them in front of you.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Michael!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I'm just getting hardcore with him.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Finally.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Yes, and hear me, Dwight, when I say I brought you into this world, and I can take you out. [hangs up] Bill Cosby.

scenes.line: [on phone] Mr. Schofield, please?

scenes.speaker: Secretary
scenes.line: He's in a meeting.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Dammit! [hangs up]

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [on phone] Is Mr. Schofield there?

scenes.speaker: Automated phone voice
scenes.line: If you'd like to reach an outside line, please dial nine first. [Michael sighs, hangs up phone]

scenes.line: So, you think Michael's going after the whale, huh?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I have a long term relationship with Harper Collins publishers and Mr. Schofield. I'm not worried.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: You sound worried.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: And you have bad skin. Oh, look everyone, we're all making observations! [gibberish sounds]

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [on phone] Well, if you could do me a big favor and tell Mr. Schofield that Michael Scott has tickets to the Wilkes-Barre Penguins game this weekend, and if he would like to join me… Hello, Daniel. How are you? Uh-huh. I sure do. Yes. [referencing rolodex card] Wanted to ask, did Kathy ever make JV?

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Look at that old dude and his rolodex go.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I spent a month putting that rolodex on his Blackberry, which he now uses as a nightlight.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Wow. High score?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: And no, I cannot lower my current prices. [phone rings] Hold on. Hello? Mr. Schofield, thank you so much for taking the time to talk. I wanted to discuss your contract with us- oh, you're considEring him. I thought Michael Scott left the paper business after his nervous breakdown.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Michael has been talking to my biggest client. Master and apprentice pitted against one another for the fate of the greater Scranton area paper market. So it's not exactly like 'Highlander,' but still…

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Hello, Dwight, I've been expecting your call. What do you want?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I would like to arrange a truce.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: So you heard Schofield is considEring a switch, and you want mercy?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Meet me in our spot in four minutes.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No. No. You think I am going to fall for that? There's no-

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Michael.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Meet- Ok, go to the spot and then walk 100 feet.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: In which direction?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Toward the sun.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: At what time?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Noon.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: That-

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: You have two seconds. [Dwight starts running]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [looking at his watch] Michael. [Madge walks by] Sorry.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Dwight.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Michael.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I hope you're not recording this conversation. [Dwight drops his pants and lifts up his shirt] Good. I cannot believe that you sided with Charles.

scenes.line: You were making me do things that were not all right.

scenes.line: So you just rat me out? You could have said no.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: And not come through for you?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: If you want a truce, I will give you a truce.

scenes.line: I want a truce.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I do too.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Let me take you and your whole company out for lunch at Alfredo's.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Cooper's.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I had fish yesterday.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Damn it.

scenes.line: [Michael, Ryan and Pam sitting at restaurant, phone rings] Oh. Dwight-elicious. Where you at?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh, hi, Michael. I'm so sorry I'm late. I got stuck in traffic.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Really? That's weird. We didn't see any.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I hit a bear.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: What?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: He's technically fine. I imagine the true horror will be when he wakes up in a zoo. [throws a fish into the vent at Michael's office] Hey, listen, will you do me a favor and order the meatball parm for me, with extra cheese?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Yeah, sure.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Ok, I will see you very soon, alright? [takes all the items off Michael's desk and puts them into briefcase, including rolodex]

scenes.line: Okay, see you in a bit. Dwight hit a bear. He'll be here in a sec.

scenes.line: [Pam, Ryan and Michael enter office] Sounds neat.

scenes.line: We can spend a couple days there.

scenes.line: Oh my God, I think we've been robbed!

scenes.line: [Michael answers phone] Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Did you enjoy your lunch?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Dwight, not now, we've been robbed.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: No, Michael, you were sabotaged.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No, Dwight, we were robbed. How would you even know? You're still stuck in traffic. [Pam holds up sign saying "Dwight did it!!"] You?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Me.

scenes.line: What about our truce?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I broke it.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: On purpose?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Why?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: You think this is some kind of game? No, this is a war, and I will not stop, I will not rest. You have no idea what kind of enemy you've created. You have unleashed the wolf!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Be that as it may, I have your meatball parm sandwich here, and I am going to eat it.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: And I knew that you would do that. The meatball parm is their worst sandwich!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh. [bites into sandwich, looks disgusted] Bastard!

scenes.line: Hi there. Dwight Schrute here. I was just calling to see if Michael Scott Paper was meeting all of your paper needs, and how is [reading off rolodex card] Brenda, age four, ponytail, and Simon, age 7? Oh, you don't say.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [holding up rolodex card] Schrute comma Dwight. And on the back he wrote, "great salesman, better friend." [turns card over] "Tall" and "beets."

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: And say hello to Cheri, who is your black wife. [hangs up and answers cell phone] I see you're begging for mercy, huh? Well, you will find none here.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Dwight, do you mind if we talk?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Sure. That'd be fine.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: If you keep coming after us, the Michael Scott Paper Company cannot succeed.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: This is war and that is what happens.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh, one more thing. I'm going to have you listen while I steal your biggest client.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh, no. No. No. No. No.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh, uh oh, I'm turning you down right now.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Michael! Michael!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: You can hear me, but I can't hear you.

scenes.line: Mr. Schofield's ready to see you now, Mr. Scott.

scenes.line: Oh, great. Mr. Schofield's ready to see me. Thank you so much.

scenes.line: Don't let him in! He's a traitor! Michael!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Walking in the door…

scenes.speaker: Mr. Schofield
scenes.line: Michael, good to see you.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Mr. Schofield, good to see you. And I'm closing the door. [Dwight runs out of the office]

scenes.line: Really?

scenes.line: Yes. He does not have the authority to say that. I, on the other hand, am the president, the owner, and the founder. It is like you are buying software from Bill Gates.

scenes.line: Are you saying you invented paper?

scenes.line: [hugging a crying Jim] Okay, okay.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh, God.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Okay, Tuna.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: Hey, guys.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Hello.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Excuse me, can I have your attention, everyone? Here's the deal, everybody, Jim Halpert is very upset and disturbed. I don't know if it was something you did, something you said, a look you gave him, maybe it was nothing at all, but here's the deal, ok? It stops now.

scenes.line: I guess I could be nicer.

scenes.line: Andy, I think Jim is messing with you.

scenes.line: Oh, really?

scenes.line: Mm-hmm. [looks over to Jim smiling through windows to the kitchen]

scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.line: Yeah, okay, what the heck is happennin' here?

scenes.line: Two things I need you to understand. One, Pam and I are very happy together.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Uh, that's not what was-

scenes.line: And two, that stuff that happened with you and Angela is a bummer, and I know you don't think you're ever gonna find someone else, but you will. I promise you, you will.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Oh man, he got me so good. I learned something about myself today. Yeah. I wish this was a sofa, cause I feel like I could sit here and talk for hours.

scenes.line: What is that thing that Dwight always says? Paper is the soil in which the seeds of business grow?

scenes.line: It's not the soil! It's the manure! Paper is the manure! On-time delivery is the soil! Aah! [runs into office]

scenes.line: Uh, hello, Dwight.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Spin move.

scenes.speaker: Secretary
scenes.line: Oh-

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Ha ha! April 13th, 2002.

scenes.speaker: Mr. Schofield
scenes.line: Dwight, I'm in a meeting.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: That's very rude.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I barge because I care. April 13th, 2002, that is the date when you tried to switch paper providers for an obscure sociology textbook, but were hung out to dry when the price of glossy stock increased.

scenes.speaker: Mr. Schofield
scenes.line: Maybe we should schedule a meeting on our-

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: La la la! Continuing. Notice my persistence and recall. Continuing! You called Dunder Mifflin, and your order was filled within an hour!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I'm going to pull a date out of the air right now. April 13th, 2002. That is the last day that you evaluated your paper needs. Is it not? We all know that the economy is bad, and bloated companies like Dunder Mifflin…

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Come on.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Are going to fall by the wayside. Two of their branches have closed within the last year. The Michael Scott Paper Company, however, has opened a new branch this very month.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: What he's not telling you is that he will abandon you.

scenes.speaker: Mr. Schofield
scenes.line: Why don't you guys just e-mail me your best offers and we can finish it up that way?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: That sounds like a fantastic idea. I will see you this weekend for the Penguins. Box seats as usual.

scenes.speaker: Mr. Schofield
scenes.line: Uh, ok, sure.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Good, good, good. I will see you.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Thank you, Mr. Schofield, for your time. Much appreciated. Oh, and tell me, um, how's your gay son?

scenes.speaker: Mr. Schofield
scenes.line: Excuse me?

scenes.line: I color code all my info. I wrote "gay son" in green. Green means go, so I know to go ahead and shut up about it. Orange means "Orange you glad you didn't bring it up?" Most colors mean "Don't say it."

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: How is Tom, the homosexual sophomore?

scenes.line: I wanted to start a company, not a war. Because in a war, you always fight those you are closest to. And the great tragedy of the civil war is that brother fought against brother. For what? What purpose did that serve? Apart from abolishing slavery? In that case, war was the right choice. This doesn't feel as important though. That's just how the world works, I guess.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: He gives me leads and I take the leads from him and in exchange it makes him feel good. And if a friend can't make you feel good, then I don't want any friends. Except Dwight, because he is our only source of fertile leads.

scenes.line: Dwight just got Howard Family Dry Cleaners.

scenes.line: Uncle Dave?

scenes.line: He's undercutting us big time. He's actually taking a loss and paying the difference out of pocket.

scenes.line: That's my family. When you mess with my family, I can't be responsible for my actions.

scenes.line: When are you ever responsible for your actions?

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Get off my ass, you hag.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Hey, hey, hey. Something about that seems inappropriate.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Betrayal ain't just a river in Egypt.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Who is that knocking on my taste buds? Why, it's Mr. Lemon. Hmmm, nice to meet you.

scenes.line: It's good. But won't it feel weird cutting into a cross?

scenes.line: Don't think of it as a cross in the Judeo-Christian sense, think of it more as a symbol of your lives crossing in marriage.

scenes.line: When I think of it like that, I do not think of the other connotations.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yes!

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I don't think so, Andy.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Sorry. Her day.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Hey, bud.

scenes.line: Are they looking at me?

scenes.line: Who?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Everyone. Everyone just keeps looking at me.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Are you sure?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Will you just talk to them, please? Pam just knew!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: It's 4:30 in the morning. Do you know where your kids are? If you are Ryan's parents or Pam's parents or my parents, you do. They're gonna be in this van. With me. Who am I? Nothing to fear. I am just a 44 year old guy with a paper route.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [honking horn] Time to make the donuts. [laughs and drives away as Ryan tries to get in the van] Come on. Whoa! No, I promise I won't do it again. Come on. [does it again] De-nied!

scenes.line: We've been making 5:00 AM deliveries for a couple weeks now. Ever since I've gotten clean there's something about fresh morning air that… just really makes me sick.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Hello! Time to make the donuts! Oh, Halpert! Whoa! Boner patrol. Arrest that man! Your donuts make me go nuts! [laughs] Hey Pam.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: We got the van at a used car lot. We think it says "Alleluia Church of Scranton." in Korean. It was either this or an old school bus with an owl living in it.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: You didn't happen to bring any coffee, did you, Michael?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Milk and sugar.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Oh, awesome. You're a life saver. [drinks from coffee cup] Wait, is this just milk and sugar?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: That's what I said.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Do you drink this every day?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Every morning.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: We're, uh, we're doing okay. A couple weeks in and, um, we're having fun. Uh, yep. We have 20– of those.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: [an Asian lady tries to enter the van] Oh, oh, excuse me! Sorry. Sorry, no. It's, uh, it's a paper company now. It's not for the church.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Okay, who covers Bans Pet Grooming?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh, they're my client.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: No, they were your client. They just called and told us they're switching over to Michael Scott Paper Company.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [sighs] Shame, Jim. I expected more.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: In the last month we have lost ten major clients to Michael Scott.

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: What are we supposed to do? They keep undercutting us on price.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: I don't want to hear excuses. I want to see improvements. This is unacceptable.

scenes.line: Hey, Boss. Uh, I'd just like to point out that I have been here less time than these guys.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Why are you telling me this?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I just think the bar should be lower for a newbie.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Is this something you really want to have said?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I don't want to have said that. But I think it's important that you know it.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: I don't know what to do to inspire these people. Okay, maybe it's my fault-

scenes.line: It's not your fault. Some people just don't want to be inspired.

scenes.line: I wrote a memo to all departments asking them to find ways to save money but, uh–

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: Charles, I got your memo. Thank you. I want you to know I'm putting my foot down when it comes to expense reports. Waste not, want not.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: Uh, well said, Angela.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Been there, done that.

scenes.line: You know what we need? We need some couches in here.

scenes.line: Michael, we should really consider getting a delivery guy.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh, you know what you would love? Is if we built a loft.

scenes.line: Why would I love that? Can we afford a delivery guy?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Like in a dorm room. You put your desk underneath, you have your loft up top. You can sleep up top.

scenes.line: Yeah, I know what a loft is.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Most dorm rooms don't even have that.

scenes.line: Most do in the magazines.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Let's see what a delivery guy costs.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: We should look into that. Or we just go for the loft.

scenes.line: Hey, David.

scenes.line: David Wallace! Hello, we've been expecting you, David Wallace. Charles and I were waiting for you.

scenes.line: There he is. There he is. How was the trip up?

scenes.line: A lot better than a month at the Scranton Radisson, I'm sure.

scenes.line: Oh, you know it hasn't been that bad. Hasn't been that bad. These people are the salt of the earth down here. You couldn't ask for a better way to learn a company.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Hmmm.

scenes.speaker: Charles
scenes.line: I feel like I should be thanking you.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Uh.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [makes kissing, puckEring sound]

scenes.line: The conference room is ready if we want to get started.
