scenes.line: You give me a gift– Bam! Thank you note. You invite me somewhere– Pow! RSVP. You do me a favor– Wham! Favor returned. Do not test my politeness.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Let me get that door for you– [runs to open door]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Whoa–

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: There you go!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Thank you very much. Now I've got it for you. [holds open door]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh… goodness… thanks. You know, here's a healthy fitness tip. If you clench your buttocks together while walking you can really take the pressure off your knees.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Is that right?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Observe. [walks towards desk]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Huh. [laughs; follows Dwight]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Right?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: That really works.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Yeah, feel free to use that. Anytime. Okay.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Hey– oh, hold on a second. Do not walk around with your jacket cattywampus.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [straightens Andy's tie] And that needs to be straight as an arrow.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Whoa– thank you very much. [takes off Dwight's glasses and blows on them] Oh boy.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Thank you very much for that.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [puts Dwight's glasses back on Dwight's face] You are very welcome.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [pulls out Andy's chair] Have a seat. Allow me.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [pulls out Dwight's chair] Have a seat yourself.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: You know what? I am going to preemptively change the batteries in your wireless mouse.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Not necessary.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: No, no, no! [takes mouse and runs away]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: You didn't have to do that.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Andy is complicating things. But I'm not worried. This will only up my game.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Hello. Scott. Table for four.

scenes.speaker: Hostess
scenes.line: Welcome Scott family. It'll be just a moment.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I use to love coming here. The chicken parm is good. Big part of my childhood. Oh, maybe Michael will start dating that too.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: What table should we take? So many to choose from.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Wow.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: [sees table decorated with a banner and balloons] Oh my God!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: What? All I see are boring old tables with no birthday decorations. Oh, wait a second! You mean this one? Wow!

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Michael, you did all this?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Not about taking credit. Let's just say we all did it.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: Well, thank you. All of you.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well, it was actually me alone, so– wow look at this place. Really makes me want to go to Italy some day.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: Oh you'll love it. You can have my guide books. I think I'm done with those really long plane rides.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh. Thank you. Thanks for lending me the books.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: So, mom… which birthday are we celebrating this year?

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: [laughs] Sticking with 49.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: 49 again? That's nine years in a row. This is now our longest family tradition.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: That's funny.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: Well, as long as you're running numbers Pam, then help me out with this one. Let's see your six months pregnant, but you've only been married for 30 days, so what does that add up to?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh, burn. Burn on you… and a little bit on me, too. [they laugh]

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: You're 54 years old.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: No. I'm 58.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: You're 58 years old?

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: Uh huh.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Congratulations.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: The only time you should care about a woman's age is if she is too young for you and I am not robbing the cradle. If anything I am robbing the grave.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Mom, have you decided what you want to be called?

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: Oh, well I like Nana, but I also like the classic Grandma.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Please be Grandma.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Definitely Grandma.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I want you to be Grandma.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: Oh, Michael what do you think? Grandma?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [nods uncomfortably] That–

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Yay, Grandma!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Hey, would you guys ever do a triathlon, do you think?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Maybe.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Helene?

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: Oh, oh no. I don't think so.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I am. I'm definitely going to do it. I've already got the run and the bike thing down. Just need to learn how to swim. Come on, you in?

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: Oh no, I think a triathlon is pretty much something I can rule out. It just– doesn't interest me.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: So it's a matter of interest. Good, okay. It's not anything you would have ever done.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: Hmm… I might have done it when I was younger, but now there's just other things I'd rather be doing, instead of running and jumping and swimming–

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well there's no jumping in a triathlon.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: Oh–

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: You're thinking of the broad jump. Would you try– bungee jumping?

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: No, no… [laughs]

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Snowboarding?

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: You want to go snowboarding?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I might.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: Michael, what are you talking about?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [sighs] Nothing. Just life– and doing things– before you die. I don't know.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Do I really want to go snowboarding? No. But I would like to if I wanted to.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [singing fanfare] Aye-yi-yi! [lifts covers off trays of food]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: What's going on in here?

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Andy bought lunch.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh… no… really?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yep, yep. Took a page right out of the old Schrute book of niceness.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: There is no book. There's only a survival guide.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: You bought breakfast for everyone, so I got lunch for everyone.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Okay, well, allow me. You know what– gosh these tacos are awfully complicated to make. I will make everyone's tacos! Gra-ga-ga-ga-ga!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: So we should get the check?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: What about your gift Michael?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh, no, no, no. No. It's stupid. You'd hate it. I hate it.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: I'm sure I won't.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Yes you will.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: He locked himself in his office all morning working on it.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: Gimme. Look at this wrapping paper. It's got the word love on it in every language.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Aww–

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I literally– I put no thought into the wrapping at all. Might as well of been toilet paper.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: [opens present, reads inscription] A scrapbook of our first memories by Michael Gary Scott. For my girlfriend Helene on your birthday. [laughs]

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: That's just an arbitrary title.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: Ok, there's a penny. What's that from?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Penny for your thoughts.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: It was from the wishing well at the mall. You threw it in. I went back later, waded in and I found it.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Wow.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: That's amazing.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: It's not amazing… at all. It's sort of weird that I went and did that. And now your wish won't come true, so that blows.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: [looking through the book] A poem!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh that I plagiarized I think.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: [reading] I can not go to school today said little Peggy Ann McKay…

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [whispers to Pam] Shel Silverstein.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: Um– I have the measles and the mumps, a gash, a rash and purple bumps. And my teachers really mean– Happy Birthday , I love you Helene.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: That's really nice Michael.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I think it sucks.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: I think it's wonderful, absolutely wonderful.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well, that's because you and I have very different tastes and you like lame things. It's a generational– sort of gap between us.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: [hugging book] God… it's a scrapbook.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Home run Michael.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: You set the bar so high.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: That was a bunt.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Whoa, whoa Dwight. I'm going to do this.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Hey, hey, hey– relax I got it covered.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: No, I insist.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: No, no, no, no, no, no, I insist. [pushes Andy out of the room and locks the door]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Ok, Dwight this is ridiculous.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Don't worry about it. You can just owe me.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Hey. Where'd you go?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh, just went to the bathroom.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: And then you stopped at the bar on the way back?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I got thirsty.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Okay, weirdo. Come on. It's time for cake.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Honestly, for a long time I thought I was going to grow old with Holly. And then I met Helene. And she is great and she already knows and has done everything that I have ever wanted to do and can tell me about it. But, I think I want to do those things myself.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Cakes really good.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: Oh, I know. I love how they use butter cream frosting.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Finish your cake, Helene.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: Hmmm?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I want you to enjoy that cake because I have something terrible I need to tell you. I want you to enjoy your cake before I tell you this terrible, terrible thing.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Helene I think you're a wonderful person and I– God– I've enjoyed dating you and being your boyfriend so much. But I have to consider Pam's feelings as a friend and a co-worker I can not in good conscience continue to date you, when I know what this is doing to her.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Michael. Michael ,it's okay.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No it's not.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I know that it took me a little while to come around and its still a little weird to get used to, but you obviously make my mom very happy. And that makes me happy.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Wow. That just– you've really grown.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Well–

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [covEring eyes] Thank you Pam. And I hope you are as gracious during this next part. Helene, once again you are a wonderful person and you have lived a great life and I envy it. And I want it someday, but just in the future. You need somebody who– who understands your references. Who is Kafkaesque? I've never– I don't know him. There's another woman. And her name is Italy… and skydiving… and bungee jumping.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Okay, so–

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: And I want kids. And you… unfortunately, have already completed that part of your journey down there.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Michael.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: It's not my decision. It's mother nature. And mother has very strict rules about fer– [waitress comes over to pour water; long pause] — tility.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: I, um– I got it.

scenes.speaker: Helene
scenes.line: I'm 58. What am I supposed to do now?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well, hobbies–

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Stop.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [reaching for something on the top shelf] Ahh.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: What's going on?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Stupid things wedged up there. No one in this office will help me.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Alright, move it.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: What if Dwight dies and I still owe him something? That is a recipe for a ghost.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh yeah, you're going to owe me big time.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: It's like a little envelope– there you go.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Got it. [looks at envelope] To Dwight. Wha– [opens envelope] Starbucks gift card.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Surprise! [laughs] It's from everybody. $15 value.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Dammit. I am no closer to taking Jim down. What a waste of a day. I could of grown poisoned mushrooms that would have been this high by now. [bends over and hold hand about 1/2 an inch from the floor] They're mushrooms. They don't get that high.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Pamela Beesly Halpert–

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: What?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: May I have a word with you in my office please?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I am working.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well, this is a work related matter.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Really?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Really?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Yes. Join me please, won't you? [Pam gets up and follows Michael into his office] I am going to give you a raise.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Why?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Because of all the good work you've done.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I have the lowest sales record of anyone here.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: That's– no, no– it's not about numbers, Pam. It's about attitude.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I have the worst attitude of any person here.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Do you want the raise or what?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Yeah, I'll take it. [turns to leave]

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Hey, Pam, Pam– with this raise there are strings attached. [Pam sighs] And the string is attached from my heart to your mean attitude.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: You're bribing me?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No! No– no I am not. Unless you want me to. DO you want me to? Cause I will. I will bribe you. No. Your face is saying don't– unless I haven't offered you enough… your face isn't changing. What is it? Talk to me face. Tell me what Pam's brain is thinking. Come on! What do you want? What do you want? Do you want a million dollars? Do you want to hit me? Want me to get down on one knee and beg you or–

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I want to hit you.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: What?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I want to hit you. I'll do that.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [nervous laughter] Oh– okay , what? I don't– Are you kidding?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: No. Are you kidding?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Ye– No. Alright. I'll take off my jacket and tense my stomach and you can just–

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: No. I don't think I can hit you in the office.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: So, um… we'll do it after work. In the parking lot. In front of everyone. I'm going to hit you as hard as I can.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: See you then.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: See you.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Hey.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Hey.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Quick question.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Are you scared?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Never. About what? A little– what are you talking–

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: We heard about the punch.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: What punch?

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: Pam. She's going to punch the crap out of your face after work.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I'm pretty sure we said slap.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: No, it's a punch and Pam has that crazy pregnancy strength now.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: I'm getting concerned that you don't seem to understand what's going to happen. Do you?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I– mmm– I'm good.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: alright. See you there.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Hey.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Do you and Pam ever get frisky?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Inappropriate.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I mean– do you ever wrestle with each other?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: All the time.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Really?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: She strong?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: She wants it bad Michael.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Can you stop this?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I can.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: And I don't support her choice to hit you.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I don't either.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: But at the same time she looks crazy and I do understand her reasoning.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Mmm-hmm. I know.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I just need some time.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: You gotta do something–

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I just need some time. Just give me some time to make a decision.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: How much time do you think you'll need?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: No more than a week. Maybe two weeks.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Come on, man!

scenes.speaker: Toby
scenes.line: Pam, can I talk to you for a second?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Oh…

scenes.speaker: Toby
scenes.line: I heard about the hit. Just– make sure it's off company property, right?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Right.

scenes.speaker: Toby
scenes.line: Okay, I think we should probably be okay.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Toby
scenes.line: Okay. And– the-the power– comes from the back foot. So its– its all one motion through the– body. So you stay a little low and there's a twist. You keep your shoulder down and you kind of throw out the arm. [demonstrates punch] Pow!

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: [stands up; gets into stance] Okay wait– it's– you're saying it comes from the foot.

scenes.speaker: Toby
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Okay. [punches Toby's hand]

scenes.speaker: Toby
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Wow!

scenes.speaker: Toby
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Meredith
scenes.line: Hey everybody, he's not in the men's room although the seat was warm so we may have just missed him.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: My money's on Pam.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: It's not a fight. What other outcome could there be?

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Michael could win.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: How? He can't hit back.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Why can't you just agree with me sometimes?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Am I scared of getting hit in the face? No. Everyday weirdo's pay dominatrix's hundreds of dollars for that very privilege. I'm scared I'm gonna love it. [claps hands] Let's do this.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: It's okay guys… I can handle this. Everybody can go home.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: We're here for the show, Michael.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: You're just a bunch of voyeurs. Are you eating popcorn?

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: It has almost no calories.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Are you ready?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: [goes to punch Michael; he flinches] You have to keep your hands down, Michael.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I know. [sighs] Okay. Alright. [Pam goes to punch him again] Oh– God!

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Michael, you have to put your hands down.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: Put your hands in your pockets.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Okay! [braces himself] Pam, Pam– I'm really sorry. I'm sorry.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: What are you sorry for?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: So many things. I don't know. It's hard to choose.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: How about for dating my mom?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Maybe that–

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: And dumping her on her birthday.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Okay– just– don't ever date a member of my family again.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Okay. I promise. [Pam starts to walk away] For the record your mom came on to me. [Pam turns around and slaps him; he gasps]

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Holy crap.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Are you okay?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No!

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: You're okay.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Feel better?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: No. You were right.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [walks with Michael back into the office; Michael is clutching is face and limping] Wait, why are you limping?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I don't know.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Let's get some raw meat on that face. I got a chicken in the freezer upstairs.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: As I watched Pam's big, strong hand coming towards my face I saw my entire life flash before my eyes. And guess what? I have four kids. And I have a hover-car and a hover-house. And my wife is a runner and it shows. And Pam and Jim are my best friends and our kids play together. And I am happy and I am rich and I never die. It doesn't sound like much, but its enough for me.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Ahh… [Dwight is holding a frozen chicken to his face]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Good, good. Keep it on there for another five minutes. Just let the swelling go down.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh thank you. Thanks. I owe you one Dwight.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Fire Jim.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I'm cashing in the favor. Fire him.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: What are you talking about–

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Do it. Promote me. Tri-managers.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Forget that.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Can I have an office?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: You know what you can keep your stupid favor. It's worthless. And this is my dinner on your face. I'm keeping it.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [pats face] Oh that feels better.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [screaming, Phyllis and Dwight wrestling] Got you! Broken arm! Boom Boom Boom! Broken Nose! Boom Boom Boom Boom! Broken Nose! Boom! Ha, gonna flip you!

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Once a year Dwight holds a seminar updating us on the newest developments in the world of karate… because as we all know, the one thing thousand year martial arts do all the time is change.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: How can I pose this to you in a relatable way? You are all members of the Yakuza and you happen to be visiting the Lackawanna trolley museum… and you are attacked by triads… how can you hold them off until your clan arrives? You cannot go wrong with a throat punch [screams, pretends to punch Meredith in the throat]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: OK, so there's no defense for that, good to know.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: No, there is a defense for that. Let me demonstrate. Someone attack me. Kevin, go!

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: No way. Last time you pulled my pants down and then you tried to choke me with my shoelace.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: False. I did choke you with your shoelace. Now come at me!

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: OK, with all due respect to everyone here, I think the most worthy opponent of you is you.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: That is correct. Unless there happened to be measles present.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: So let's just say that Dwight has come at you with the throat punch. Now how would you, Dwight, defend against it?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Easy. Allow me to demonstrate. I am attacking myself with a throat punch. Here it comes. [gives himself a fake throat punch] Block. Grasp wrist as such. [grasps wrist]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: And what if he comes at you with the other hand, because he does have two.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Good point. Second, throat punch, absorb the blow. [gives himself another throat punch and proceeds to both attack and defend himself] Groin punch, hip block, elbow to the gut. Uh oh, up to the nose. No, you're not. Ow! Oh!

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh my God, he's making you look like such a fool.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: He really is, but not for long. [steps on foot] Ow! Instep, oh, not again. [more screaming] You let go, you let go. Oh, you're right, I can't hold on.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: You two are so evenly matched I don't know how one of you is going to get the upper hand.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: The important thing to remember Jim… we always have what is called the element of surprise. [hits himself in the groin and moans]

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: But I would say my favorite art form is a tie between sculpting and stand up comedy.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I did stand up comedy once.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: You did?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yeah, I killed.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: That sounds like it was hilarious.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: It was hilarious.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Michael?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Yes?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: What is the meaning of this email that everyone got?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: You'll have to be more specific Dwight, I get like eight emails a day.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: This one, from David Wallace to all Dunder Mifflin.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Woo hoo, shout out!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Hello everyone I am sure you have seen the item in the Journal. I just want to stress that it's all conjecture. If there's any concrete news you will know ASAP.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Erin, do we have the journal?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Your feelings journal? You told me to put it in the time capsule.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Did you?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Michael, he means the Wall Street Journal online.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh, the Wall.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: I found the article. [everyone walks over to his desk, he begins reading the article] "On a day marked by panicked corporate board meetings, one that is relatively not surprising is Dunder Mifflin's. It is rumored that they will recommend… " and the article cuts off.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: It's $1.99 to finish the article. I wonder what it was going to say? [no one makes a move to pay for the article]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Are you serious? [starts typing on the computer and Andy begins to lean in toward the computer]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I got it, I got it… Oh, Tuna beat me to it.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: "It is rumored that they will recommend declaring bankruptcy."

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No, no, that doesn't make any sense.

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: Oh lord, we're all gonna lose our jobs.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Not necessarily, bankruptcy could mean a lot of things. Maybe they're just restructuring to get out of debt.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh, that sounds awful.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Or it could mean the end of Dunder Mifflin.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh God. Well, that's an interesting theory.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: You know what? You can all have jobs at Schrute Farms as human scarecrows. It doesn't pay much and you can't unionize.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace’s Secretary
scenes.line: I'm sorry, Michael, David's in a meeting.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Ah, well maybe you should spy on him. [in Valley Girl voice] Oh my God, wouldn't that be hilarious! [laughs]

scenes.speaker: David Wallace’s Secretary
scenes.line: Um, I'll just have him call you back.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: OK, OK. Good. I'll catch you on the flippity flip. Bye. [hangs up phone] He's busy, he'll call me back when he's free.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: [retching sounds coming from the men's bathroom, Kevin walks to the door and goes in] Michael, are you OK? Did you throw up in there?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No, I'm just poopin'. You know how I be.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: It smells like throw up in here.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Crazy world. Lotta smells.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: [in lunch room with several coworkers] Guys, what if this is our last day at work? What if we never see each other ever again? [Andy scoffs and looks over at Erin, Erin looks sad]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I like Erin. There, I said it. I was kinda hoping she would ask me out, but things have not panned out on that front, so… it is time for the Nard Dog to take matters into his own paws.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [Michael in his office playing music loudly, Jim walks in and turns the volume down, Michael trailing off on singing] We have to do something because people are losing it out there wondEring what's going to happen.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: OK, we need some sort of distraction for everybody. Anything new on YouTube? Doesn't even need to be good. Oh God, I can't think, need more Mullins.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Listen, Wallace said these were just rumors, right? So we have no reason to think the company is anything but fine. So if we just go on with our work, you and me, they'll follow along.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Monkey see, monkey do.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: That's it.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Monkey pee all over you.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: That rhymes, so what have we on the docket today?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: We have a monthly staff meeting

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Alright, let's conference room it up! [everyone is now in the conference room] Here's the deal guys. There is no new information as of yet, so I suggest we all just keep working.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Sure I'm a little nervous, but doing our work will make us feel better. I only slack off when things are good.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Customers have to use the coupon code from the website. And as of now there is no differentiation between the letter O and the zero, but we are working on that. Stay tuned for that.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [Michael leaves] He needs me. Seat saved infinity. [leaves]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: OK, great.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [walks back in, on cell phone] What? Oh my God! [everyone starts asking questions] There has been a murder. There's been a murder in Savannah. [runs back to his office]

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Games have the power to distract people from stressful situations. Battleship got me through my parents' divorce. Operation got me through my vasectomy, i.e., my operation. I don't think I would have been able to endure my breakup with Holly had it not been for Toss Across.

scenes.speaker: Meredith
scenes.line: [reading the game box cover] Belles, Bourbon and Bullets, a murder mystery dinner party game.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: It is so much fun. Everybody plays a character, we go around the room, we try to figure out who did it…

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey, I am wondEring if this is a, uh, terrible idea.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: This is my call Jim, big picture stuff, it's about murder.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I thought we agreed that we wouldn't do things like this.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Tube City, you owe me one.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Co-managing is a give and take. You have to pick your battles. One of the battles that I picked was to stop Michael from running plastic tubes all over the office and placing hamsters inside of them. He was going to call it Tube City. So, yes, I do owe him one.

scenes.speaker: Voice on CD player
scenes.line: August the 5th, 1955. It's a sad day down here in Savannah. Local magnate Bill Bourbon was killed last night and all y'all have congregated tonight for a meal to celebrate Bill as he passes on to his great reward. You're not just here to pay your respects, you have to figure out which of y'all is the no-count scoundrel who killed him.

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: This is ridiculous. [gets up to leave, as does Angela]

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: There will be food. You leave, you do not get food.

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: What kind of food?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Sandwich platters.

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: I'm in. [sits back down]

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Baby carrots. [Angela sits back down]

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: OK, here are your character cards. Take one, pass it down. Here is your prop box, some of your characters will have props. Now, on your character card, it tells you who you are, and what your alibi is. Everything else is up to your imagination. So, if you talk slowly in real life, your character could, say, have been kicked in the head by a horse.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Whoa, I'll try it.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: OK, use your imaginations.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Who'd you get?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Naughty Nellie Nutmeg, a vivacious young socialite with a penchant for scandal.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Oooooo, saucy.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: How about you?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Nathaniel Nutmeg, the local bartender and Nellie's brother.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: Michael, I don't like this game. It's scary.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: It's not scary.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: I don't like my character.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Who are you?

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: Voodoo Mama Juju, the witch doctor of the Savannah swamps. I'm not comfortable with this. [holds up a head]

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well how do you think I feel? I mean I have to play Caleb Crawdad, handsome playboy. Every night, a different woman. Being oogled. Having to hug and kiss and spoon, I make them feel beautiful.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [looks at Oscar who is using his phone, grabs it] Well, well, well. What is this contraption, I do declare?

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: It's my blackberry Michael, I am trying to get updates on the company.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Who's Michael? I'm Caleb Crawdad, I do declare.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: You don't have to keep saying "I do declare". Any time you say something it means you are declaring.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: That is the way Southern people talk.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: And what Designing Woman are you basing that on?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Delta Burke, I do declare. Now, shall we get to the mystery?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I'll go. [stands up, begins speaking with a southern accent] My name is Deborah U. Tante. Deb for short.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: That's clever, Debutante.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Bill Bourbon was my uncle. I would have never hurt him any more than I'd hurt a June bug.

scenes.speaker: Meredith
scenes.line: Nice accent. You sound like Forrest Gump.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I do not.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Well, you do actually. You've got this kinda like Florida Panhandle thing going, whereas what you really want is more of a Savannah accent, which is more like molasses just sorta spillin' out of your mouth.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Oooo, now do the Swedish chef.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Uh, not familiar, what province is he from?

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: He lives on Sesame Street, dumbass.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: You know, I think I'm supposed to say something to Pam, I mean, Deb, OK? [in character] I overheard you asking the butler where the pistol was kept.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Wait a minute, wait a minute. I'm the butler. You were listening in on that? You rich people. You think you can do whatever you want to the servant class!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No, no, no. Don't turn this into a political thing.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I will poison your food.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I reckon I got something to say to Miss Beatrix Bourbon, if'n she don't mind.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oooooo, doggie, we got a party now!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I do believe that the game is a big hit. People are really diving into their characters.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Y'all.

scenes.speaker: Creed
scenes.line: [Creed pulls into the parking lot and goes into the office] Sorry I'm late, boss. What's going on?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [accent] Sir, there has been a murder, and you are a suspect.

scenes.speaker: Creed
scenes.line: OK. Hang on just a second. Let me just settle in and I'll be right back.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Very good, very good. Now, no one was there in the wine cellar. [Creed gets in his car and drives away]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [in character] Hey there young lady.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Hello.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I would be remiss if I did not ask the pretty young lady out on a date for this weekend.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Sounds like a plan, Sugar.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Alright, a plan it is.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Voodoo Mama Juju, explain your dalliance with the Dark Arts.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: It's not my fault, I was exposed to Harry Potter.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I know you did it!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I know she didn't do it. It's never the person you most suspect. It's also never the person you least suspect, since anyone with half a brain would suspect them the most. Therefore I know the killer to be Phyllis, AKA Beatrix Bourbon, the person I most medium suspect.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: [in character] Do you want to go out on a date with me? We can make out by the horses.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Well, you know ol' Nellie's always up for a romp in the hay.

scenes.speaker: Meredith
scenes.line: How about a threesome?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Yeah, my boudoir's always open.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Nice.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I'm a little worried I might have asked out Naughty Nellie and not Erin. Which would be a whole lot less appealing, because Naughty Nellie says yes to everyone. And she might be a murderer.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: I just got an email from corporate, specifically for Accounting to stop all payments to our vendors.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: What does that mean?

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Well, maybe nothing but it could mean a problem with liquidity-

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [accent] Whoa. What's this strange Yankee accent coming out of your mouth, son? This here's Savannah.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: [tries to speak in a high-pitched southern accent] This plantation, we're running low on greenbacks. We're having problems paying the people who give us the seeds and the dirt. We can't pay… [in regular voice] – Michael, I can't – Basically it could mean a lot of things, but it is unprecedented, so it's cause for concern.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: OK, I'm going back to work.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No no no no no no no. [accent] I'm going to skip forward to a relevant clue. Here we go.

scenes.speaker: Voice on CD player
scenes.line: Well by now you've figured out that ol' Beatrix Bourbon was the killer.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Michael, I was doing so well.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [accent] Are you going to believe that? That is a mis- that's a misdirection. We still don't know who the murderer is. [everyone leaves] Nellie Nutmeg, come back in here. I can't do this myself. Voodoo Mama Juju… what am I gonna do?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: OK, so Corporate is still in their meeting.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: That could be a good sign.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: Hey everyone, Kevin's going to give us his take on the situation. Let's listen up.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Alright guys, it's a work day and you guys work here, so let's go do some work.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Now, Jim telling us all to work? I think that is a very good sign.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: Don't just say things.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [Michael walks in] Oh, hey, Michael. Listen, I brought up those sales targets. Do you want to-

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [accent] I do believe you have me mistaken, my name is Caleb Crawdad. Y'all skedaddled way too soon. We need to reopen this case.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: No, you're not reopening the case. The case is closed.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No it ain't.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Frankly, I'm not surprised. A lot of the evidence seemed to be based on puns.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Just thinking about Weekend at Bernie's. It's funny, the guy's dead the whole time.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: I haven't seen it.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Speaking of weekends, you excited about our date this weekend?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: [accent] Of course, Nathaniel.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yeah, OK.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: [accent] Where are you taking me?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [accent] Well, finest steakhouse in all Savannah.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: [accent] Savannah? That's a far way from Scranton.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Did you mean a real date?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: No. [laughs] Did you?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Totally… not. [Erin gets up and walks away]

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: I thought it was for real. So I was excited, but it was just, it was part of the game.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: You're sure it was water, it couldn't have been acid?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I already declared you, it was too dark to tell.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Stop playing games with me, Crawdad.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: This is not a game, this is my life. You are out of order, sir.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Answer me.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: You are out of order.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: You are out of order.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: You are-

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I think Michael may have snapped.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Or maybe he's just stuck in character.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Well, which is worse? Snapped or stuck?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Both. They're both worse.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: It's going to be alright. We're a good company, we'll figure this out. We're not going under.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Jim, what if we both lose our jobs? I'm trying to think of a way that this all ends up fine, and I can't think of one.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [comes into Jim's office using accent] Deb, what in the world – do you have the vapors?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Michael, not now.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Can't wait, we have to get you to our witch doctor right now. Come on. Come on.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I should just go. [accent] Where to now Caleb?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: To Mama Juju Boo Boo.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Michael, can I… OK, I'm just going to skip right past the what and go with why.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Because this is the recreation of a crime scene.

scenes.speaker: Meredith
scenes.line: [laying on the ground] I'm the dead body and these are my brain chunks.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Hey shut up. You're dead.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Michael, can I talk to you in your office?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No Michael here, my name is-

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Caleb!

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Today of all days…

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No, you shut up. They need this game, Jim. Let us have this stupid little game, alright? [Jim nods]

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [accent] Oh, you startled me. My stars, my heart nearly leapt out of my chest. What can I do you for?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Wallace is on the phone. He's returning your call.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Detective Wallace?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: I don't think so. I think it's David Wallace from Dunder Mifflin.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Aw, shucks, tell him I'm not here.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: You're not gonna answer the phone?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No, I only answer to Detective Wallace 'cause I got a warm body in the other room.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I'll take it.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey David.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Hey, sorry to be getting back to you guys so late. Things are still a bit unclear, we didn't officially decide anything yet.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh, OK.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: But if I can be candid with you here Jim, it's not good. We fully expect to be out of money by the end of the year. Insolvent. So, well… You know what? I'm sorry, I have to run. But we will talk soon, OK?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Sure. Oh, you know, while I have you… today I was working on this pitch for a supermarket chain, and it would actually be a big account and I wanted to-

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: You know what? I can't really get my head around anything like that right now, but that's great. Keep after it, but I gotta run.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: OK.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Thanks Jim.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: See ya.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: [Jim comes out of the office] What's the news?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Nothing yet.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Well, I guess that's not-

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Well there is some bad news. [accent] There has been another murder.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: A murder, you say? I do declare.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Conference room everyone.

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: Do we have to play?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: No.

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: Super.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh, this could be a juicy one.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Get in there!

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I think today was a good day to have two managers. 'Cause if you're a family stuck on a lifeboat in the middle of the ocean, one parent might want to just keep rowing. But if the other parent wants to play a game, it's not because they're crazy. It's because they're doing it for the kids. And I get that now.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: There has been a lot of murder and a lot of intrigue. My little heart can barely take it no more. [regular voice] Today is the hardest I have worked in a long, long time.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [Andy, Michael, and Dwight are pointing imaginary guns at each other] I didn't do it!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: OK, everybody just calm down.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I am calm.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: On the count of three we're all going to put down our guns.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I have crossbows.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: We'll put down our weaponry on the count of three, you ready?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: OK, I'm ready.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: One, two, three… [all scream]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Andy revealed himself to be a double agent. At which point Dwight felt comfortable revealing that he also was double agent. And then Michael announced to everybody that – get this- he was a double agent. Oh, and it is 6:00.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [Michael, Dwight, Andy and now Pam are in the circle and training their 'weapons' on each other, Jim walks in] Really?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: [accent] It wasn't me. I'm not goin' down for this!

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yeah, I want to go home.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Get the keys out of my purse, start the car. [Jim and Pam slowly back out of the office, Pam has her weapon trained on everyone and then they run out]

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: [Dwight enters dressed as Recyclops] Not again.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Bow down before Recyclops.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Five years ago, corporate said we had to start a recycling program for Earth Day so Dwight took the lead on that and introduced us to a very close friend of his named Recyclops.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Happy Earth Day, everyone. I'm Recyclops. Did you know that an old milk carton can be sawed in half and used as a planter?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: The next year he really stepped things up.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Who has put a number seven plastic in a number four bin?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: A year after that Recylcops really began to take shape.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Recylops will drown you in your over-watered lawns.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Then tragedy struck Recyclops when his fictional planet was attacked by some other fictitious thing… I can't remember.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Recyclops will have his revenge.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I think this was also the year he renounced Earth Day and vowed to the destroy the planet he once loved.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Oh my God, you guys, look. It's Recyclops.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Recyclops destroys! [starts tearing through the office]

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: Oh, is today Recyclops Day?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: I thought you were killed by Polluticorn.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Polluticorn wishes. [starts spraying the office with something]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: That's aerosol spray. It's terrible for the environment.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Humans are terrible for the environment.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: The thing I like most about Recyclops is that he's creating a different world for our child.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Mmm.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: A world where you truly can be anything you want.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: God bless you, Recyclops. And your cold robot heart. [Dwight throws an aluminum can towards the recycling bin and misses]

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [seated] Ok. Ok. How 'bout this? [rises, waves, sits back down]

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: That's great.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I want it to be better than 'Great', Pam. How 'bout I remain seated… and I just do a little bit of a nod. Sort of a humble thing. [demonstrates]

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Sure.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Nope. Then my face is down. They can't see my face.

scenes.speaker: Meredith
scenes.line: And it looks like you're taking a dump.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Alan Brand is the CEO of the company, if title's important to you, has personally invited moi to go to New York to the shareholder's meeting and sit up on the stage with the board of directors. And at some point they are going to introduce me as the most successful branch manager that they have. And then Michael Scott turns and waves to the crowd… and the crowd goes wild.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [doing an announcer voice] Ladies and gentlemen from Scranton, Pennsylvania, please welcome Michael 'The Machine' Scott. [Michael waves, twirls and sits down]

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Don't do the twirl.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Lose the twirl.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: The twirl sucks.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Michael, I hated the twirl.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [still doing the voice & spinning in his chair] Hate the twirl!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Ok. Obviously I'm not going to do the twirl. I only did it because I nailed the wave.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Yeah, good. Don't do it.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I am not going to do the twirl. Alright? It's not even a twirl, it's a spin. I might do the spin.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: The long term problem is bad investments that they need to dump. The short term problem is the company has no cash and there's no where to get it.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Ok, Oscar, I don't need the whole enchilada just the bullet points.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Those are the bullet points.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well, could you condense it please?

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: That's as simple as I can make it.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Michael? The limo's here for you.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: It's not a limo. It's a town car. Town cars are actually better, though. Better torque. Better handling.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: He said limousine, so…

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: [at window in conference room] Check it out, guys. There's a limo down here. [everyone heads to the conference room] Michael, look. Oh, man.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: They sent a limo.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Town cars suck. Town car is something that a company sends when they're in trouble. A limousine is something that a company sends when they have cause for celebration. And in this case I think we are celebrating me.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [everyone is rushing down the stairs to see the limo] Oh, wait. Wait. Wow. Wow! Oh, no way. Look at that.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: What kind of mileage does this baby get?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: It's like what high school kids take to prom on tv shows.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: This is so typical of management to spend money on this. Ugh. Bunch of boobs.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Hate to break it to you Oscar but some of us like boobs.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Calves. Calves all the way.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I'm so jealous right now.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Hey, you know who you should be jealous of? Yourself. Because you're invited and you're invited and you're invited and you and you and you and you and you and you-

scenes.speaker: Limo Driver
scenes.line: Car seats eight.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: What?

scenes.speaker: Limo Driver
scenes.line: The car seats eight.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: The limo seats eight. Ok. Then Jim and Pam and Ryan plus a guest.

scenes.speaker: Jim & Pam
scenes.line: No thanks.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: I'll use it when you're done.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [others start raising their hands to be picked] Mmm… whoa.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: The Dunder Mifflin stock symbol is DMI. Do you know what that stands for? Dummies, morons and idiots. Because that's what you'd have to be to own it. And, as one of those idiots, I believe the board owes me answers.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [in the limo with Dwight, Andy and Oscar] I wish the windows weren't tinted so people could see us in here.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Hey, guys, do you think anyone might have had sex in here?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Definitely.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Smells like it.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Definitely. Look they got pillows. That. That's bigger than my bed.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Word.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yeah! Yeah! Yeah!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [the limo driver raises the divider window] Who's playing with the button?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey, Ryan. Could you start consolidating all our Rolodex information into Outlook?

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Uh, it doesn't seem like there's much of a point if the company's going under.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: But if the company doesn't go under then we'll finally have all our contacts in one program.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: The company's probably going under, though.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Could go either way.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Seems like it's leaning one way.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Maybe we should just wait and find out.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Definitely.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Ok.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: So should we wait to find out before we start doing all this stuff?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Nah. Might as well do it now.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Michael, what if somebody asks you a question at this meeting? Are you just gonna wave, or what?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I will have to answer.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I'll ask you a question.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Make it a softball. Something he can, like, crank out of the park.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Michael Scott you run the most profitable branch of Dunder Mifflin. How do you do it?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No, no. That's too hard. Say your name is Zamboni and then I will say, 'Well, we're sort of on thin ice.' [they all laugh] I won't say that. I'll something like that.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: This is your big day. Come on.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh, my god. This is it.

scenes.speaker: Laurie
scenes.line: Mr. Scott?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Laurie
scenes.line: I'm Laurie.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh, hi.

scenes.speaker: Laurie
scenes.line: Thank you for joining us. Come with me.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well, thank you and, and please call – continue to call me Mr. Scott.

scenes.speaker: Laurie
scenes.line: Ok. If you just want to follow me I'll take you up to the lounge.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well, I guess this is as far as I can take you guys. So –

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Kay.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Good luck, Michael.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: See you later.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [walking past bodyguards at the door] Officers. Thank you.

scenes.speaker: Laurie
scenes.line: After you, Mr. Scott.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Thank you.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Michael.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Hello.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: So glad you could make it.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Thank you.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: How was the ride?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh. It was awesome. Very, very sublime.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: I'm glad. I want to introduce you to everyone. First we'll start with Alan Brand. Alan? CEO. Michael Scott, Branch manager, Scranton.

scenes.speaker: Alan
scenes.line: It's nice to meet you, Michael.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: It's nice to meet you, too. It's an honor and a privilege.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Seated, we have the former congressman, Chris O'Keefe.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Ah. [bows] Your eminence.

scenes.speaker: Registrar
scenes.line: For those of you with questions, please line up behind one of the four microphones that have been placed in the aisles.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Coming through. Che, che, che, che, che, che. [spots microphone and gets in line, sees an empty mic and attempts to get there first] Excuse me. Excuse me. Excuse me. Excuse me. [a line appears from nowhere] Ah. Damn it. [heads back to the original line which is now even longer] Wha- okay [grunts]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I was hoping to lob Michael his softball question early. I wanted to swing by the garment district, pick up a few crates of my shirts. I got a shirt guy.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Can you believe this? The money they spent on this convention hall. [finding a seat] Excuse me, miss. I just want to take the stupid board of directors by their necks. This is so simple.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yeah. Well, you should do that. Get in line.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Oh, what a great idea and lose my job. No thank you.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Look, do you want to be able to tell your grandkids you stood up for yourself during the – America's biggest financial crisis?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: How is he gonna have grandkids?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: You guys ever protect the president?

scenes.speaker: Security
scenes.line: No.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: What about Madonna? Or Obama twins? Anybody famous?

scenes.speaker: Security
scenes.line: Not supposed to talk about it. Nelly Furtado.

scenes.speaker: Alan
scenes.line: Alright, guys. You ready?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Rock and roll. [they walk into convention room and are booed by everyone]

scenes.speaker: Alan
scenes.line: Dunder Mifflin is still a strong company. We are poised to come through this more streamlined and profitable than ever. [boos from the crowd]

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [to David] This is not as much fun as I thought it would be.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: It was fun when we weren't on the brink of bankruptcy.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [accidentally into his microphone] We're going bankrupt, you think? [angry jeEring from the crowd] They are really angry.

scenes.speaker: Alan
scenes.line: The shareholders need to empower our leadership –

scenes.speaker: Woman in line
scenes.line: I'm just gonna run to the bathroom. Will you save my place?

scenes.speaker: Man in line
scenes.line: Sure.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: No. You will not.

scenes.speaker: Woman in line
scenes.line: Excuse me?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh, I'm sorry. Were you raised in a household with no consequences?

scenes.speaker: Woman in line
scenes.line: It'll just be a second.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh. If onlys and justs were candies and nuts then every day would be Erntedankfest.

scenes.speaker: Alan
scenes.line: … and we're confident. There are many things to be optimistic about in Dunder Mifflin's future and one of them is here with us today. Michael Scott, Scranton Branch manager.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [loudly applauds] Yes.

scenes.speaker: Alan
scenes.line: In these uncertain times, Michael has managed to maintain steady profits from his Scranton branch. We all thank you, Michael. [scattered applause] Another bright spot in the Dunder Mifflin landscape, our new waste pulp re-purposing plant in Milford. [applause]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey, Phyllis. Are you just getting back from lunch now?

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Bob took me to Capello's. We got a little tipsy.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Ok. You shouldn't be telling me that stuff and also shouldn't be taking two hour lunches without telling me.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Oh, it's ok. Michael doesn't really care about these things.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I care about them and I'm just as much of a boss as Michael. [Stanley laughs] What's so funny? I'm a co-manager.

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: That doesn't make you a boss.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: It's not like you can fire people or anything.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Well – who? How did you? Who, who told you this?

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Ryan.

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: Can't say.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Sorry. Plastered.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Ok. Who else has heard the rumor that I am not as much in charge as Michael? [everyone raises there hands – including Pam]

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Stuff gets around. I don't participate.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Who here heard it from Ryan?

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Does and email count?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Yeah. [everyone raises hands again]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I am just as much of a boss as Michael and I can do anything that Michael can do. Alright? Who here believes that I have as much power as Michael? [Pam, after a moment, is the only one who raises her hand]

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I forgot I have to support him no matter what. Close one.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: These questions are bush league.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: You should get up and say something. You've got to be true to what's in there. [points to Oscar's heart] Don't be a wuss.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I've always been the guy who can rally other people to rebel. In high school I organized a walk out over standardized testing. Got over 500 students to just skip the SATs. At the last second I chickened out, took it anyway, got a 1220, always regretted it. I feel lachrymose .

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: [over the crowd booing] Believe me everyone is working very hard, working weekends, struggling, trying to right the ship.

scenes.speaker: Shareholder
scenes.line: You're a criminal.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Hey, hey, hey. I'm sorry. These are not criminals. They are nice. They invited me to come here today. They invited me to their hospitality suite where I had free food and it was delicious. Get this. Know how nice they are? The sent a stretch limo all the way to pick me up in Scranton. That's –

scenes.speaker: Female Shareholder
scenes.line: Limousine?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Second Shareholder
scenes.line: You're all corrupt. You should be in jail. [crowd agrees]

scenes.speaker: Alan
scenes.line: Quiet! Quiet, please! Please, quiet! Quiet, please. We want to hear your questions.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Do you love her or do you love the idea of her?

scenes.speaker: Creed
scenes.line: I don't know, man. I just don't know.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I gotta make an example out of him. Should I just fire him?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Can you actually fire people?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: To be honest, I don't know, but maybe I could just yell at him in front of people.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Well, I can't really imagine you yelling at anyone.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh, well I yell. You've heard me yell.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Oh. Ok. I've heard you exclaim. Like the time you said, 'Hey, look. We parked over here!'.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Well, that was apple-picking day and there's no need to yell that day, you know. I was just excited to find the car. Perfect end to a perfect day.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Well, you'll figure it out.

scenes.speaker: Alan
scenes.line: Ok. We're gonna take a 15 minute break and then we're gonna answer more questions.

scenes.speaker: Third Shareholder
scenes.line: You haven't said anything yet and we're headed for bankruptcy. [crowd agrees]

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [board of directors has started to exit] Yeah, well, that's not gonna happen. That's not gonna happen. We'll be back with some answers. [a few murmurs from the crowd of 'What answers?'] I – ok. I know that you're mad at me and you're mad at all them –

scenes.speaker: Fourth Shareholder
scenes.line: How are you gonna fix the company?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Ok. Alright. We are gonna – we're gonna go out there during this break and we are gonna come back with a plan. We're gonna come back with a plan for you. It's a 45 day plan. 45 days to get us back on track. [crowd starts to agree and perk up] 45 points. It's a 45 day/45 point. One point per day. We get the 45 points we are back in business. [crowd applauds] And you can take that to the bank. [applause continue] And Limo Lady, we are going completely carbon neutral. [crowd has gotten very excited and is cheEring] I love you, New York! [Michael does the spin and leaves the stage – then runs back across the stage] You. You.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey, Ryan. How's it going?

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: [playing Tetris on his computer] Here's the thing. Um, I've tried it like five different ways in my head and – Oh, got one. Um, I'm such a perfectionist…

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Mmm-hmm.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: That I'd kinda rather not do it all then do a crappy version.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Simple data entry, though. So there's really only one way to do it.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Sounds like you have a really specific vision for it. Do you wanna maybe just take a whack at it?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: You know what?

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: What?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I think I know the problem.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Great.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I think you seem distracted.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Yep, that is a problem.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: But, you know what? I came up with something and I think it's really gonna help.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Well, I'm glad you're finally being proactive, Jim.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I am, too. Let me show you.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Wow. Things are really picking up.

scenes.speaker: O’Keefe
scenes.line: What was that about?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: What?

scenes.speaker: Alan
scenes.line: You were supposed to wave.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I did wave. I did a lot more than wave.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: What are we supposed to tell them now? Ok? You've dug us quite a hole.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: We tell them the plan, right?

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: There is no plan.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Here's what we're gonna do. The 45 day thing that I outlined, we go with that. Day 45, company saved. Day 44, go. What do we got? We have 15 minutes.

scenes.speaker: O’Keefe
scenes.line: Excuse me?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Just whatever comes to mind. Shout it out.

scenes.speaker: O’Keefe
scenes.line: Who the hell is this guy?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I am the guy who roused that crowd.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Got them on their feet.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.line: They were so happy down there.

scenes.line: No.

scenes.line: I think you're doing a great job.

scenes.line: Hey Mr. Scott, What you gonna do, What you gonna do make our dreams come true. Hey Mr. Scott, What you gonna do, What you gonna do make our dreams come true.

scenes.line: Hey, Rockefeller Center!

scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.line: This is all we have.

scenes.line: Ugh.

scenes.line: It is warm feelings.

scenes.line: Thirty! Twenty-nine! Twenty-eight! [others join]

scenes.line: Twenty- seven! Twenty-six! …

scenes.line: Ooh.

scenes.line: Ah!

scenes.line: You didn't decorate it?

scenes.line: No.

scenes.line: Everyone.

scenes.line: Is it, is it fake?

scenes.line: Pam!

scenes.line: Yes, we are unveiling, an artificial tree, that will never die…

scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.line: Like the spirit of Christmas!

scenes.line: This was a successful unveiling! Go back to work! Merry Christmas!

scenes.line: Hello. Sorry guys. [louder, face is scratched up.] Sorry guys. I'm not sure I've earned the right to make announcements yet. But whoever is giving me the Twelve Days of Christmas? scenes.line: What psycho would send that as a gift? [Kelly hugs Erin]

scenes.line: Ho ho ho! Merry Christmas boys and girls! It's me, Santa Claus!

scenes.line: Hey Santa!

scenes.line: They finally let you do it!

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Yeah!

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Congrats Phil!

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: It's so edgy!

scenes.line: So Santa, what can we expect from this party?

scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.line: That's too funny.

scenes.line: What the hell is going on?

scenes.line: Phyllis, Jim? Phyllis is Santa?

scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.line: Phyllis?

scenes.line: Yeah I told her a long time ago she could do it.

scenes.line: Take it back. That is absurd.

scenes.line: No, I'm not gonna do that.

scenes.line: No? No! Jim! Come on!

scenes.line: I think she's doing a good job.

scenes.line: It's insane! A woman Santa, where does it stop? No! Jim, this may be the last Christmas that we have here, doesn't it make you a tiny bit anxious, me NOT playing Santa? Come on!

scenes.line: I'm not gonna go tell Phyllis that she can't be Santa.

scenes.line: Fine! Then do it anonymously. Ransom note style. You can- I -you know what, I have a bunch of letters cut out of magazines in my desk. You can use those.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: If this were Russia, yeah sure. Everyone would go to one Santa, and there would be a line around the block and once you sat on her lap and she'd ask you what you wanted, you would say probably "freedom." At which point the KGB would arrest you and send you to Siberia. It's a good thing Russia doesn't exist anymore.

scenes.line: [santa voice] Ho ho ho! Why pay more to sit next to old Tranny Claus over there, when you can sit on my lap. Phyllis is only … pretending to be a man, I'm the real thing. Sit down on my lap and there will be no doubt!

scenes.line: [mutters] Okay…

scenes.line: No it's not, not like penis-wise. [as Santa] Hello little boy, what's your name?

scenes.line: When can I sit on your lap?

scenes.line: Right now! Come on over here, big boy! There we go. [Kevin sits on his lap. It's a struggle] Oh my God.

scenes.line: That's really comfortable. [Michael gasps]

scenes.line: What would you like for Christmas little boy?

scenes.line: What did you think was going to happen?

scenes.line: I didn't know. Nobody's ever let me sit on their lap before.

scenes.line: All right, just say "some toys" please.

scenes.line: Damn it Kevin, come on.

scenes.line: What about if I tell you the things I don't want?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Okay get off, get off! [pushes Kevin off] Oh! Oh, God!

scenes.line: I didn't even get to tell you what I wanted!

scenes.line: Awesome.

scenes.line: Well?

scenes.line: I'm trying Phyllis. You're Santa.

scenes.line: The only Santa.

scenes.line: That's what I want.

scenes.line: You promised me this. Don't make me get Bob involved!

scenes.line: What would Bob do?

scenes.line: Never mind, I shouldn't have said that.

scenes.line: Hmm.

scenes.line: Great!

scenes.line: Hey! Okay! Everybody! The office is being pulled apart! I realize that. There are traditions at stake. And there are–

scenes.line: Who wants Phyllis as Santa? [most everyone raises their hand]

scenes.line: Not a gun. [crosses gun off his "what could it be" list]

scenes.line: Okay Pam.

scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.line: Yes! They're the only two gay guys I know. But they should be together.

scenes.line: Ho ho ho! For Stanley! Ho ho ho! You've been very good this year –
