scenes.line: Hello. [comes in carrying 4 gallons of orange juice and his water bottle] Is anybody home? Oh, thank you, Erin. Now if everyone would please ready their canteens, so I can fill them with the sweet, sweet nectar of Gabe's homeland, and then propose a toast. Here we go.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: You know when people say getting fired was the best thing that ever happened to them? I feel sorry for those people. That's the best thing? Really? Ugh.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well, I'm not really one for making speeches.

scenes.speaker: Everyone
scenes.line: Yes. Yes, you are. You make a lot.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: But I feel pretty good right now. I really do. A lot better than I did earlier. Let me tell you.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: That's your toast?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No. This is my toast. I think this whole thing with Sabre is going to work out. I have a very good feeling about it.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Michael, this isn't a toast. You're just thinking out loud.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Here's my toast. Orange juice is in here. And, like Saber, it is from Florida, and it is good.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Just 'cause you have liquid that doesn't make it a toast.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Here's the toast. I'm gonna do it now. Raise your container to us and to Sabre.

scenes.speaker: All
scenes.line: To us and to Sabre.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Mm. Wow. That is metallicy. Ugh. That's like drinking a battery. Ah, really gets you in the fillings, doesn't it? Okay, anyway, welcome.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: [singing] Well, it's a mess, what a mess. What you gonna do? You're going to take out your Suck It and you suck it. Suck it. Yeah, take out your Suck It and you suck it.

scenes.speaker: Teddy
scenes.line: Suck it!

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Yeah!

scenes.speaker: Teddy
scenes.line: Suck it!

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Yeah!

scenes.speaker: Teddy
scenes.line: Suck it!

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Yeah! Take out the Suck It and we'll…

scenes.speaker: Teddy
scenes.line: Suck it!

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Yeah!

scenes.speaker: Teddy
scenes.line: Suck it!

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Yeah!

scenes.speaker: Both
scenes.line: Take out my Suck It and we'll suck it.

scenes.speaker: David
scenes.line: Yeah! Teddy!

scenes.speaker: Teddy
scenes.line: Yeah. [high-five each other]

scenes.speaker: Hotel Employee
scenes.line: [on phone] Vancouver Court Hotel, how many I help you?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Hello Vancouver, this is Michael Scott calling from the United States of America! I have a reservation in your fair city from February 12th to the 19th, first week of the Olympics.

scenes.speaker: Hotel Employee
scenes.line: Well, we are looking forward to having you, so, let me just pull up your information here…

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Okey doke.

scenes.speaker: Hotel Employee
scenes.line: Um, I don't seem to have it, sir.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: What?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [looking through Michael's email] I'm not seeing anything under "confirmation."

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Could it be under "affirmation?" Cause you have thousands of those.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No. [to hotel employee on phone] We're trying to look it up right now.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: You did get the e-vite to my barbeque!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Um, come on.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Michael…

scenes.speaker: Hotel Employee
scenes.line: Uh, sir? A lot of people are trying to get last-minute reservations at hotels here for the Olympics, but we've been fully booked for months.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well, I have been booked for three years, so you should have that. I've always heard that British Columbia is a very nice place, but I am not getting that from this conversation.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Wait, I got it! Confirmation code:

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Today, Jo Bennett, the CEO from Sabre, is coming to see us here for the first time. She bought us sight unseen, like a mail-order bride, so she's gotta be kinda nervous. I mean, are we ugly? Are we smart? Are we cool? Are we too cool? Do we speak English?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [Jo Bennett enters with two humongous dogs, everyone stands to welcome her except Dwight] Why hello!

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: This is Michael Scott, co-regional manager of this branch.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Pleasure to meet you, Miss Bennett.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Oh, that's Mrs. Bennett, sweetheart. My husband and I are divorced, but I kept the "Mrs." just to piss off the new wife. Well, let's take a gander around this place.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [Jo's dogs are sniffing at his crotch] These sure are pretty dogs…

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: They love a good crotch.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: They sure do.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: You should take that as a compliment!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Oh, I do!

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: [to Dwight] Hello.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Hello.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Do you always stay seated when a lady enters the room?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I am treating you the same as a man, for whom I would also not stand. Unless it was the President. Or Judge Judy.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: I like that.

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: This is Accounting.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Hi!

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Good-looking group.

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: Over here is Meredith Palmer and Creed Bratton.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Another couple of heartbreakers. Who is this tall drink of sun tea?

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: That is Jim Halpert, he is the co-regional manager of this office.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: [gesturing to Michael] I thought this guy was the manager?

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: Oh, he is. He's the co-manager, and that's the other co-manager.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Two guys doing one job? We gotta do something about that!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Got some Valentine's cards for my coworkers and my bro-workers.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: [as Andy is passing her a card] No, no!

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: What, no candy?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Valentine's Day, right around the corner. Erin and I have been on zero dates. So I got her a Valentine's Day card, but I didn't wanna seem "too eager," so I got cards for everyone in the whole office to kind of dilute it a little bit.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [throwing a card at Meredith, which skims her throat]:

scenes.speaker: Meredith
scenes.line: Yeah, I have this thing about men cutting or threatening to cut my throat. Don't try to cut my throat.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Jo, I don't know how things work in Florida, which from your description sounds like a colorful, lawless swamp, but here it takes two men to do one job, where in Florida it might take one very strong woman to do such a job.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Whoa, whoa.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Whoa, whoa!

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I'll take over. Um, what we're doing here:

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: I'm Jolene Bennett, Jo for short. I'm a breast cancer survivor, close, personal friends with Nancy Pelosi, and Truman Capote and I slept with three of the same guys. When I was a little girl, I was terrified to fly, and now I have my own pilot's license. I am CEO of Sabre International, and I sell the best damn printers and all-in-one machines Korea can make. Pleased to meet you.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [almost running into Erin] Whoa-oh, traffic jam!

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Uh-oh, traffic jam on route three!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [imitating car noises] Beep-beep! Beeooop-beep!

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Beep! Twenty people dead in a pile-up!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: There's blood everywhere! Um, I got you a Valentine's card.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: [opening card] Oh, you did? Aw, a bird and a dog!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yeah, well it's Snoopy and Woodstock.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: You named them?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Uh, Charles Schultz did. I thought it was relevant cause I got you all those birds for Christmas, remember?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Uh, yeah I do remember. [reading card] Aw, they love each other.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Oh, look at that. They sure do. I hadn't noticed.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Wow, it smells really good too.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yeah! It's Roger Federer for men, I sprayed some in there.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Andy, whoa! Thank you very much!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: It's got pheromones in it.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Hey!

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Hi.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: [to Angela, who's having a hard time deciding on a chair] Just choosing seats, not getting married. Chop, chop little onion!

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Jo, there's books in my chair.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: That's right, darlin', now you're the proud new owner of a Sabre handbook and my autobiography. Now, you all must be in a tizzy. I can see it on your faces, I mean, what's going on now? I mean, who owns Dunder Mifflin? Right? I mean, Sabre? What's that? Some company I've never heard of? Down in Tallahassee? Where is that? Near Mars?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No, we know. Texas!

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Now Dunder Mifflin has an arm's reach in all these small businesses all over the northeast. Now we're gonna take that arm, and we're gonna start selling printers.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I could manage my way around that.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: They're the easiest-to-use printers on the market.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I will try to manage my excitement!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I have been saying the word "manager" a lot, so whenever Jo thinks "manager" she thinks of me. Camel cigarettes did the same thing with Joe Camel by making him look like a penis. I can't even go near a cigarette now without thinking of a penis. And vise-versa.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: I think that's it. So we're all good! [many employees raise their hands] Thanks ya'll.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [Jo leaves] I, uh…

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: [reading her Valentine's card from Andy] Oh my God.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: I guess Andy likes me. I never thought of him in that way. But, I guess in most romantic comedies, the guy you're supposed to be with is the one you never thought of in that way. You might have even thought he was annoying or possibly homosexual.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: So, check this out. According to the handbook, you could make more money as a salesman than as a manager. They have all these incentive programs. I ran your numbers from last year.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: This is way more than I make now.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I don't think I'm gonna miss being manager. You know how some people say they're not in it for the money? Well, with all due respect to this job, I think I'm definitely in it for the money. And quite honestly, the women.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey, you got a second?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Sure. You here to tell me that you think I would be a better manager and that you are sorry for being such a jerk?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Actually, yeah.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: What?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Exactly that. I think that you absolutely deserve the manager position more than I do.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: What? Really?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yeah!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Wow!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: La la la, hello Oscar!

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Michael. Reading.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: What are you reading?

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: The Atlantic.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh, that is my favorite ocean! I love it! I am so happy right now. No! I can't keep it a secret any longer. Jim is stepping down to salesman, I am going to be the sole manager once again.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: I should step into sales myself.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Why, is there an untapped gay market?

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Sabre has no caps on commissions. He can make a lot more money in sales.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: …Where did you get that information.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Manual.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Manuel who?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well, according to the manual, there is no cap on commissions. I have been hustled.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Son of a bitch. [enters conference room] Pardon me.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Oh, speak of the devil. We were just talking about you. Have a seat!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Now Jim here is thinking about taking himself out of the running for being manager.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Really? Aw, that is so sweet of you! But, I cannot accept, because I have been thinking about it, and I think I wanna go back to sales.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Really?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Really.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Yeah. You can take the man out of the salesman, but you can't take the sales out of salesman.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Well, I think you're both being a little too modest.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: No, I really, really think Michael is better at being manager for so many reasons.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No, I think I would be bad. I would sleep in my office, and I would sexually harass people.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Why would you do that?

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: I'm turning myself in right now!

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: You know, Michael, you have more experience in sales and management, so I'm gonna defer to your judgment.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Thank you.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: I think you [to Michael] will become the salesman, and congratulations! [to Jim] You're gonna be the new manager of this branch!

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Great! That's great. Congratulations. Have fun signing my commission checks, boss.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: [pointing to the window in Michael's office] Oh, Michael marked his heights. He's grown!

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Mm!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [on phone] Bobcat, this is Dragon. Listen. He's been promoted to sole manager. We've got to step this up. Meet me behind the dumpster in ninety seconds. [hangs up phone] 89… 88…

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: You're twenty minutes late!

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: [walking up] Um, I was at another dumpster!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Just admit you lost track of time.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Ryan and I have been meeting up to work on our diabolical plot against Jim. Ryan is always late for our meetings. I wish I had a lair.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Did you see Saw?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Of course I seesaw. Mose and I seesaw all the time.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: No, uh, the movie. Did you see the movie Saw?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh, yeah. Great film. Almost as fun as going on a seesaw.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Okay, the reason these movies are so popular, is the element of psychological torment.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I like where you're going with this. Continue.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Could we lure him into an old warehouse or something?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I have an old barn!

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Yes!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: It's kinda smelly, but that might be a plus! And then what?

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: We do what they did in Saw! … I mean, we don't kill him, obviously. I have a mask…

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Okay, that's your idea? Exactly like in the movie!? That is the most idiotic thing I have ever heard in my life!

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Well suggest something else then! Don't just…

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: He's supposed to cut his leg off? Think!

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Don't just criticize my idea!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Think!

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: You think of something then!

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Michael, I'm worried that, uh, not all your toys are gonna fit on your new desk.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: How is that possible?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Well, in your old office there were all those ledges and extra space.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No excuses Erin, come on! Make it happen.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: You know, I actually think I should get back to work. Jim asked me to do some stuff, and he's manager.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh, yeah. Fine, fine. Leave it here. I have to make some sales anyway. Who should I call with my magic sales fingers? [Michael's phone rings] Michael Scott, head of sales.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [on phone] You gotta do something, man. You can't just sit there.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: The new IT guy. Nick.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Nick.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I think he is the key. He's very trusting, he's looking for friends, he has been given an awesome amount of power, and does not know how to wield it.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Like Frodo!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Why don't you just let me handle the Tolkien references, okay dumb jock?

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Well, I think he can be corrupted. Like Gollum.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Smeagol was corrupted and became Gollum.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I might start a diabolical plot against him after this one.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Who's hungry?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: What is that?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: It's ants on a log. Michael would always have me bring them in at 2:30 and say "Who's hungry?"

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh. I'm fine. Thank you, though.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Do you want me to spin you in your chair and make you dizzy?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Why would I wanna do that?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: It's a thinking technique. All the top executives do it. It keeps the brain moving, and a spinning brain is a working brain.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: For now, I'm just gonna go back to work here…

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Oh sure.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yeah. Thank you.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Well.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: [on phone] It will be a pleasure doing business with you. Thanks, bye. [hangs up phone, blows train whistle] I just got a new account for the gentleman's club in Carbondale. It is called "Curves." I went by there the other day, saw some of the women walking in. Not really my cup of tea. Actually, Kevin, you might like it!

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Nice!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: You know, we really don't announce out loud our sales that much.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Why not? It's part of the sales experience.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: It's not really 1992 anymore.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Well, okay…

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: [reading Andy's card] You brighten my day with the sound of your voice, you bring so much laughter and love, you're everything to me, and I was so blessed when God sent you here to me.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Geez louise.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: I know, obsessed with me much?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Well, everyone got one.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: What did yours say?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Friends are worth sharing a doghouse with.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: It's no wonder that Andy gave Kelly such a romantic card. I can't compete with her. That girl can sing, and dance, and gets all of her clothes at the mall. And I feel like such a fool for thinking that Andy was only going after one girl, cause Andy Bernard is a playboy. And, why shouldn't he be? He's got it all.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Ho-ho. There he is, the IT guy. So you discovered the break room.

scenes.speaker: Nick
scenes.line: Uh, yep.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I imagine one of the best things about being an IT guy is, you get to know everyone's computer passwords.

scenes.speaker: Nick
scenes.line: No, I actually don't.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Listen, I know you have to say that, but we got a little problem here. There is an employee named Jim Halpert, and he is doing some terrible things, okay? He is molesting people via the internet. And we need to stop him.

scenes.speaker: Nick
scenes.line: I think that you should call the cops.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: No, the cops called us. So I'm gonna need you to give me the password to Jim Halpert's computer.

scenes.speaker: Nick
scenes.line: I don't know what to tell you, man. I'm sorry, I just can't give out his password like that.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Nick. We could make things very, very difficult for you.

scenes.speaker: Nick
scenes.line: Are you… you threatening me?

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Threatening you? No. [tries to crush an aluminum can, Dwight crushes an apple]

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: What is that smell? Do you smell that? What is that? Like a sulfur deposit under here?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Michael, stop.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No, I'm serious, we don't have to put up… Is it the dogs?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Michael…

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: You know what, we don't have to deal with this. I am going to Google sulfur maps.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Michael, it's Phyllis.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: No, this is geological.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: I sent an email out to everyone in this area that this might be a side effect to my new allergy medication I'm on.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Are you kidding me?

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: No.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: And you guys are okay with this?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: She sent an email, so.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: I did.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [has two tissues in his nostrils] It's not cause of the smell. I'm just expecting a nosebleed.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Oh my God.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: Oh! You scared me!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I'm sorry, I thought you saw me.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: I didn't see you. And you were there all along. [takes papers out of copy machine] Well, I warmed it up for you so, should be good to go.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Cool, thanks.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: Bye, Andy. [kisses his cheek]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: …That was weird.

scenes.speaker: Meredith
scenes.line: No it ain't. We all saw the Valentine you gave her.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I don't even know what that card said.

scenes.speaker: Meredith
scenes.line: Believe me, if I got that card? We'd be in the bathroom doin' it right… now.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Hey.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: You know, it's funny. I used to stand in here and wish I was out there. Now I'm out there, and I wish I was in here.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Well, the grass is always greener.

scenes.speaker: Michael
scenes.line: Yeah. Except there's no grass out there. It's just a farty dirt patch.
