scenes.line: The Senator? [Oscar nods] He was married before, and he has a kid.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: [whispers] So!?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: And don't say that thing about how lots of gay guys have kids.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: I have a very strong suspicion.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Did you see him at a bathhouse?

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: What bathhouse?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: The windowless building by the Baskin Robbins.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: [confused, whispers] What?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Forget it. I'm never gonna know what goes on there.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: My friend at the Scranton Blade is totally plugged into these matters.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: You're in the gay mafia.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: You're thinking of another group. Much wealthier, much older. [whispers, smiles] You sound ignorant.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: You guys, um, talking Senator?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: No.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: No. Why would we be talking about the Senator?

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: 'Cause he's totally gay? [walks away]

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Um, how do I know that Robert is gay? He "liked" my facebook photos at 3 o'clock in the morning.

scenes.speaker: David Brent
scenes.line: [on video resume on a laptop] Name? David Brent. Occupation? Inspirer. Status? None of your business. Young, free, and single, though. Thanks for asking. Hear you're looking for a new boss. Yeah? Someone to tell a bunch of discontented, underencouraged drones what to do every day. Is that it? Oh. Our out-of-touch powers that be? Want me to fire them, if they don't see things your way? Then I ain't that dude. Bye-bye, baby, bye-bye. Get some other corporate suit to lay down the law. What? You've changed your mind? You're now looking for a leader of men? Ipso facto, women too. [points at self] When do I start? Yeah. [Jim looks uninterested in this candidate]

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Do you know what it took to get Bob to notice me? I waited in his office every morning wearing nothing but kitty-cat ears. I did that every day for two weeks. And on the tenth day he walked in, he was naked too, except a dog nose. Guess what we did then?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: [trying to cut off Phyllis] I… I don't think I can do that.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Bestiality. Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Well, that's not my personality.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: If my daughter were asking me… [both giggle]

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Yes?

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: I would say, if you want someone, if you really want them,… go get them.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: I do really want him.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: So, uh… here you go. [gives resume to Jim]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Great.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Hope it's all right.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I'm sure it's fine.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: The guy who was in here earlier, interviewed after me, how'd he do?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Howard Cline?

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Ehh, that's not who I'm talking about.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [checks sheet] Oh… Deshaun Williams.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Yes. How did he do?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: He's an amazing man. He's a Rhodes Scholar. He invented an app that invents apps. Fantastic kisser…

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Come on man. I'm being serious. Don't joke.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Darryl! We all know you. Your interview is not nearly as important as the other guys. [Darryl taps a couple times on Jim's desk and walks away]

scenes.speaker: Nellie Bertram
scenes.line: First, I'll take down the cubicle walls.

scenes.speaker: Toby
scenes.line: But there aren't…

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: Symbol of transparency. There'd be no titles. Everyone would have the same job. Same goes for me. I'd take your job, but I'd reject the title.

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: A little un-specific.

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: Everyone would be known for their accomplishments.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: That's very interesting. Um, I feel like there might be a conflict there, and if a conflict did arise, how would that be dealt with?

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: Ooh? Yeah. Mm. Scratch everything from before. I tell you what I'd do. Go the other way. More cubicles. More division. Everyone is somebody's boss, and that person can fire the person below them. [overlapping comments by the Search Committee] At least once a month, the lowest performing person… [does a cut-throat hand gesture] bye bye!

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: How would you compare, like, an accountant and HR?

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: Well, I'll tell you how. Shall I? I'll tell you how.

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: By splitting the difference. Just… just, somewhere in the middle.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I think that's probably all we need to hear from…

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: Zen office. Hmm? Thought of that? That's what I'd do. Everyone takes their shoes off, before they come in. Okay. There'd be no desks. You just sit on the floor.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: That's very…

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: You've got a Thai woman, out in the back. Sockee! Sockee!

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: Okay, that's not gonna be…

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: Sockee!… is her name. Okay? Shes administEring massage, all right, if you need it. If you don't, whatever, just talk to her! She's a person! Either way, 50 minutes of that and you…you are cracking to go. [smiles]

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Is there a front runner?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: You know what? They all just sort of blend together after a while.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Well, there must be someone who stands out.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: No, not at all. In fact, I'm not even taking it seriously. I think at the end of the day, I'm just gonna pick a name out of the hat.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Well…

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: The hell you will! I worked for the last boss for 15 years. According to my doctor, I don't have another 15 years if I want to keep up the same dietary and sexual lifestyle, which I intend to.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: [in mock seriousness] Oh no, Stanley… you'll live forever…

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: My next boss will be my last boss. He'll be at my funeral. So I would appreciate it if you would take this seriously. [dunks his half-eaten donut in Jim's coffee, takes it back out, and leaves]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Uh–

scenes.speaker: Meredith
scenes.line: You pick a crappy boss, you're responsible for my crappy life. [leaves]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Okay, everybody, I was just making a joke. I am taking it seriously, I promise.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Are you? [leaves]

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Little advice? Take a day off from the whole Jim schtick. Try caring about something. You might like how it feels… James. [closes his office door, leaving Jim alone in the break room]

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: [walks in with her dogs] Gabe, honey! Oh, lord. Take all this. [gives the dog leashes and multiple bags to Gabe]

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: All right.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Here. Jim! Did you hear Stern this morning?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: No, was it good?

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Ohh, Robin was good. She's always good. Keeps him on his toes. Its Howard's show though. [picks up resume from Jim's desk] Whose is this? Darryl Philbin. Ohh. Very nice to see a familiar face on top. Ah… a little long aren't we? Four pages? Is this the same Darryl Philbin who's had two jobs in ten years at one company?

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Yes, thanks to you, who promoted me, after we, uh, interfaced.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Coordinated and implemented receipt storage and delivery of over 2.5 billion units of inventory. 2.5 billion, Darryl? 2.5 billion units of what?

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Paper material, ma'am.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Paper material?

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: [softly] Pieces of paper. [Jo rolls her eyes]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [clears throat] Jo, may I speak to you for a second?

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Or what? You gonna shoot me?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Ha ha ha! Ha ha ha! Ohh, I enjoy laughing at my mistakes, because I've learned so much from them. I'd like to be interviewed for the position.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: I'll interview you right now.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Question 1. Ever shot a gun in the office?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: It's complicated.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Yeah, but see… it's not.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: I don't think we should tell her. Angela went a whole day without telling me I had lettuce in my teeth. Screw her.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I'm a woman. I would want to know.

scenes.speaker: Meredith
scenes.line: Yeah, you gotta know.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Okay, but if Angela can get a gay man to marry her, maybe I could get a lesbian to marry me? Huh? Huh? That's hot.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: You have met a lesbian in real life, right?

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: You know, this is probably is her last chance at a family.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: She does seem happy.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: You're right. You're right. She seems happy. We don't tell her.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: We don't tell her.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: Excuse me, Ms. Bennett, may I have a word?

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: Uh,… can it be in private? [to Gabe] Don't worry, it's not about you. [Gabe smiles and leaves] As Minority Executive, I think it's my responsibility to let you know that Gabe is gross. I don't think it's professional that he was sleeping with the receptionist, and then when Erin dumped him, so that she could be with Andy, he became a total crazy stalker psycho.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Welcome to Scranton, Jo. Land of a thousand problems only you can fix. [Jo's phone starts vibrating, she picks it up and sees Dwight has texted her "Dwight's ability as a manager has lead him to higher levels of proffesional success,"] Oh for god's sake. He's texting me his resume one line at a time. These are costing me ten cents a piece, you jackass! I'm roaming!

scenes.speaker: Creed
scenes.line: [to Jordan] Get me our biggest client on the phone, right this instant. [closes his office door]

scenes.speaker: Jordan
scenes.line: Who is our biggest client?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Uh, just put him through to me.

scenes.speaker: Jordan
scenes.line: [laughs] Okay.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Hello! This is… the client.

scenes.speaker: Creed
scenes.line: It's Creed. FYI, I'm starting my own paper company, looking to poach some chumps, you in?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Creed
scenes.line: Hehehe, cool. Let's keep this on the QT, okay? I uh, I don't want you to be a dead mamma jamma.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Great.

scenes.speaker: Creed
scenes.line: All right, thank you, bye-bye.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Thank you, bye-bye.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: [knocks and enters] Jo, you have one more candidate. He's a burn victim.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Huh?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: [motions toward her face] He's all messed up. I can tell him to get lost if you want.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: No, send him in. [to Search Committee] Who is this?

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: I have no idea.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [seeing Dwight wearing sunglasses and whose face and hands are completely covered in gauze] Oh, I know this guy. [Dwight awkwardly hands copies of his resume to the Search Committee] Hello! Mr. "Soo-ven-yay." Mr. "Jacques Soo-ven-yay." Nice to meet you. It says here you're French. [Dwight nods] So you worked at your last job for 15 years as Assistant to the Regional Manager.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [mumbling through the gauze] Assistant Regional Manager.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Assistant to the Regional Manager.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [again] Assistant Regional Manager.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: What is it?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [in a cheesy French accent] Assistant Regional Manager.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh, that's my mistake, sorry about that. The last paper company you worked for burned to the ground? And all because they wouldn't hire a manager who lived and breathed paper? That's a travesty.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: I want to talk to Dwight Schrute for a second. I want to ask him a question. [Gabe gets up to leave] If he isn't here in sixty seconds…

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Uhh. Wait. Wait! No. Stop! Stop. Jo… [takes off sunglasses and reveals his face] It's me. I'm Dwight.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [looks extremely confused] No. No! Wait, but, I mean, you're Dwight, and then… he's the… [trails off]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [whispers] Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [looks astonished] Ohhhh!

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: Very unprofessional, "Jacques." Or, should I say, Dwight.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Let's just say I had hired this Jack Souvenir. Then what?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I would have dressed this way every day, legally changed my name, learned French sign language, shown up, and been the best damn branch manager you'd ever seen!

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: All that for this job.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: That's f***ing crazy. [Jo and Dwight both smile] Get outta here. [Dwight leaves] What a nutjob.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: This guy was good. Although, he did keep saying that he needed two weeks off right at the beginning for a trip to the finger lakes. Seriously. Every five minutes, he was like, "just making sure the finger lakes thing is clear."

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Okay, it's fun to talk about the rejects, but uh, who's got ya excited?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Finger Lakes guy is good. Darryl is also very good.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Who's this fella? Went to Cornell. What's wrong with him?

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: How much time do you have? Sales ability? None. Integrity? See sales ability. [makes a "zero" hand gesture]

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: And that's your unbiased opinion.

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: Yes, it is.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: So it's not relevant that he took the receptionist away from you?

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: Oh, Jo. Jo, I'm disappointed in you. Some people let personal things into the workpl-. Is she with him? Because I thought that she was…

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Gabe…ugh… you got all close to these people. Got involved in their lives. Let's get you back to Florida. We'll figure out something for you.

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: That sounds like a promotion!

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: It's not. Let's get Kelly in here to take his place.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Um… why Kelly?

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: 'Cause Gabe's tall and weak. She's short and strong. I'm doing an opposites thing.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: How'd my girl Nellie do?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh, I didn't know you knew her?

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: She didn't mention it?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: No.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Integrity move. I like it.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: You know, she also gave me a reason to think that maybe she wasn't a good fit.

scenes.speaker: Jo
scenes.line: Well, I'm not saying you must hire her. If you find someone who's clearly a fit, then fine. Just make sure they fit real good. No more manager turnover. Don't mess this up, Jim. And give Dwight an interview. I like a little bit of crazy.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: [hiding under desk, raises a sock puppet up, talking in high-pitched voice] Ahh!

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Erin, what are you doing?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: I've been turned into a puppet!

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Okay. [walks away]

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: [giggling, walks to Erin's desk] Look at the puppet! Hi, puppet! Who are you?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: I went to drop off the FedEx forms and an evil witch named Angela turned me into a puppet!

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: [giggles] Yeah. Low blow, puppet.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: And there's only one thing that can change me back into a real girl.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: It's good. It's just that I wish the puppets would talk more about the alphabet. Not for me… but, if any kids are watching… A, B, and so forth. You know,… M-N-L-O, P… F…

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: [as sock puppet] I need the most special thing in the office.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Silence?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: A date with the best salesman… Andy Bernard! [Andy walks over to Erin's desk]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Hey, Erin.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: [gets up] Oh.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Where'd you learn how to puppet like that?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: [shrugs] I've done it all my life.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Listen, I'm really flattered, but I don't think we should.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Erin's my best friend in this office, hands down, but… when she asked me out, I just didn't have that feeling, you know? [clip jumps ahead] Aren't there some things that you really want to like, but you just can't… seem to like it, like, Mad Men… or football… [clips jumps ahead] Let's not forget, Erin chose Gabe over me. That happened. I'm not going to apologize for getting over her, okay? I'm sorry. [clip jumps ahead] I would go for someone who's more… she's great, though.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: [loudly] Stanley, I won't be able to invite everyone to the wedding, because we want to keep it to 350.

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: I'll get over it.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: I mean, we just have to see how many Senators and members of Congress want to attend, before we can open it up to regular people. Pam, you know how you and Jim did your ironic wedding? [Pam looks confused] Do you still have the plans for the dream wedding that you couldn't afford?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: That was our dream wedding.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: Niagara Falls? Pregnant? That was your dream? Pork medallions?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: [looks over at Oscar, who is quietly watching this happen] I hope… you have a very beautiful wedding, Angela.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: Hmm.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: All right. Name.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Dwight Schrute.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Thank you, Mr. Schnoot. [closes his binder] We will let you know.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: You have to interview me…

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I just did. The answer to that one question told me everything I need to know.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I demand more questions!

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [ignoring Dwight] All right, guys, good day, a lot of candidates. Let's discuss.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Okay! If you're not going to interview me, then I'll do it.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: What will be your first priority? I will have seven first priorities. Safety, profits, fostEring a community of self-reliance and entrepreneurship, listening, respect for human life, bolstEring our public image, and… [chuckles] getting everyone home on time. Dwight, let me be frank. In an accident that no one can blame you for, an antique gun was discharged while you were acting manager. How are we ever to trust you again? [whispEring] That's a great question. [Jim nods] I am going to institute a strict no-firearms policy for this office that extends to myself as well. Wow. All of my concerns are disappearing.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Thank you, Dwight.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Thank you. [clears throat and gets up] You'll be hearing from us shortly, Mr. Schrute, and I think you're gonna like the call you're going to receive. [smiles] Oh, come on. I'm just happy that I got this meeting. [leaves]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Well, that was quick.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: [sighs] Very, very interesting. And you know what? I'm impressed.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: He's not a real candidate.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: I don't know, Jim, 'cause, makes me think about something my grandfather used to say, which is that, sometimes, the hand that jumps out of the grave and grabs you around the throat; that is the hand that you want on the wheel.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: You took the deal.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: Yeah, it was a great deal.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: That's not okay.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: I don't know. Dwight seems like a great leader to me, and I look forward to the personal perks that he promised me privately. What do you think, Toby?

scenes.speaker: Toby
scenes.line: Well, we could try him out for a little while… [Jim drops his pen, looks exasperated] and if it doesn't work out, you know, maybe one of us could, you know, step in…

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: What is happening right now?

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Is it true that you're making Dwight the manager?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: No, why would you think that?

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: He and Kelly said, then they pre-fired me.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Okay. [walks out of conference room] Okay, guys, just so you all know, no decision has been made, and Dwight is definitely not the boss.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: That is correct. Actually, Dwight is not the manager yet.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: No, no, no. Not ever, 'cause that's not gonna happen.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Well, it's not entirely up to you, is it? Seems to me like someone's getting a little power-mad.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Am I the only one who remembers what he did when he was in charge? I feel like I'm going a little bit crazy.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Tuna… You're completely sane.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Thank you.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Who do you like for the job? Is there anyone who maybe was a little underwhelming at first, but now seems like a safe, if not slightly unexciting, choice?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Okay, seems like everybody has an opinion. So, who else? Anybody?

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Do you mean it? Anybody? Are you sure?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [while sighing] I suppose I am.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Okay… well what do 'I' want in a manager?… let me see. [walks slowly across the office] what do 'I' want?…

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: I don't think he meant, that–

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: So now anyone gets to talk at any times?

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Go ahead.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: What do 'I' want?… I'm looking for someone… who… [smiles] Everyone is listening to me. [Dwight looks at the camera, annoyed]

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Can I say…?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: I think it should be Darryl.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: What a surprise! Minorities sticking together.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Kelly's on your side.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: I'm sorry, is that all you think of me? A minority? I am so much more than that. I am a dancer, I'm a singer, I'm a fashion designer.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Whoever it is, I think they should be lame. [Stanley shakes his head and rolls his eyes] Kind a a non-threatening, moderate personality.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: I want an outsider.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Perfect. There are several outside candidates that we think would be really-

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: No, I mean an outsider. Like someone on the margins of society, who doesn't see things the way we do, like a homeless person.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: A homeless person. Really? A homeless person.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: No, you're right, Pam, let's just leave him to the welfare system and let that handle it.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: No, I want you to say that you think the 'best' person to be our new manager is a homeless person.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Let me guess who you want, Pam. Rachael Ray? The ladies of The View?

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: I got away with… everything, under the last boss, and it wasn't good for me, at all. So, I want guidance. I want leadership. But don't just, like, boss me around, you know? Like, lead me. Lead me… when I'm in the mood… to be led.

scenes.speaker: Meredith
scenes.line: I just want, for once, a smart, professional, decisive, well-hung man in his forties.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey! Hey! Hey!

scenes.speaker: Meredith
scenes.line: Okay, fine. Uhh, the guy with a tiny penis. Are you happy? [sarcastically] Let's hire that guy! [Jim looks speechless]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: She may have a point there… would a small penis work? Small-to-moderate.

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: [walks in] Gotta catch a plane.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Ohh, hey Gabe, I'm sorry, we… we didn't get you a cake or anything. We're gonna miss you.

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: Oh, well I'm still the corporate liaison to the branch.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: You are not leaving without giving me a hug. [hugs Gabe] Ughh.

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: Okay, you know what, you don't need to make that sound.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: I'm sorry! You were just a lot bonier than I thought you were gonna be!

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: There are plenty of people who love touching me. [camera zooms to Ryan, who looks at the camera, extremely skeptical] I'm a terrific hugger. I've been with a bunch of girls where that's basically all they want to do. I will see you all soon.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Later, man.

scenes.speaker: All
scenes.line: [various] Good luck! Goodbye! Good luck at your new job.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Take care, man.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: We're gonna miss you, Gabe. [Gabe leaves]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [stands up] Uh, listen up. Listen up, ladies. I want the job. There, I said it. I'm educated. I'm capable. I like all of you… and I won't make any changes.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: I see it. [nods and smiles] I see it like I see a mountain that I'm standing in front of [voice cracks] and facing, and I'm like…

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Yeah. [Oscar looks confused] Yeah, Andy would be wonderful as boss. Erin made a good point. [brushes Erin's hair with her hand]

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: No, we're not related. I got the call. But… I'll tell her some other day. [smiles]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: What about Darryl? We can all agree that he's a stand-up guy, right?

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: Well, let me be clear. I only speak for myself, and not myself and the Senator. I think we have some wonderful candidates, and there's a great, lively debate here, but let's think about-

scenes.speaker: Toby
scenes.line: No, no,… no. Sorry. We cut Kevin off for the same thing. You have to have something to say, if you talk. [Angela rolls her eyes and stops talking]

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Exactly.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: [enters the office with his daughter, who runs in and hugs Jim] Jada, no, no, no, Jada, what are you doing? [Jim looks knowingly at the camera] Oh. So sorry, guys. I hope my family didn't disrupt your meeting.

scenes.speaker: Jada
scenes.line: Daddy, are these the people who are making you manager?

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: [sighs] Maybe, sweetheart. Single dad. Challenges.

scenes.speaker: Jada
scenes.line: I don't know if he'd be a good manager [Jim shakes his head and looks wide-eyed at Darryl], but he's a really great dad!

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Okay, shush it. This was a mistake. Let's go. [Darryl and Jada leave, Ryan slowly shakes his head]

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: It seems like we all know enough to vote. Should we just vote now?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: What? No, no, it's not a vote.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Then what was this all about?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I don't know. This conversation really got away from me.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: I don't care. They can just vote.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: No, they can't. That's not how this is gonna work. [exhales] We're going in this room, we're going to have a meeting. We're gonna make a recommendation to Jo, and she's gonna give you her recommendation on Monday. Okay? [to Kelly and Toby, as they re-enter the conference room] What the hell happened out there? [Kevin tries to follow, but the door is closed on him]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Sometimes you hear about people failing upwards. I think I'm about to do that.

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: This job? Oh, yeah, I'll get it. Jo's an old friend. I think… I'm her best friend. She's not my best friend.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Every day I have a blueberry muffin. Today, I did not have a blueberry muffin. Should have had the blueberry muffin… especially considEring how incredibly superstitious I am.

scenes.speaker: Fred
scenes.line: No, I've never been more sure of anything in my life. I will be the new boss of… [looks back to glance at lobby directory] Vance Refrigeration.

scenes.speaker: Merv
scenes.line: Honestly, I think I… I sabotaged myself. It's like I'm afraid of being happy. Case in point… I was supposed to start another job today.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: [chuckles] I will get offered the job. That's a… call I've received many times. The slight hopefulness in their voice, the pregnant pause… while they wait to hear my response, and then… my response.

scenes.speaker: Finger Lakes Guy
scenes.line: [geeky voice] I want the job. I really do. It's just, the rest of my family's in the Finger Lakes right now. I'm supposed to be in the Finger Lakes right now. I told them I was on a hike; snuck away to do this interview. I gotta get back pretty soon; they'll worry. People disappear in the Finger Lakes.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I will run this branch, or I will destroy this branch, or… [shrugs] I don't know. Something always works out. [leaves]

scenes.speaker: Creed
scenes.line: You remind me so much of my fourth-biggest client.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: [in high-pitched, damsel-like voice] Is that right?

scenes.speaker: Creed
scenes.line: I think you two should meet.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Well, okay!

scenes.speaker: Creed
scenes.line: Hey Jordana! Patch my ninth- and fourth-biggest clients together. [Pam puts down phone and picks it back up]

scenes.speaker: Pam as “fourth-biggest client”
scenes.line: [in a comedic male voice] Hello!

scenes.speaker: Pam as “ninth-biggest client”
scenes.line: [in high-pitched, damsel-like voice] Hello!

scenes.speaker: Pam as “fourth-biggest client”
scenes.line: Hi, how are ya? [Erin looks amused, Stanley and Phyllis look at Pam, confused]

scenes.speaker: Pam as “ninth-biggest client”
scenes.line: Ohho! I'm good! Don't you just love paper, and things about paper!

scenes.speaker: Pam as “fourth-biggest client”
scenes.line: Hey, are you single? This seems like a love connection to me!

scenes.speaker: Creed

scenes.line: Okay, we are now on a planet where Kevin is the most creative person around, and I am just some good-looking guy.

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: [as Lincoln] I just don't understand. It's 1865, victory is ours, I've saved the very soul of our nation, and yet… happiness eludes me. Oh, perhaps a trip to the theater will enliven my spirits.

scenes.speaker: Audience
scenes.line: No!

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: 'Kay, so another thing about oatmeal cookies. Who even wants them? I mean, I've seen Toby eat one, like, once, but other than that… [scoffs] like, forget it.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Interesting. So what is Dunder Mifflin's oatmeal cookie? What is the product that no one wants?

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: how about that two-hole-punch letter? Only the lawyers want that punch at the top and they use legal.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: That's the oatmeal cookie. Fantastic, Kevin. Fantastic. [laughs]

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Thank you.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: By the way, did we leave all the food on the bus?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Let's talk about food for a second. Food for thought.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yeah, that's what I had for breakfast and I think that's probably why I'm still hungry.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Hunger! Hunger for victory! Hunger for honor. Hunger for pride.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Hunger for hamburger.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Hunger for chicken chimichangas. Right, Darryl?

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: That's good.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Exactly. Now do you know the Civil War soldiers were hungry for? Pride! Now, each battalion had its own flag and they guarded these flags with their lives. Colonel Harrison Jeffords of the Fourth Michigan Infantry saw his flag being carried away, chased it down with nothing but a sword. Fought tooth and nail at the foot of that flag until he died. He wasn't about to let them have that flag. Pride. Right, guys? [holds up flag] I commissioned this flag for Dunder Mifflin. Cost me two hundred dollars.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Only two hundred dollars?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: We are all branches on this tree. And from the tree comes paper. We're all part of a business. But business is war. What's that I hear? Uh, a rebel paper company is coming to take our flag! Wha- what's going on here? Wee-hoo! Come and get it! Who's gonna get the flag? Who's getting it? Whoa! Hey! Ho! Don't look where I am, look where I'm going. Juke right, juke left.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Andy, this is inappropriate. People died here, man.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Get the flag! Get the flag! Come on, Big Tuna. What you gonna do about it? We got a flag right here. Wee-hoo!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Spangler Springs is a mile this way.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh wow. So that's two miles if you incorporate the walk back.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Its… I mean come on.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: I don't think I should walk anymore. You know all I had for breakfast was oatmeal, yogurt, coffee, orange juice and toast. Two poached eggs. And then half a sandwich on the bus.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Alright fine. You know what – I guess this place just hasn't rubbed off on you the way I hoped it would. I'm still going. And I'm not going to ask anymore. I'm not even going to look back. I'm just going to assume that you're with me.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [Andy looks back to find everyone sitting] You said you weren't going to look back.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: And why is Black Rock suddenly the paragon by which all hedge funds must now be compared?

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: I don't know.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Right. I mean you're an accountant. Those bogus prospectuses must drive you insane.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Yes. I am an accountant.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Dwight – this is one of the archivists here. I thought maybe we could consult him.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Really?

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Well. Anyone employed by the Gettysburg Industrial Complex is certainly going to want to keep quiet about the Battle of Schrute Farms.

scenes.speaker: Archivist
scenes.line: Schrute Farms did you say? That is a fascinating little chapter of the Civil War.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: You've heard about it?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: YES! Ha! Prepare to be refuted! Go on.

scenes.speaker: Archivist
scenes.line: There you go.

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.line: Families and sweethearts back home waited desperately for letters from the front.

scenes.speaker: Soldier
scenes.line: Dearest mother I'm sorry it has been so long since my last letter. It is three months since I arrived at Schrute Farms and I fear I may never leave this place alive. Melvin Fifer Garris.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Hallowed ground.

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.line: But the Battle at Schrute Farms was no battle at all. It was a code used by pacifists from both North and South who turned the Pennsylvania farmhouse into an artistic community and a refuge from the war.

scenes.speaker: Amanda
scenes.line: [on film] You have to understand. Poets, artists, dancers – these kind of men preferred peace to war. These delicate lovely men found a place of refuge among the Schrutes at Schrute Farms. Amidst the macho brutality of war this was a place where dandies and dreamers could put on plays and sing tender ballads and dance in the moonlight. I like to think of Schrute Farms as the Underground Railroad for the sensitive… and well… fabulous.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Wow. This is so much better than the story you made up.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I've seen enough.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: You're right. There should be a monument to this.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Never trust a cookie with a woman's name. Pecan Sandy. Lorna Doone. Madeline. They'll just break your heart.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: [laughing] Kevin!

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Robert I hate to interrupt. But I would love to pitch you one last idea. I call it the Big Mac idea.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: What?!? No!

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Big Mac idea. That sounds encouraging.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: It's really, really good Robert. Let me explain.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: No! This is not fair! This is my idea. He's trying to steal it because he's jealous of me.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Well what is the idea?

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Every time you buy a Big Mac you set one ingredient aside. Then at the end of the week you have a free Big Mac. And you love it even more because you made it with your own hands.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: You know what? Now I remember. That was your idea. [patting Kevin on the back] That is 100 percent your idea.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Oh my. It was just actually cookies the whole time?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [making pencil imprint] Dammit.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Hey.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: You guys came. Where's everyone else?

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Back at the bus. We were locked out. Phyllis is sitting on the ground eating a dirty sandwich.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yeah I asked the bus driver to lock it because our stuff was in there. I guess he follows orders.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yeah sorry everyone else didn't come. I think they're just tired. With holes in their shoes. And they have dysentery.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Even without an audience you're still at it.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: What are you talking about?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Our office has a disease. And it goes by many names. Sarcasm. Snark. Wisecracks. You take things people care about and you make them feel lame about it with your jokes. That's what you did with this trip.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Andy – this whole idea of our situation being just like war? It's just not true. We just work at a paper company. And you're our regional manager. And guess what man? You don't have to prove anything. We like you as regional manager. Andy if you don't believe me take a look at what's on my head. I'm wearing a very pink hat. I've been getting weird looks all day because I'm pretty sure "DM does GB" means something kinda sexual. But guess who's wearing them? All of us. Just for you man. That's huge.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: You don't like the hats?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: They're terrible.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: I hate myself.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: They just didn't turn out how I wanted. In my head they were cooler, but they do look weird.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [voiceover the three walking] The world will little note, nor long remember the fight Jim and I had here at Gettysburg and that's good because I was basically wrong. I wanted my team to be, like, this army and I was their general. But I guess it's really more like they're just people who work in an office and I'm their manager. Yeah that's really probably a better analogy now that I think about it.

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: Abe and Mary are seated watching the show. [in Lincoln voice] Oh Mary this is wonderful… Ok Mary stop your scolding. I'll be quiet. [aside to the audience] I need her like I need a hole in the head! [scattered chuckles from the crowd] [Gabe raises his hand with a finger pointed in the shape of a gun to his head] BANG! Ooh [Gabe falls to the ground and the crowd claps, Gabe picks up the Lincoln hat, bows, runs to the crowd and trades it back for his pink "DM does GB" hat and runs off]

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Haha! There he is. You mind lending a hand? I'm typing up a memo to share your ideas with the board.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: I can do that.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Great…ok.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Your arm feels good on my back.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: For some reason, my boss is obsessed with cookies. It's not my specialty. My specialty is pizza. But I'm flexible.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Charge!

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: Isn't Gettysburg like three hours away?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: No. It's like two hours and forty-six minutes.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: It's kind of a haul, so we should probably get going. And tuna, I made a special sandwich for you, guess which kind.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Tuna?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yes! Tuna of the land. Turkey. With pesto.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: And to drink?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Water.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh-ho, I am in.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I'm excited, I've actually never been to Gettysburg. Uh, my family was gonna go once, but then my brothers convinced me if was full of dead soldier zombies, so I freaked out and we turned the car around. But I'm older now, I can outrun a zombie.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Getting everyone on the bus, check. Giving everyone hats, check. Sexiest eastern European girls, uh, check.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Hey, Devil's Den is that way, we should check it out. That's where the snipers hid.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Please! Everyone and their mother goes to Devil's Den. It's the Olive Garden of Gettysburg.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Oh, I like Olive Garden.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Well, I meant that in a bad way. Obviously it tastes good, but it's not cool.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Where do all the cool kids go when they come to this consecrated ground?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: That is what I'm showing you.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I know what you guys are all thinking right now: Hey, let's go pee on the grave of some confederate soldiers, but you know what? Joke's on you. It only makes the flowers grow back more beautifully.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Best thing you can do for the deceased is to pee on their graves. Then you dance and work the urine into the root systems. Doesn't hurt to have a smile on your face, either.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Guys! Over here, we found the bus.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Open the door, Jim.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: It's locked.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Are you sure? Yeah, it's locked.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: It's not locked, gimme that…

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: That's weird, if it's not locked, why isn't it opening?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: It's, it's latched closed.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Ok, you know what? Andy probably has the number for this guy. I'm gonna find him.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: I'll come with you.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Ow! Ee! I sat on my sandwich.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: And that's how the printing press was invented.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [enters office doing Michael Jackson impression] Everybody beat it. Don't beat it, stay where you are.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: There you are. Dillinger Graphics said their shipment is late.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: What did you say?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Nothing, I just-

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: What would you say?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: That it'll be the first shipment out today.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: That is exactly the right thing to say! Do it! Git-er-done! Phyllis, you just married Joe Order, you're new name is Phyllis Order [fill this order], get it?

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: I don't get it.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Jim, in regards to our high-five scheduled for four PM today, it has been moved up to now. Yes.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: We didn't have one scheduled.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [knocks water bottle on to Jim's desk] Oh, little help. Wow your hair is really thinning.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Standing is proven to be healthier, increases productivity and just looks cooler. Picture someone doing something heroic. Now was he sitting or standing? Not counting FDR.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Every second you sit there is an hour off your life. Look at all of you. I feel like you're in a suicide cult.

scenes.speaker: Creed
scenes.line: No. No. No. You're way off on that one.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh yeah?

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Are you really comfortable standing there? I tried one of those and I just never hit the sweet spot.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey guys let's just all admit it. Ok? Dwight's better than us. He had the guts to stop sitting. And he's never, ever going to go back on it right?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: That's right Jim.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Hey man.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [jumping up from an almost sitting position] Hey.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Taking a load off huh?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: No. Putting a load on more like it.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Good luck with that.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Last thing I need is luck. [hunches down again]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [to Angela] Thank you so much. [hums]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [sees a pole poking out Dwight's pant leg] What are you up to? Oops look out! [grabs Dwight's wallet]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: What are you doing? Give that back. Come on!

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Prank! [throws money from Dwight's wallet on the floor]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh that's real creative.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: You know what it's not my best. Because you could just easily bend over and pick it up right?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I could, but I just don't feel like it loser.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Because you're sitting?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Standing.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Ok.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Don't!

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Because you're sitting?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Standing.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: You know I have to do this.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I know. [Jim pushes him over, Dwight screams]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [signing his name] Andrew… Baines… Bernard.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I think you could just do Andy Bernard.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Andrew Baines Bernard. I love filling these out. Because it's like taking a test, but I know the answers.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: [loudly knocking on the window] In four seconds my wife is going to be coming through that door. I told her she could work here. Under no circumstances can that be allowed to happen. [to Mrs. California] There you are! Honey how on earth could you miss the elevator?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: What was that?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I don't know. He wasn't talking to me. But if I were you I wouldn't hire his wife.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: That's why my foundation – The Dream for a Wish Foundation – is going to put them out of business. They're not going to know what hit them.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Everyone. I'd like to introduce my wife Mrs. Robert California. Mrs. California this is everyone.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Hello. Oh call me Susan please.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Last night at dinner Susan and I were talking about her returning to work. So she's here today to see if there's a good fit. Something tells me it just might work out. This is Andy Bernard the regional manager.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Hello nice to meet you.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Hey there. It's a pleasure.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Andy would you be so kind as to show Susan around the office. Show her the various departments. Find a place where she'll shine.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I would love to. But I have to be completely honest with you guys. We're 100 percent staffed up.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Andy. Let's see if there's a good fit first. Then we'll talk.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Alright.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Knock, knock, knock, knock, knock.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: You don't have to say it if you're doing it.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [laughs] Remember how you said that you were looking in the office to do calisthenics and aerobics?

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Uh weight lifting yeah.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Well today's your lucky day. I have opened in this very office building Dwight Schrute's Gym for Muscles. You wanna take a look?

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: I'll take a look.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Your path from obesity begins right here!

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: I've been meaning to join a gym. [narrating over a montage of scenes with him and Val] For my health. I used to say I wanted to live long enough to see a black President. I didn't realize how easy that would be. So now I want to live long enough to see a really, really gay President. Or a supermodel President. I want to see all the different kinds of Presidents.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Obese people in my office are a drain on resources. Chairs wear out faster, it takes more Freon to keep them cool, they flush the toilets more often, plus their massive BMs bust the rivets on my pipes. But a gym turns fat into cash.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Alright! The DM Express is pulling out.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Well it was really nice to meet you Brian.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Actually Ryan.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Oh, Ryan.

scenes.speaker: Ryan
scenes.line: Bitttch!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: We will start here at Erinville.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Hi.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Hoo-hoo!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Reception. Your classic one-man operation.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Although I was watching a movie and Merryl Streep had two secretaries.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I was watching a movie and a bunch of apes took over San Francisco. Just saying.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Two secretaries could convey a sense of importance and success to our clients. Certainly worth exploring; wouldn't you agree Andy?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I'll explore exploring it.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Good. It seems like you have this under control. So I'll just duck out and run the company for a while.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Ok uh next stop on the tour sales. Here we go. Station stop Jim Halpert. Oh boy our resident truth teller. [Jim laughs nervously] Alright have at it. Let 'er rip. What do you hate about this place?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Well it's sales. So you have to be able to live in the world of rejection.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Maybe you do. Hi. I'm Dwight. Sales is really not so hard ok? It's paper. We have it and they want it so bad they are willing to pay for it.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Jim?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Well it's not that easy. It's kind of sometimes difficult.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: It's the second easiest job in the world. [to camera] Being a mom.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: I love shopping and sales is just the other side of that.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: That is true.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: You know if you joined our sales department you would be working very closely with our department head Mr. Dwight Schrute.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: That's me.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Dwight why don't you tell Susan about some of your hobbies. Survival skills. Ranking of animals.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Maybe over a beer after she's closed her first sale [makes gun click noise].

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Well make that a red wine and I'll tell you my animal rankings [makes gun click noise back].

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Oh how am I supposed to pull this off? [montage of office workers in friendly interactions with Susan]. The entire office is being nice to her than they've ever been to me. What I wouldn't give for one of Phyllis' classic room clearing farts right now.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Ready? What do you think?

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Um no. This is not a gym. This is like a scene out of Saw 5.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: You haven't even looked around yet. Look. Gravel bucket squat yoke [squats, grunts and lifts] Right? Dedicated phone book ripping station [tries and fails to tear a phone book in half]. You ever cut tin before? Five yards in and your forearms will be on fire. Plus I will buy the tin back from you that you cut for two cents a yard. Now let's go over membership. I'm going to need the first month's and the last month's up front. $49 per month. But every third month is $59 a month. But the fourth month is a discount month at $19 per month…

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Obviously you know how a gym works. So you know I'm not going to pay money for this. You want people to come to your gym? Make a real gym.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Darryl… [picks up sledgehammer and swings it at a hanging tire]

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Make a real gym.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: I was thinking accounting might be a good fit because I really clicked with Oscar and I do have some experience in bookkeeping.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: But we already have a surplus of accountants as it is.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Uh I could work in customer service. HR even.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Those are fully staffed as well.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Are you telling me that there's no one in this entire office that could use an extra pair of hands?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [laughing nervously] Yes.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: I am the CEO and I am telling an employee of mine what to do.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Let me beat around the bush for a second. Our chairman of the board has some very strong feelings about-

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Robert this is very uncomfortable. Obviously there's no place for me here. So thank you for trying. Why don't we just let it go.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: No. Absolutely not. Andrew there must be something you can do. Think.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: There are lots of considerations.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: I would be eternally grateful. It's not a bad thing to have the CEO owe you one.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Alright. Well then welcome aboard.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: So what happens next?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: We get you over to HR and then we get you set up with accounting. [phone rings] Hang on. Hello?

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: [on phone] Say hello grandma.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Hi gam-gam.

scenes.speaker: Robert

scenes.line: It's not that kind of ladle.

scenes.line: Very cute. [holds out the phone]

scenes.line: Aw, let me see-

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: [grabs phone] Ah, just the battery on these things. I'm sorry, I've got to recharge this.

scenes.line: I get it. Last time I had a job, I remember I hated the boss' wife. Of course, she was married to Robert.

scenes.line: Your employees don't seem to be taking to me.

scenes.line: Andy! Andy, could you step in here, please? We'll fix this.

scenes.line: [chuckles] Please. Andrew, my wife… has brought up an issue that requires your attention. So, uh, if you'll excuse me, I should step out, get to the ATM before that homeless man sets up camp for the night.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Okey-dokey, artichokey. You hate it, don't you?

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Do you not want me here?

scenes.line: Why would you say that?

scenes.line: It's okay. I understand. I'm not sure how I would feel about having the boss' wife work for me either.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: It's not that, exactly.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: But it is something.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Let's just say that if you don't want to work here, I am totally prepared to respect that.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Why would you not want me working here?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I don't know. [chuckles]

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: I think I understand what you're going through. My husband can be a very difficult man to read, can't he?

scenes.line: Yes! The dude is an enigma.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Mm-hmm. So he is mixed up in this, isn't he?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Ah… [stammers]

scenes.line: Got it.

scenes.line: What do you think you're doing?

scenes.line: I was watching you. You want to know how long it really was?

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: No.

scenes.line: Eight minutes!

scenes.line: Dude, I'm gonna be here all week, right? Five days a week, I figure I'll start slow.

scenes.line: That's what I said.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: You know, get it right.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I know.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [to Susan] Cameras…

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: [enters] Oh, still here. Terrific.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Andy and I had a great conversation. And I just want to let you know that I am not going to be working here.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Well that's a shame.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: It just was one of those things-

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Is it? Because we talked about it and it seems like that might be what you want. Which is fine.

scenes.line: Where did this come from? Did Andy say that?

scenes.line: No, he did not, but I could tell he was struggling to understand what was expected of him.

scenes.line: What's the struggle? He made a great call, hired a great person.

scenes.line: You sure about that?

scenes.line: Absolutely.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: No games?

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: No games.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Because Andy seemed to think there was some information he was not able to share with me.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Okay, enough of this. I mean, really, enough. It's gotten way out of hand. Andrew, this is my wife. Whatever privacy you were trying to protect between us, I thank you for. But it is not welcome right now. Just be honest.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Andy?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yes?

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Why do you keep looking at my husband?

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Andy, just answer the question.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: No games?

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: No games.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Okay. I mean, it was kind of funny, actually. Robert storms in and he says, "in four seconds, my wife's gonna be in here. I told her she could work here. Under no circumstances can that be allowed to happen." [laughs]

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: You lying son of a bitch!

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Tell my wife you're lying.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I am lying. I am a compulsive liar.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: That's not true, is it?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: No, it's not. I tell the truth most of the time and I was just telling the truth about your husband. Jim knows. He was there.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: This is preposterous.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Robert…

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Let's get Jim in here. [Jim shoves out of fram in his chair, Robert looks for Jim] Where's Jim?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: He just rolled out and crawled out.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Can you call security, tell 'em to keep an eye out for him? Time to settle this.

scenes.line: [to Hank who is closing the gate] Oh wait, wait, wait! Hold on, hold on. I just need to get through. Just real quick. Real quick, open… uh, okay. [runs]

scenes.line: [sees Jim's abandoned car] That's weird. Well, he's gotta be around here somewhere.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [shoe falls while climbing ladder] Oh. Ow. Ow. Ow. [grunts] Creed. I was never here, all right?

scenes.speaker: Creed
scenes.line: Okay. What about your friend?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh boy.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: This is my gym, my rules. You do exactly as I say, no questions asked.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Yeah, I'm gonna ask questions and I might not do what you say.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: First thing, we're gonna stretch the pelvic bowl. Ready? Get down on the floor.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Okay, I'm not doing that.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Really? Too embarrassing for you? Huh? You wish that every exercise was strutting around the gym like the Fonz? Well how do you think the Fonz got so cool? He stretched his pelvic bowl!

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: I didn't know Darryl joined.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Looks that way.

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: Nice pelvic bowl. Deep.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Hello Jim. [Jim tries to escape]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [grabs Jim's leg] No, no. No, no, no! Don't! Damn it, Tuna!

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: So I think you know what we want to know.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Do I?

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [mutters] I know, I do.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Jim, I've had enough of your unhelpfulness.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I really wish I could help. I'm not really sure how I can…

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: For God's sake, did Robert tell you that he didn't want me working here?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: That's the thing. See, I didn't want to get in the middle of this. Still don't. But here's something: I feel that maybe, if we take a step back, this is a simple case of anxiety to work with a spouse.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [laughs] I think we've got ourselves an answer.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: No.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: That makes complete sense. Thank you all for a wonderful day.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Perfect!

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Jim…

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yes?

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Answer the question, please.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [sighs] I don't know what you want me to tell you. To be really honest, my wife works here. And I love it. She literally makes me work harder. She makes me smarter. She makes me remember why I'm here. And between us, she's on maternity leave right now, and I would love to leave this room and see her face. I would love it. I don't know how this helps, but it's just what I'm thinking.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: All right. Thanks.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yes. All right. Great. [leaves]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Uh…

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yep.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: [Robert holds the door, she walks through] Thank you. [leaves]

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: [claps Andy's shoulder] Heh.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Andy.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Hey, Mrs. California.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Hey. Uh, I'm sorry about the position you were put in today.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: You know, honestly, we all wanted you to work there. Except for him. Especially me.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Yeah, I thought we really hit it off.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Well, different circumstances.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Who knows?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Who knows?

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: Maybe after all this settles down…

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Totally.

scenes.speaker: Susan
scenes.line: It's a date.

scenes.line: Hmm?

scenes.line: You're nothing! You're so weak, you call yourself a man? Huh?

scenes.line: This doesn't help me. I don't respond to that kind of strategy.

scenes.line: Okay, fine. Finish your set on your own and never come back to my gym again!

scenes.line: Dwight, come back and spot me.

scenes.line: All right, I'll help you. But first, you gotta tell me what your goal is. What do you want?

scenes.line: No! Because if that was the case, the bar would be up by now. What is your goal?

scenes.line: Help me!

scenes.line: What do you want!?!

scenes.line: To look good for Val!

scenes.line: Val Kilmer? I don't buy it. That doesn't make any sense. Wow… I figured out your goal. I am going to make you the buffest dude Val Kilmer has ever seen.

scenes.line: They say that if you can strengthen your core, it improves your sexual performance. So, you will find me on the Ab-Blaster. And then you will find me blasting…uh, a very nice young woman.

scenes.line: Hey, what are you listening to?

scenes.speaker: Gabe
scenes.line: Steve Martin. [laughs, then falls] uh, I'm fine. [grunts]

scenes.line: Um, where's the shower?

scenes.line: There is no shower.

scenes.speaker: Kathy
scenes.line: There isn't?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: What does this look like, a shower store? Get lost.

scenes.line: You have got to be kidding me! No shower?!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Exercise lengthens life. Improves mood, boosts sex drive, and I've already covered the BM of it all. It's miraculous the effect that I will have on their lives.

scenes.line: So, Roberto Californio doesn't want to work with his wife. I get it. And, he wants to give his wife a job. Totally get it. What I am struggling with is the part of this that's impossible.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: I love my wife.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: This whole thing is making me very uncomfortable. I'm not getting between the boss and his wife so just ask me about something else. You know Stanley's tie is really the story of the day…

scenes.line: It's my birthday.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Ok, so that's a disaster. Luckily have a two-part plan. One, run. Two, hide. It's pretty smart, right? [walks into Vance Refrigeration office] Hi, how you doing? I'm Jim Halpert from across the hall. We are redoing our supply closet and I was wondEring if I could take a look at yours for some ideas.

scenes.line: Let me just check with Bob.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: You absolutely should. He said it was ok, so till you get him, I'll just be in, you know. [closes door behind him to supply closet]

scenes.line: [on phone] Bob? Jim just went into the closet.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Ugh! He's always one step ahead of us! How does he do that?

scenes.speaker: Mrs. California
scenes.line: This is insulting!

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: This whole accusation is insulting. Come on.

scenes.line: [Singing as if he were the dolls in his office] Christmas tiiiime is heeeere! [Normal voice] Wow. Thanks guys, that sounded amazing. Hi, I'm Andy Bernard and I am the first office Santa ever to make holiday wishes come true.

scenes.line: Holiday wishes.

scenes.line: What's that, Stanley?

scenes.line: We know exactly what holiday you're referring to.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: It is important to be mindful of all belief systems at our holiday party.

scenes.line: I've been here eighteen years and have suffered through some weird thematic Christmases. A Honolulu Christmas, A Pulp Fiction Christmas, A Muslim Christmas, Moroccan Christmas. Mo-rocca Christmas. I don't want it. Christmas is Christmas is Christmas is Christmas.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I got Stanley tickets to see Lewis Black for his birthday. …Might not have been the best idea.

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: I don't want no Kwanza wreath, I don't need a dreidel in my face, that's it's own thing. And who's that black Santa for?! I don't care! I know Santa ain't black! I could care less. I want Christmas! Just give me plain baby Jesus, lying in a manger, Christmas!

scenes.speaker: Meredith
scenes.line: What is the status on my wish?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Fulfilled! Brought my bicycle, so I can be your designated driver later. In the event that you drink to much, which is by no means required.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: What about my wish that we don't have to attend meetings that degrade our sense of adulthood?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: That, I cannot do, but I did get you an acre of property on the moon.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Where? Dark side or light side?

scenes.line: Light side.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Is it by the Sea of Tranquility?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: As a matter of fact, yes. Directly adjacent…beachfront.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Thank you, Andy.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: So, who's wish is next? Oh, what about Santa's wish? My biggest wish is that you all get along well with Jessica…C'mon guys, Jessica?…Jim, tell 'em who Jessica is.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: She's not your grandmother, is she?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Ugh! Gam-gam's name is Ruth, Jim, you should know. I introduced you on speakerphone that time?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Jessica is my super serious girlfriend, who is seriously awesome and seriously sexy. Only thing that's not serious, by the way? Our repartee.

scenes.speaker: Creed
scenes.line: That's great. When you know you know. Hey, what's Ruth's deal, man?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Totally out of your league. So in summation, ho ho ho, please be nice to Jessica and mistletoe is not an excuse for sexual assault, and don't go near Gam-gam.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: I love Jessica, and I haven't even met her yet. It's like we don't even need to meet, you know? I already love you. Stay home.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: I just want you to know that I will be mean to Jessica if you want me to be.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Oh no, no. It's fine, Kelly.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: It's really no problem. I was already planning on being mean to her.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: That's OK, I don't want you to do that.

scenes.line: [laughing] Hello, ah. Merry Christmas, Erin. Kelly, Happy Pancha Ganapati.

scenes.line: Eww, what is that?

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: The five day Hindu celebration in December honoring the god Ganesh, Patron of the Arts.

scenes.speaker: Kelly
scenes.line: Cool.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Hey, man.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: Hey! [Kevin embraces Robert in a tight hug] Oh!

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: How ya holdin' up…because of your wife leaving you?

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Kevin?

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: I actually appreciate the human intimacy. Feel like a kitten being cradled by a gorilla.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: It's been ten days since I had sexual intercourse.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Well you came to the right place…Ah, this, this party'll cheer you right up.

scenes.line: I hope so. The corporate party was wretched. I am so tired of the Black Eyed Peas. It's rock-n-roll for people who don't like rock-n-roll. It's rap for people who don't like rap. It's pop for people who don't like pop…ah, heartbreaking. [gestures to Andy in Santa costume]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Oh, thank you.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Well, I hate to have to take my Santa hat off, and put on my hard ass hat. [puts on baseball cap that has a foam rear-end on it with the words "HARD ASS"] But, this is serious. It's come to my attention that somebody who shall remain nameless, wants to switch desk clumps.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Fine with me. Jim can leave anytime he wants. Goodbye.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: It wasn't me.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: It wasn't either of you.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Kathy wants to leave our clump?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Sh sh sh sh! Don't look. Who it was is not important…but she did say that your constant pranking and one-upsmanship is driving her crazy. She or he.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I just wanna say, this is not my fault. OK? The weak always bully the strong. Contrary to what you see in the media. I am always acting in self-defense. Occasionally preemptive self-defense. [punches Jim in the arm]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Ow, What are you doing? [Jim fights back]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Hey! Hey! Respect the hat!

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Pam never seemed to have a problem with us.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Alright. I'm gonna speak in a language you both understand…Mo-nay.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: What was that?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: What is it?

scenes.line: OK!

scenes.line: OK.

scenes.line: Hey.

scenes.line: Ah, OK.

scenes.line: That's not what it should be, it should just be like a trinket or something.

scenes.line: [slurring slightly] It's that I wish Jessica was dead.

scenes.line: You you, wait. You mean you wish she wasn't here or something.

scenes.line: Hey, you know, you can't say that, OK? That's my girlfriend that you're talking about. You and I are not together anymore. You need to get over it! Take your wish back.

scenes.line: Too late! It's already been wished! And you promised it would come true. You wrote it in an email! So, which one are you? A murderer or a liar? [Andy leaves]

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Hey.

scenes.line: Hey.

scenes.line: Um.

scenes.line: That's awful.

scenes.line: Cici is Jim's daughter.

scenes.line: I don't-

scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.line: No!

scenes.line: O…K.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: It's, I mean.

scenes.line: Let me just see that one more time. Yep, you know what? I know who my friends are, now. But I shouldn't have got you involved because the truth is, I don't even really care about this picture, it's a little out of focus. It was probably an accident, right? Like…

scenes.line: What?

Dwight plays air violin/guitar and sings along] Hi-yah!!!!! [gabe, Creed and Nate join in as shots show various gift giving] Yeah!!!! Christmas!!!!

scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.line: No…I don't, hmm, I don't know.

scenes.line: OK.

scenes.line: By the way, I'm not gonna mess with you and Dwight's bonuses. I think it's causing more problems. So just be yourselves, have fun, and try not to let it affect your work.

scenes.line: Alright. I will definitely do that.

scenes.line: Alright, I'll tell Dwight.

scenes.line: You know what? You're sitting, and thinking, and it's probably better if it comes from me anyway.

scenes.line: Christmas miracles do happen.

scenes.line: Yes. They totally do.

scenes.line: Well help me, OK? Just, uh take…

scenes.line: I'm trying but you need to-

scenes.line: Hey.

scenes.line: And…

scenes.line: And what?

scenes.line: And you have any advice or anything?

scenes.speaker: Robert
scenes.line: No [laughs] my god.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: …Help me feel better…

scenes.line: I've been married thrice and each has ended in an acrimonious divorce, I'm not sure I'm the best person to give love advice…I was hoping you were gonna make me feel better.

scenes.speaker: Nate
scenes.line: When you do your makeup,

scenes.speaker: Jessica
scenes.line: Uh huh.

scenes.line: How long you, does it take usually? Cause…

scenes.line: Um, it ta-, um it depends.

scenes.speaker: Toby
scenes.line: …Chad Flendermen's kryptonite. [Darryl walks up to Toby and Val in a tuxedo]

scenes.line: OK great.

scenes.line: OK

scenes.line: Perfect.

scenes.speaker: Jessica
scenes.line: Bye [kiss]…I still don't get why you can't just call her a cab and pay for it.

scenes.speaker: Jessica
scenes.line: Oh

scenes.speaker: Jessica
scenes.line: OK [laughs] Bye.

scenes.line: OK, bye. [helps Meredith off the floor] Alright Meredith,

scenes.line: Thank god Erin's getting a ride home with Robert because she is trashed. [laughs] and who better to drive her home than Robert, I mean, what a stand up guy, you know? scenes.line: Let's go, let's go.
