scenes.line: Sure, yeah, go ahead.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Thanks, dude. You—you sure it's okay? 'Cause you're kinda—

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yeah, absolutely. Do people like sitting next to you? You're clean, right?

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Oh, Dove Men.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Nice. Music. Do you listen to it in earbuds? You don't listen to it at all because we're at work, not a Florence and the Machine concert, so—

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Yeah, could I just have a minute to prepare for this?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Sure, yeah. Do whatever you need to do.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Thanks, dude.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Right after you do one thing for me. I need you to breathe in my face.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Why?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I need you to breathe in my face right now.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: [exhales]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: What are we working with, peppermint or wintergreen?

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Wintergreen.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I knew it, I knew it.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Yeah, good nose.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I looked at you coming around, and I said, "Wintergreen."

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I can't hire Clark. Yeah, he looks like a Schrute, but he thinks like a Halpert and he acts like a Beesly.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Okay, here's one. A customer who ordered enough paper to qualify for a volume discount now wants to return half the stock. You can't rebate the sales price or credit for future purchases because you brokered the deal for a third party.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: That's just a classic no-win situation.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Thank you.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: So I'd Kobayashi Maru it.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Damn it! Perfect answer, again.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Yep.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Think Dwight, think. You have a ream of 16-bond …

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: You know what, Dwight?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: And anoth—

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: This interview's over, and I get the job. I just Kobayashi Maru'd the whole process.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: No.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Yeah. Star Trek rules.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: It does, but still no.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Come on, man. I mean, did Trevor do that? Did Rolf do that?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh, you think they're my only friends? I've got way more friends than that, and they're all better than the losers who work here.

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: This is not natural.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Just – I don't wanna make assumptions based on people's physical appearances.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Well, of course not, but does physical appearance include smell?

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: They smell so bad.

scenes.speaker: Meredith
scenes.line: If I ever get that bad, you'd tell me, right?

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Meredith, I tell you all the time.

scenes.speaker: Meredith
scenes.line: [chuckles] Walked right into that one.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Next up, my cousin Mose. Mose could make a great paper salesman. He's got a natural fear of paper, which would motivate him to get as much of it out of this office as possible. I've got big expectations, Mose-wise.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: What quality would make you a good sales associate?

scenes.speaker: Mose
scenes.line: People person.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: It says here on your resume that you spent the last 15 years as a sales rep for Dow Chemical.

scenes.speaker: Mose
scenes.line: That's right.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: You know we live together, right?

scenes.speaker: Mose
scenes.line: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: And I've never seen you go to work, ever.

scenes.speaker: Mose
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: So why is this on your resume? [door slams]

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: So how'd you guys hear about the position?

scenes.speaker: Gabor
scenes.line: My—my mom.

scenes.speaker: Nate
scenes.line: Dwight called my house, but he didn't realize that I had already moved out, because my mom and I are quarrelling because I- I can't stay out of her stuff.

scenes.speaker: Zeke
scenes.line: Dwight's my cousin, so I overheard him telling my brother Mose about the job opportunity in the shower.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: You were in the shower or he was in the shower?

scenes.speaker: Zeke
scenes.line: Everyone was in the shower. It's a cow shower, so there's like, a ton of people in there.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: So you guys all know Dwight already?

scenes.speaker: Melvina
scenes.line: I was his babysitter, and then we dated for a while. He was a passionate lover and the sweetest little baby.

scenes.speaker: Gabor
scenes.line: I knew you looked familiar. You used to pick up Dwight from school.

scenes.speaker: Melvina
scenes.line: You went to X-Men school too? [exhales]

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: X-Men school?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: When I was young, I spent several years at a private school where I was told I would be taught to harness my mutant abilities. Turned out it was a conman copying Charles Xavier's School for Gifted Youngsters from the X-Men comic books. Took me years to figure out that it was a con. Some people never figured it out.

scenes.speaker: Gabor
scenes.line: Oh, I have a few powers. Night hearing. Dogs understand where I point. And our training included picking carrots, scrubbing tubs, sewing imitation Levi's. A lot of telemarketing.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: I don't want to sit near any of those people for the next 20 years. Someone say something.

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: I said something when they were thinking of hiring Jim. Didn't work then. And now look what he's doing to us.

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: Yeah, Jim, this is all your fault.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: How is it my fault?

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: Here's an exercise for you, Jim. Imagine there are consequences to your actions. Imagine the whole world does not revolve around this. There are others.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: But it's Dwight who's bring in all the weirdos.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Yeah, but Jim, Dwight's a weirdo. We can't blame a weirdo for bringing in weirdos. We can blame a normal for creating a situation where a weirdo was allowed to bring in weirdos.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Hey, I'm the one who has to sit next to this weirdo when Jim's away. I'm in a position where I'm rooting for Nate, and that just feels wrong. [sighs] Forget it. I need to work on my mural. I have some pointy trees that I need to round off.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: [on phone] Hey Jim, I thought our call was for later.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yeah, this is actually about the new sales guy. Uh, Dwight has brought in a bunch of real weirdos. And I was wondEring if I could have some input—

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [presses speaker button] This is Dwight Schrute. Who am I speaking to? And don't lie. I can tell if you're lying.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Hey, Dwight. It's David.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: David.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Jim says he'd like some say in the hiring process.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Really? That's interesting. 'Cause I was thinking that since Jim is only here part time, he might not be as invested in the decision-making process as someone like me who's here every day. And frankly, killing it lately.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I was just thinking that because this person is gonna be sitting at my desk, near my wife—

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Jim, another thing. Since we are gonna have to hire this junior sales associate to cover for you, I am going to have to pay you only for the days that you actually work.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh. Um…

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Okay. I can't say that that's not fair.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Sounds fair to me, David.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: And I know we have a call scheduled for later –

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh, yeah, so we'll just do that later.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: No. Why not do it now?

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Yeah. What's up Jim?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Uh… [clears throat] Well, it's about Athlead. I'm sorry. Does Dwight have to be on this part of the phone call?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I'd love to be in the loop, David.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: It's okay. Go ahead, Jim.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: There's a very exciting opportunity to be a core investor –

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Okay. Jim, I'm gonna have to stop you right there.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yes, okay. Bye.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [whispers] I'd love to invest.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: No, thanks.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I'd like to give you $100 million. [snickers] [phone ringing]

scenes.speaker: Hide
scenes.line: Why you make trees into bushes? You don't make paper from bushes.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Hide, they're giving out jobs upstairs. Why don't you go up and get one?

scenes.speaker: Hide
scenes.line: Thank you.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Troy
scenes.line: Whoops.

scenes.speaker: Zeke
scenes.line: [patting Darryl's hair] It's dense. Like bread.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Dwight, you can't just hire someone 'cause they're your friend.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I'm not. These people are the best of the best. I find talent an attractive quality in a friend.

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: They're freaks, Dwight. All your friends are weirdos and freaks.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: You know who else was a freak? Spider-man. And he was also a hero.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Your friends are like Spider-man, if he had gotten bitten by a spider and then got really into masturbating.

scenes.speaker: Wolf
scenes.line: Man, how cool is it gonna be when I start working here? Paintball fights at lunch.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Mandatory paintball. Uh, wolf, please report to the parking lot for mandatory paintball at lunch.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Wolf is hilarious. He has executed me over 100 times at point-blank range. Half of 'em, we were on the same team. Oh my God. How I screamed. Ah, that goof.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Sell me this piece of paper. Watch this.

scenes.speaker: Wolf
scenes.line: Do you want this paper?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I sure do.

scenes.speaker: Wolf
scenes.line: It's not very good.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I will pay you whatever it takes.

scenes.speaker: Wolf
scenes.line: I think I wanna keep it now. It must be pretty special if you want it so bad.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: No, you have lots of other pieces of paper that are just like it. So here, just take my money.

scenes.speaker: Wolf
scenes.line: Stop trying to get my paper buddy. Okay read my lips. It's over.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Okay. Good. That was great. So. Wow. You're still at the 570 number?

scenes.speaker: Wolf
scenes.line: I am.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Okay. Good, good, good. [sighs]

scenes.speaker: Hide
scenes.line: I have eight years experience selling electronics in Sanyo store in downtown Tokyo. I was a doctor. And I have a business degree from Tokyo University.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: This isn't gonna work out.

scenes.speaker: Hide
scenes.line: Thank you. [chuckles]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Nate is a proven entity, but not without his handicaps; hearing, vision, basic cognition. Trevor is great, but I saw no fire in him today. And this is a guy who loves to start fires. Troy is literally one of a kind. He's a goblin, or a hobbit, or a kobold, which is a type of gremlin. And yet I'm hesitant. Why can't I pull the trigger on any of them?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [groaning] No, no, no. I just need to tell them. I just need to tell them. [knock at door]

scenes.speaker: Melvina
scenes.line: Do you need to be changed?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I do that myself now.

scenes.speaker: Melvina
scenes.line: Mm. Are you going to make a decision soon? I've been double-parked for five hours. I'm wondEring if I should move my car.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: No, you've been towed by now. They tow after about 45 minutes.

scenes.speaker: Melvina
scenes.line: Well, the joke's on them. I live right next to the tow yard. All they did was save me some gas.

scenes.speaker: Trevor
scenes.line: Hey man, we get how difficult this is. And no matter how you choose, we're still gonna be your friend.

scenes.speaker: Wolf
scenes.line: Yeah, whether it's me or Troy Underbridge, or Gabor, or Melvina—

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Or none of you [chuckles]

scenes.speaker: Wolf
scenes.line: Yeah, you'd bring us all down here, put us through the wringer and then choose none of us.

scenes.speaker: Trevor
scenes.line: Can you imagine how insulting that would be? The contempt that a person like that would have to have for you.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I wish I could hire all of you.

scenes.speaker: Zeke
scenes.line: I could start Monday.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Psst. Jim Jim? [whispEring] Jim, turn around. Jim, turn around. Jim, turn around.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Ahh, I love staring off in one direction. If I'm not looking south, I'm not livin'. That's what I always say.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Just act natural. [grunts]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: And I was thinking it's only fair that you help make this decision since they'll be sitting at your desk next to your wife.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: But you know I wouldn't hire any of these all-stars.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Aah! God, that sucks! Aah! What are you gonna do? I mean, it's your call.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Nope. Your friends not turning out to be as great as you thought? Not even Gabor?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I guess I just have higher standards for my work colleagues than for my friends. I just couldn't picture any of them in the old gold and gray.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I knew it. You designed a uniform for Dunder Mifflin.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Summer. Winter. Jungle. Formal.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Well, I for one, was amazed at how qualified everyone was. You?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Yes. Thank you. Amazed.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: And I gotta say, this was a tough decision. And we had to go with none of you.

scenes.speaker: Sensei Ira
scenes.line: I'm sorry?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: What? This is such bullcrap!

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Well, you know, Wallace put me in charge, so you have no say.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Wow. So much crap. It's just a load of B.C. How could you do this to them?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Too much now.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Nate
scenes.line: Do we get our resumes back or do you keep them? Because I only have the one, and I have a chili recipe on the back that I really wanna keep.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Okay, this is an outrage. Ugh! You know what? This is Jim Halpert's home address, in case you guys wanna toilet paper his house or whatever.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: That seems inconsiderate.

scenes.speaker: Rolf
scenes.line: No. We get it. Thanks so much for the opportunity, Dwight. Don't open any suspicious packages you may receive. No, wait. Do open them. Totally safe.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Guys, it wasn't up to me. Rolf, come on. Guys, it wasn't my choice! I would have hired all of you! Gabor, Gabor.

scenes.speaker: Trevor
scenes.line: Well, my day's shot.

scenes.speaker: Rolf
scenes.line: Yeah, it's that weird hour where it's too late to start a slow roast and too early for a Swanson's.

scenes.speaker: Wolf
scenes.line: I got it. Paintball.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh, that sounds awesome. Can we wait till I get off work?

scenes.speaker: Trevor
scenes.line: [yelling] And what are we supposed to do until then?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Wolf
scenes.line: Let's just go, you guys.

scenes.speaker: Rolf
scenes.line: Yeah. No limit on weapons class, right?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: All right. I think that went well.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: So, uh, if you just take a look at this, and then that'll print out—Hey. Meet your new desk mate.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: What's up good lookin'?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Oh, cool. Hey Clark.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Trust me, this is the least of all evils. It took me all day to pull this off, so you should be thrilled, considEring.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Yeah, I guess. I mean, I kinda liked my old desk mate.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Okay. I'm really sorry I told the guys I'd be there for the board meeting.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Of course.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I'll call you when I get there.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: All right.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Bye.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Take care of my wife. I will be back.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: They say that everyone outgrows their friends at some point in their lives. Well I just outgrew them all in the span of three hours.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Hey, Pam, I'm going to the kitchen. You want anything?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I'm good.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh, hey, I'll take a coffee.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Oh, I'm sorry. You gotta be this cool for coffee.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [scoffs]

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Hey, Dwight. Wanna haze the new guy?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Who, me?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Us.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Absolutely, I do. [giggles]

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Okay. Okay, here. Okay, so the next time he goes to the bathroom, I'll distract him, you take that.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Okay, yeah, I know what to do. Okay. Oh, that's great.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: [shushes]

scenes.speaker: Pam & Dwight
scenes.line: [laughs]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Aah!

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: No!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Welcome to the club, pig! [laughs]

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: No, Dwight!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Aah!

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: No, it does matter who ends up sitting next to Pam when I'm gone. The people around you are basically who you end up spending your life with. I mean, because of where my desk was, I spent all those years looking at Pam, and I fell in love. So, that stuff matters. Definitely does.

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: Have you seen Darryl?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: He's around here somewhere.

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: Mmm. [exits, Erin smiles deviously]

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Yeah, Darryl's here. So is Santa Claus. It's just a regular Thursday. [checks for anyone around] Neither guy is here. And, it's Friday. Welcome to me and Darryl's world of lies.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Nobody knows it yet, but Darryl already started working in Philly. So now, he has to sneak out of here like the sneakiest little sneaky-sneak you ever saw. And I'm his helper. It's so fun.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: [as Darryl descends stairs, Erin ascends carrying a giant teddy bear] Darryl. Meet… bear… ull.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: How much did you pay for that?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Nothing. Won him at the carnival. Spent a ton on tickets, though. Drive safe.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Everybody knows I go to Philly. I've just been using sick days I saved up. But, Erin was so excited about being sneaky-sneaks, I went along with it.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: [exiting Darryl's office] Ha, ha, ha! Darryl, you are too much! [to Phyllis] That guy's hilarious. He's here today. [giant teddy bear is viewed in Darryl's office]

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I've really been putting in the hours on this mural. And my boss is totally OK with it, because he's in the Bahamas and has no clue what anybody is doing. I'm usually very self-critical. I hate what I paint. But, I don't know, this time I feel like it's, um, it's really coming together… [sees mural] Oh my god! [camera pans to mural with butts painted over it] Wha? You've gotta be kidding me! What it… are those… are those butts? [to warehouse crew] Huh? No way. No way!

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: Excuse me, everyone. Is it OK if I leave early from work today? It's Phillip's first birthday and the senator and I are hosting a party at our house.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Aw, cute! So there'll be a bunch of kids.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: No. No children. Our house is not kid-friendly. Most of our furniture is sharp. Also, ew. It will mostly be campaign donors.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Angela, I am prepared to donate a whopping… [pulls cash from wallet] 8 dollars to Lipton For America to have an invitation…

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: No, no, please. You know, actually, none of you could even really make the cut for this thing. Which I am so sad about.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: [undertone] Angela. You're going to find out, so I thought I'd let you know that, uh, Robert invited me too.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: What?

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: He said he wanted me there for support.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: I'm his! His… wife.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Angela's husband and I are in love. But, as a politician in this town, you still need the conventional blonde wife on your lawn signs. He is risking everything to have me there today. [laughs] Me.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: [on phone with Robert] We agreed that you wouldn't be seen with him in public. It's humiliating for me. Well, if you get to bring a stud, maybe I do too.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [in Darryl and Jim's Philly apartment] Hey.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Hey.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: We are splitting a sublet on a place near Philly.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Just a couple of grown, sexy-ass roommates.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: And, as much as I miss Pam and the kids, it's, uh, kinda nice to live the bachelor life again. You know, let your hair down.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Jim was nice enough to give me his bedroom.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I'm couching it!

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Which usually means there's clothes all over the living room.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: And this dude labels his food. He's the clean one. And, I'm the messy one. How much fun is this?

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: I love Jim. I love that he hooked me up with a job. It's just, he uses old t-shirts as wash rags. He doesn't wash his dishes. Apparently, they need to [quote-unquote fingers] soak… He hooked me up with a job.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: [ascends on lift, using megaphone] Attention, everyone. Can I have your attention, please? Yeah, I don't know everybody's name down here, but whoever did this will you please raise your hand. [no one replies] Hello? This is not over. OK? I will stay up here all day if I have to. Is that what you want? [descends on lift] Yeah, I will also come down if I want to. It's my choice.

scenes.speaker: Pam

Val's no help. Andy's gone. Jim's out. I just feel like I'm on my own here. [boom microphone bumps her head, she smiles] I mean, OK, not completely on my own. But, in terms of people who can do something. Thank you, Brian.

scenes.line: Yes. Thank you. Let's answer that question.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: I was politely saying nothing can be done. I thought I was clear.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: What? Come on guys. We need to figure out who did this and punish them. This isn't just about me. This is about all of us. This is our mural. Don't you see? How much we worked on this? How much time and energy? We put our heart and soul into this thing.

scenes.line: David Wallace called this meeting?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Sure did. I was as surprised as you, but apparently, he is very passionate about public art.

scenes.speaker: Pam

scenes.line: Pam, I'll help you.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: You will?

scenes.line: If there's anything I hate worse than art, it's crime.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Thank you.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Yeah?

scenes.line: Great.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Or melons. Like cantaloups. With the halves are cut off. And then, just the bottom parts…

scenes.line: It's all right. It's all right.

scenes.line: No. She needs her rest again.

scenes.line: It's cool. Reading's tricky sometimes.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh, um… Are you really mad about this?

scenes.line: That's my go-to thermos. That's all.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh. It's your go-to therm. Oh, man. That's a bummer. I'm sorry about that.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: No big deal. No big deal.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: No, no. If it's a big deal, it's a big deal.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Nah, nah…

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: No big deal.

scenes.line: [as Jim empties thermos into trash] Nah, nah, nah. You don't have to do that.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: I don't know. You gonna wash it? Or you gonna let it soak?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [after tense pause] OK. Here ya go. [roughly hands Darryl his thermos]

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Thank you.

scenes.line: So, Frank. Do you have any thoughts about what was done? By you?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: [to Nellie] Maybe, maybe I could, could get the ball rolling. [Nellie nods] Um, Frank? Hi. Pam. Um, I am so sorry if I've done anything to offend you. I'm sure it isn't easy for you guys to have an upstairs person coming down in your space. So. Truly. If, if, I apologize. But enough about me. Your turn.

scenes.speaker: Toby
scenes.line: [Warehouse Worker Frank remains silent, picks ear] You sort of deserve an apology here. Frank?

scenes.speaker: Frank
scenes.line: I'm sorry I didn't like your crappy doodles. I drew a butt. Big deal. Butts are funny.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Well, I didn't think that butt was funny.

scenes.speaker: Frank
scenes.line: Well, maybe if you got the stick out of yours.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: What was that?

scenes.speaker: Frank
scenes.line: You know what? You people can't fire me. So, screw you. [exits]

scenes.line: Whoa! Hey! That is not OK. What are you gonna do about that?

scenes.speaker: Toby
scenes.line: Uh… it… compliment…

scenes.line: That sucked. He didn't apologize. There's no talking to that guy.

scenes.line: Oh, your little feelings party didn't work out? Huh? Who won the hugging contest? Oh, let me guess. Everyone tied for first.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: We should just take him down.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Wait. Are you saying…

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I'm saying we should go scorched earth on that guy's face.

scenes.line: He messed with something that was important to you. We need to mess with something that's important to him.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Yes!

scenes.line: A little eye for an eye action.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Yes!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Go all Hammurabi on this clown.

scenes.line: We need an infiltrator.

scenes.line: I know just the man for the job. [looks at Clark]

scenes.line: Clark?

scenes.line: He even looks like a mole.

scenes.speaker: Senator Lipton
scenes.line: Yes. We're good friends. Good friends.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Senator Lipton
scenes.line: You know, I suppose that may ruffle a few feathers. For a long time, our party has turned it's back on the Hispanic people. Well, that is not who I am. [puts arms around Oscar] I am a friend of the Latino community. And if you ask me, it's time we bid bigotry hasta luego. [guests laugh] Now, does my embrace of Hispanics make me more electable? Given demographic trends? I don't know. And I don't care. What I care about is Oscar. [slaps Oscar's cheek] My friend. Mi amigo. Oscar. [guests applaud as he hugs Oscar]

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Maybe I should be insulted that he only invited me here to be his token Mexican friend. But, he could of invited any number of Hispanics that he knows. His gardener, Rogelio. Or he could've invited… Rogelio. But, he chose me. Rogelio's Malaysian… The son of a bitch is Malaysian.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Oh, hey.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: I usually watch TV during my lunch breaks. It's cool?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yeah. Totally.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: All right.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [after Darryl eyes him drinking from a thermos] It's mine. Don't worry.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: I didn't say anything.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I don't think you had to.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Excuse me?

scenes.line: I think you might be going a little crazy with this labeling thing, man. I mean, you put your name on a five pound bag of flour. Are you honestly saying that if I needed flour I couldn't use that?

scenes.line: What you need flour for, Jim?

scenes.line: That's not the point.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: What? You making bread?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: No, I'm not making bread.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: What kind of bread you making? Pumpernickel?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Darryl, it doesn't matter. I think you know the point I'm trying to make.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: All right, I'm being a jerk. You got me this job. I should be grateful. I am, I just… you know, I get finicky about my stuff. That's all.

scenes.line: It's all good. Are we all good?

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: We good.

scenes.line: What's that cooler?

scenes.line: Nothing. [pulls out a can of soda] It's mine. [Jim shakes his head] [after looking through DVR] What happened to my Tavis Smileys?

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Well, my only crime was loving the local sports teams and trying to be one of the guys.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Silence. You'll now be working in the warehouse with the untouchables. Now, go make your hands rough with work.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: OK, boss. [quietly] Pam, you know this is ridiculous, right? Like you're smarter than this.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Shh, shh.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: This is never gonna work.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Shh. Remember your lines.

scenes.line: What lines?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Go move some paper!

scenes.line: [to Darryl on phone] Hey, you know that guy Frank who works in the warehouse?

scenes.line: OK. What does he like? What's important to him? Does he have like a favorite pair of boots or a lunch box or…

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: What? Is he retiring? You getting him a gift or something?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Yeah, something like that.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: I know he loves his pick up truck.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Oh, great! [to Dwight] His truck!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Great. Get the plate number.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: OK. [to Darryl] Do you know the plate… never mind. Why would you know that? And why would I be asking that?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: So we know which truck to van…

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Hey. While I got you on the phone, your husband's like a sloppy, homeless hobo. Can you fix that?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Yeah. I was kinda hoping you could. I gotta go. Bye. [to Dwight] Come on. [camera pans to Clark duct taped to a chair]

scenes.line: Hold on a second. Uh, Sandeep? Let's get you closer to the senator. Just about there. Great. And, Oscar? I'm gonna need you to step a little closer to the senator, as well. Somewhere there.

scenes.line: He's blocking me.

scenes.line: It's only a photo, honey.

scenes.line: [to party waiter] Excuse me, uh, what's your name?

scenes.line: Angela.

scenes.line: I saw that. That's great!

scenes.line: Good. I'm glad you feel better. This has been a wonderful day. I have to say, I like hanging out with a vengeful bitch.

scenes.line: I know. You miss Angela, don't you?

scenes.line: Ugh! Don't sympathize. You're ruining the mood. Back to work. Draw his penis.

scenes.line: Hey, hey, hey! [knocks Frank down with boom microphone]

scenes.line: Whoa.

scenes.line: [as Frank gets up] Easy! [Frank grabs him]

scenes.line: You son of a bitch!

scenes.line: Oh. Oh!

scenes.line: Erin says she's gonna break up with Andy, but I'm not sure. He's coming back tomorrow and surprise, today, she wants to do whatever I'd like. You know, when I was a kid, we had a dog who go real sick and we had to 'send him to a farm'. And on his last day, we did everything he loved.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Great.

scenes.speaker: Pete
scenes.line: I'll get my coat.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Perfect. [Pete walks away eying the camera knowingly]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [knocks on Andy's door, then pretends to answer as Andy] Come in.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [talking to Andy's empty chair] Andy, hi. I just made another huge sale for the company that you manage. I need you to authorize that expense report and sign off on that contract.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [pretending to be Andy] I would be happy to. It would be my pleasure, Mr. Schrute. Rick-a-dick-doo, rick-a-dick-dick-dick, rick-a-dick-doo.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I really like Andy these days. He's pretend and he does exactly as I tell him to. All that will change when real Andy comes back tomorrow. [thinks for a moment] Unless he comes back as pretend Dwight. In which case, we're in for an epic, confusing showdown.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Andy left a carton of milk in the fridge. So, I've been sneaking a little bit every day for the last three months. It's been yummy. But now, Andy's coming back. So, I guess it's goodbye chunky, lemon milk.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: [to entire office] OK, I'll say it. I wish Andy had stayed on his trip.

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: I say we all have one last fun boss-less day.

scenes.speaker: Meredith
scenes.line: Yeah, let's get some booze and some cocaine and just blow it out. No consequences.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Or the mini mall. They have all these Valentine Day deals. You can get 20% off if you come in with your husband or your [to Nellie] boyfriend. But, I mean, if you don't have one of those you can probably just bring whoever it is you use to kill your loneliness.

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: Phil, I'll pretend to be your husband. I'm already sick of you, so it'll seem realistic.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Oh…

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: They have a nail salon there where I get my feet detailed. [to Meredith] They use a watch repair kit.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: [to Angela] Ew! I'll be your foot buddy.

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: Everyone, it is our last day here with no manager. I say we go to the mini mall. Clark, you will be my fake boyfriend so I can get the discount.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: It's what I do. [everyone begins to leave]

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Darryl, everyone seems to be pairing off. Do you want to pretend to be a couple so we get the…

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: No… yes, yes. Why wouldn't I… wanna pretend to be gay? Got no problem with that.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: All right, it'll be easy. Don't be nervous, just follow my…

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: [interrupting] Stop talking 'bout it. I said I'm fine with it.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: [eating] These are gross.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: They are terrible.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Oh, hey, don't fill up on chocolates. I made us a lunch reservation at State Street Grill.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh my god. That's so romantic.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: It's with Brian and Alyssa.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh my god. That's less romantic.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I know. But we should go. We need to thank him for, you know, saving my life.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yeah, yeah. No, totally. That's good. So, should we just get a bottle of wine later and celebrate?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: That sounds nice.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I'm very excited to see Brian. Brian's a great guy. And Pam and I have gotten really close to he and his wife, Alyssa over the years. And he got fired for protecting my wife from a jerk in the warehouse. I'm sorry, but you know him. He's a good guy.

scenes.speaker: Nail stylist 1
scenes.line: Oh, tiny, poor lady is back. Oh, get the baby clipper. [other nails stylists gush over Angela]

scenes.speaker: Nail stylist 2
scenes.line: [to Clark] You take off your glasses.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: 'Kay. [removes glasses]

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: [nail stylist 2 giggles] What?

scenes.speaker: Nail stylist 2
scenes.line: Your boyfriend. He look like a pretty girl.

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: My boyfriend does look like a pretty girl, doesn't he? Yes, a very little pretty girl. And you know what, now that you are developing, we should go and get you a training bra. [both laugh at Clark]

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Oh, you guys think this is funny? You know what? No more discount. [to nail manager] Excuse me. [gesturing he and Nellie] Full price. We're not together.

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: Oh, come on!

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: She's living a lie.

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: Turns out, I can't even be in a pretend relationship.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: [to nail manager] Hi. We'd like a couples discount on a pair of foot massages.

scenes.speaker: Nail manager
scenes.line: No. No discount for two men. Two men are not a couple.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: We are together. Romantically.

scenes.speaker: Nail manager
scenes.line: Two men? [other nail stylist speaks Korean to manager, both laugh] [gestures index fingers bumping together] Doesn't work. No discount.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Oh, it works. Him and me, all right, we are crazy in love. More love than your small mind can comprehend. And we have two disposable incomes. And no kids. And we're taking our business elsewhere. [Oscar and Darryl exit holding hands]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: [enters restaurant with Pam] Hey, Brian.

scenes.speaker: Brian
scenes.line: Hey.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Sorry we're late.

scenes.speaker: Brian
scenes.line: Oh, uh, no problem. I finished all the bread.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Ha,ha,ha, yeah OK.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: What?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: He's on a no carb thing. Supposedly.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh.

scenes.speaker: Brian
scenes.line: It's, uh, great to see you guys. Thanks for coming.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Are you kidding? Thank you, man. I mean, I've wanted the opportunity to say thanks for… everything. And I'm really sorry about the job. That just seems crazy.

scenes.speaker: Brian
scenes.line: It's fine. What are you gonna do, you know? But, if you guys know of any work, I'm fully available.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Well, my dad can't hear a thing. You could boom his whole life for him.

scenes.speaker: Brian
scenes.line: That's… OK, great. Does he pay well?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Where's Alyssa?

scenes.speaker: Brian
scenes.line: Uh, yeah. Um, you know, Alyssa's, she's not gonna make it today.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Oh.

scenes.speaker: Brian
scenes.line: Actually, we're not gonna make it. Um… we're splitting up.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [to Andy's empty chair] I have yet another sales order for you to sign.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [acting as Andy] Why thank you Mr. Schrute. I don't know how you do it. You're a god. Rick-a-dick-dick-doo.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [in his office doorway, bearded and unkept] Hi Dwight.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: You're back. [surveys Andy] And you're disgusting.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: [as everyone returns to the office] Ah, geez. My nails aren't dry yet. I don't think I can work for at least a couple hours.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Well, well, well, look who it is.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Andy.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I guess I can cancel my order from Zappos.com because, oh, the loafers have arrived.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Andy!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Hey! Sweetheart! [approaches Erin] I have missed you so much.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: [obviously avoiding Andy's embrace] Yes. [gives Andy high fives] Welcome back, buddy.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [attempting to hug Erin as she resists] I have been dreaming of this moment.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Me too. So much. I'm so happy.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: I am really, really bad at break ups. Technically, I'm still dating my first grade boyfriend. I mean, we just had our 20th anniversary. And, I forgot to get him something.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: What happened? We thought you were coming back tomorrow.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Well, Valentine's surprise for Erin. Hello? Super romantic. And I got you something. [removes wooden instruments from bag] Oh, it's a couple of pieces of bamboo. Big deal, right? No. These are musical instruments. It's so we can play island music together. Cause I have this. [removes güiro and begins playing and singing] Clop the cloppers. Yeah, clop 'em. It's called Bembe. [sings while Kevin echoes]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Hey, Burning Man, if it's not selling out too much, you might want to throw on a tie. David Wallace is gonna be here in an hour.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Obviously, that's why I'm here. I mean, I came back early to surprise Erin. Happy Valentine's Day, sweetheart. [tries to embrace Erin but she begins playing cloppers] But, I'm just saying, I'm also excited about the Wallace meeting.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Why? Isn't he just coming in to rip you a new one for being gone three months?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: No. Please. Come on, Clark. Wallace knows that he's been gone for the last three months. [Andy stalls] Right? Wallace does know that you've been gone for the last three months?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I have no idea. I don't know what he knows or doesn't know. But we've been in touch the whole time. I mean, it's not hard to get high-speed internet in Turks de Caicos, people. It's in every Bembe cafe.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: He only emailed me four times.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Question. Where's Jim?

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: He and Pam are having their Valentine's Day lunch.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: For two hours? Really?

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: So, you're concerned about peoples' long absence from their place of work?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: If the shoe fits. [plays güiro and sings, Kevin echoes]

scenes.speaker: Brian
scenes.line: We were telling two different versions of the same story. And then, everything just went numb.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Well, I mean, that's OK. It doesn't mean that it's over. Right? I mean, couples fight.

scenes.speaker: Brian
scenes.line: Yeah. That's the thing. When we were fighting, it weirdly felt like the relationship was still alive. And, it wasn't until we stopped fighting that, we realized that it was over. You know, it's over. [overcome by emotion] I'm sorry, this is… oh my god, OK. [to Pam] We have to stop seeing each other like this. We have to find a different way to communicate other than breaking down in front of each other.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: [obviously flustered] Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: What?

scenes.speaker: Brian
scenes.line: At least my crying won't get you fired.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Crying?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I noticed that you landed the Scranton White Pages account. That is tremendous.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Thank you.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: And you sold it to Jan too.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Yes!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I mean… I'm impressed.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [laughing together] Yeah!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Well, there's one problem. Couldn't help but notice that you offered a price point that was not approved by the head office. So… gotta run that stuff by me, Dwight.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: You were on a boat.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I was…

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: On a boat.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: That…

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: In the ocean.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: OK. The issue is that you need to run this stuff by me. Coolio? Are we coolio? [Dwight resists] Just say the word 'coolio'.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I'm not gonna say it.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Say it.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Not a word.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Coolio.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: No! [Andy makes a call] What do you think you're doing?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Just gonna call the Scranton White Pages and clear this right up.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Don't you dare! Andy!

scenes.speaker: Jan
scenes.line: [on phone] Hello?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Hey, Jan. Nard dog here.

scenes.speaker: Jan
scenes.line: Oh, Andy.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I was just looking over the paperwork. I found a little hiccup.

scenes.speaker: Jan
scenes.line: Really?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yeah. It appears my employee offered you a price that he was not authorized to.

scenes.speaker: Jan
scenes.line: Hmm.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [whispers] Coolio.

scenes.speaker: Jan
scenes.line: Seriously? You're calling me a few weeks after finalizing our contract to gouge me now for more money? Is that what you're doing?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Coolio. Coolio.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: No. No, no, no Jan I think you misunderstood.

scenes.speaker: Jan
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Coolio.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: It, it's, it's actually just an issue…

scenes.speaker: Jan
scenes.line: You know what? You know what, uh, Nard dog? There is an option in the contract that allows me to back out within 30 days of signing. So, I would like to exercise that option.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: No, Jan! Please do not listen to this boob! Remember Clark. He gave you everything. Everything.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Jan, I don't know what he's talking about but…

scenes.speaker: Jan
scenes.line: Tell Angela to send me a final invoice.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Well, ah, ah…

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Please Ja, Ja… [Jan hangs up]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Aw! That was not how I had hoped that would go.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [approaching Accounting] Hey, everybody, great job. [to Angela] Listen, we're a smidge behind on my paychecks.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: Yes, well, as you know, we get paid on Fridays. And you haven't been here for 12 Fridays. [hands Andy a folder]

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: All right. Thank you very much. [examines checks] Looking good. [after noticing something on Angela's desk] Who's that little fella?

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: It's a bonus check. For you. From Wallace. Because the branch exceeded it's targets over the past quarter.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Wow, that's wonderful!

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: A quarter's three months. That's how long you've been gone.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Uh-huh.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: Uh-huh.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Uh-huh… [after awkward pause] Uh-huh. [Angela hands him the bonus check] Thank you. Great. Well, we're all up to speed.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Two seconds of the turd dog and he loses the biggest sale this branch has ever seen.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: [emotional] Do you have any idea what I had to do to get that sale from Jan? I mean, I went all out. All out. I mean like everything was out the whole week.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: He just waltzes back in here like he owns the chunky, lemon milk. Who needs him, right?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: God! I just don't know what we'd do. I mean, short of telling David Wallace that he was gone for three months.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I'd like to rat out Andy. Unfortunately, I have a bit of a boy-who-cried-wolf dynamic with David Wallace. Except, instead of a boy, I'm a man. And instead of a wolf, I cried genetically-engineered monster wolf.

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: I'm not going to rat on him. No, Andy gave me a second chance. So, the least I could do is let somebody else rat on him. Meredith, why don't you?

scenes.speaker: Meredith
scenes.line: Meredith Palmer ain't never been called no nark. Floozy? Yes. Alkie? Check. Einstein sarcastically? You bet. But never no nark. Vomit mop? Sure. Floor meat? That's me. Flesh hoover?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Hey!

scenes.speaker: Pete
scenes.line: Meredith, that's plenty. All right? That's more than plenty. Why does no one stop her?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Guys. I know that a lot of people are mad at Andy and, believe me, I am too. But, he has been through a lot and we all used to love him, right? So, if he's gonna get in trouble, just let it be his fault not ours. I don't want that on my hands.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Fine! The state he's in, Wallace will take one look at him and probably fire him anyway.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [appears approaching group, shaved and in a suit] What's going on in here, dirty players? Let's get back to busting some paper rhymes. Come on. [singing] Who's that girl? Who's that girl? It's Andy! [resumes talking] All right. Back to work.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: OK, I can tell you're mad at me. Do you wanna just, um, I don't know, tell me why?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I don't know. I thought that was a little weird. You told me Brian got fired for the whole warehouse thing. And you intentionally left out a kind of major, intimate detail. I don't know, Pam, I guess I just feel like a chump. Who knows less about his marriage than the sound guy.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I didn't tell you about the crying because I didn't want you to know how upset I was. Because it would've stressed you out and you're always saying how much you don't want more stress.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yeah, well. Yeah, OK. Well, then thank you. Thanks to both of you.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: It's not Brian's fault.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: No, you're right. And, and I'm not mad at Brian. And to be honest, I probably don't have any reason to be mad at all because I wasn't there. So, let's just forget about it.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: OK.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I need you guys to tell me all the highlights from the last three months in case David asks. Just a few things I could sprinkle into conversation. Any big sales or office gossip.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Well, we had the Scranton White Pages.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Not helpful. Let's stay positive, people. OK?

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: [enters] Hey guys.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Hey! David! How are ya? Ah, we were just having our weekly round table where we motivate each other. Not gonna lie, I get as much out of it as they do.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Sounds great. Don't let me interrupt. What ever you guys have been doing this last quarter, I couldn't be happier with the numbers.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Thank you.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Well, finish up. I'm gonna meet with Val about that warehouse guy you had to let go and you and I will talk in 15 minutes?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Great!

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: [leaving] Great job, everybody!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [whispEring] We had to let a warehouse guy go?!

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: You know Pam's mural? Well, Frank…

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [interrupting] … lit the whole thing on fire. It was crazy.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: What?!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: There was a fire in the warehouse?

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: The whole thing is in ashes. Fire department was here. It was in all the papers.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Whoa.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: This is what I'm talking about! This would be good to know. All right, what else?

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: We started selling balloons.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: What?!

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Yeah. And, uh, Kathy Ireland signed on as the official spokes-babe of Dunder-Mifflin.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: No kidding?

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Yeah. In the European billboards, she's gonna be topless.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Wow. Go Kathy. She's like 50.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: They're tasteful.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Good, good. What else?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Who knew the balloon game would be so lucrative? And thank god, right? We needed the income after the fire.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: What fire?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: The warehouse fire. Weren't you just down there? It's like burnt to ashes.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: It looked fine to me.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [catches on to the ruse] I am speaking metaphorically, of course. You know I have lots of irons in quote-unquote fire. Well, that's one of them. You know, making sure that the warehouse logistics is a well-oiled, properly-stoked fire.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: OK.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I think you'll agree I explained that pretty well.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: [preparing to leave] Thanks, Andy.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Thank you.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: All right. Everyone! [waves to office and exits]

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: [enters Andy's office to find him playing güiro] Fish sounds great.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yeah, I guess.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Really playing the scales, huh?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yeah, it just sort of sounds like noise to me now. You think I need a new fish?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: I don't love you anymore.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: What?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: I still like you, but you were gone a really long time. And, you didn't really email me all that much. You retweeted me, a lot to be fair. But I don't love you.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: OK, I get it. You're unhappy. I've been gone a long time and we lost a little bit of juju. But, you and me, we have a future. There is a lot of love here.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: I just said there isn't love.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: On your side. But there's tons on my side. It's gushing. We're just out of sync right now. But that's just timing, it's timing. I mean, my parents lasted 38, 40 years. They were never happy at the same time.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: I guess.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I mean, what do we have left? 35, maybe 40 years? If we're lucky. I mean, I have spent a lot of time in the sun.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: You got really sunburned.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I'm gonna be a prune in like, 3 years.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Ugh.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I know you may not be feeling love for me right now but, if you fake it, I won't be able to tell the difference. So, I'll feel good. And then, eventually, maybe, you'll actually start to love me again.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: You really think we can get that back?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yes. [hugs Erin] Come on. Totally.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: You know what? Maybe we should cancel that bottle of wine tonight.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Oh?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yeah. I just feel like I got a bunch of stuff to do in Philly and I'm sure you have stuff to do. So we can just… I don't know, drop me at the bus station?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Are you sure?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I just feel like we're gonna fight.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: [obviously hurt] Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: So… how 'bout let's not?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: OK. [they begin to leave]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh, um. [pulls item from bag and hands to Pam] Happy Valentine's Day. Sorry, I didn't have time to wrap it.

scenes.line: [gasps]
