scenes.speaker: Producer
scenes.line: Oh god.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: She yelled at me. I can't wash my eyeball. I can't do that. I can't.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Andy Bernard can't squirt water in his eye and act like it doesn't freak him out. But you know who can? Older Male Lab Assistant Number One.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Do you believe in me?

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: I believe I want to go home.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [throws plane far] Yeah! Ok! Beat that! [Erin throws plane, loses, Dwight laughs] Whoo! Ok.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Dammit! Dammit, god. [To Pete] Sorry. Yeah I'm fine. I'm fine. I got mad. Cause I don't like losing. I'm just gonna- Sorry I'm mad! I'm mad, I'm really mad. I wanted to win. We were gonna win a lot of money, I was gonna buy you a sweater. It's stupid. Just the whole contest is stupid. That's how it feels.

scenes.speaker: Pete
scenes.line: Yeah. [Erin kicks box] Whoa!

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Sorry I'm mad! I don't like losing! I thought I was going to win!

scenes.speaker: Pete
scenes.line: Ok [tries to help her] Hey hey hey, whoa.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Sorry. Sorry. I'm going to go upstairs and just…

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Oh, I made us a date to take my mom out to dinner to thank her for all that extra babysitting.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Well, you know how much I appreciate the opportunity to hang out with your mom more. So let me just put this in my calendar.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I acknowledge with gratitude that you are being kind and responsible enough to include it in your calendar.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Thank you. Your mom is a treasure.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Well, I appreciate that some opportunities can be unpleasant- [Jim's phone rings, he answers]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey that's work, hold on. Hey Wade, did Cole Hamels call back or what? Great. Good.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Uh, to speak my truth, I'd appreciate if you hung that up cause we were in the middle of a conversation. [Jim hangs up phone] I appreciate the sacrifice.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Ok to speak my truth, that was a little sarcastic. I think that's a little unfair.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Really? I've been putting the kids to bed by myself every night for a months. And you had to miss one phone call. Is that your truth, Jim? That's really your truth?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I guess I will swallow my truth.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Are you guys high? Because if so, to speak my truth, I would appreciate the sacrifice of including me in some hits off your kind buds.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: We're not high.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I wish we'd started this exercise six months ago. My heart just feels so… blocked up.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: The Mark 47 is ready for launch. [throws plane but it sticks to his hand] Less paste.

scenes.speaker: Director
scenes.line: Here we go. Rolling and… action!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [doing eyewash] AHHH! AHHH! AHHH! AHHH!!

scenes.speaker: Director
scenes.line: And cut. We can fix the sound in post.

scenes.speaker: Producer
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I can do a better one.

scenes.speaker: Producer
scenes.line: That's fine, we'll move on.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I said I can do a better one. Darryl…

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Action!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [eyewashes again] AHH! AHH! AHH!

scenes.speaker: Carla
scenes.line: Kid can act!

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yeah! Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: Each contestant will throw two aeroplanes.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: After you.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: Thank you. [plane loops up and falls at her feet] Oh god!

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: Angela's first throw, terrible. Dwight.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: [fake throws and drops plane] Oh! Oh man! It slipped out of my hand, what a whiff. Ah, how'd that happen? God. [Angela smiles]

scenes.speaker: Esther
scenes.line: We want you to win. Dwight told me about your situation. It's such a pity. Use the money wisely. [Angela looks disgusted]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Alright.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: Don't you dare tank this. [Dwight throws plane far, Angela fake throws and drops her plane]

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: And we have a winner. And it's Dwight. And it is everyone because this is over.

scenes.speaker: Creed
scenes.line: Two grand huh? I know a guy who can turn that into eight hundred dollars. And it's me.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: [To Esther] Well, I guess you needed the money more than me huh? Use it wisely.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: I was disappointed in Dwight today. He showed a weakness that was unbecoming. Even if he did do it for me. I don't need pity and I don't need charity. I have my dignity and that's enough. And as long as I have that, I'll be ok.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I know this was really weird, and it was really hard. But I think we're making progress. So I'm really sorry that I have to go but let's keep at this. Ok?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Ok. [intense moment where Jim leaves and Pam seems conflicted. She notices his umbrella and runs out to follow him]

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Jim! [hands him umbrella]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Thanks.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Alright, have a good trip.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Bye.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Bye. [walks away]

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey! [Runs after her and looks into her eyes] I… [hugs her tightly, Pam doesn't hug back]

scenes.speaker: Pastor
scenes.line: [Flashback to Jim & Pam's wedding] Love suffers long and is kind. It is not proud. Love bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Love never fails. [Pam hugs Jim back finally] And now these three remain: Faith, hope and love. But the greatest of these is love. [Pam kisses Jim]

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I love you.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I love you.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I'm taking some time off from work—well, my other work—because we needed it.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: It's great.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: It's great.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: The phone has been ringing off the hook. The guys in Philly are kind of going nuts.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: But that doesn't matter. This does. It's the only thing that matters. We've had some really nice days together.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Nice morning, too.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Beesly! Oh, my god.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Hey. Which tie makes me look like a guy who likes sofas? My agent's putting me up for a furniture commercial.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Ah, definitely blue.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Totally, right? So, Big Tuna, what's up? Back in the small pond?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: For now, yeah. I was spreading myself way too thin—

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Thin-sliced tuna. Carpaccio. Go on.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Uh, well, it took me a while, but I finally realized that I can't give 100% to two things at once you know.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Tell me about it, you know? I've been trying to act and manage this branch. Half the time I don't know if I'm wearing my stage makeup or my work makeup.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Huh. Well, you know, you can't have everything so you gotta ask yourself what makes you the happiest. You just go all in for what's most important. That's my new thing.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: [noticing Angela looking very unkempt] Is everything ok?

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: No. Everything is not okay. The county took my cats.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Wait, all of them?

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: Two sacks' worth. Apparently my apartment complex has rules about how many pets are too many for a studio. And while I was out picking Phillip up from daycare, they came. They came into my house.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: That's—that's awful, Angela. I'm so sorry.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: It's the [bleep] that lives downstairs. She's this uptight, judgmental shrew. You know the type.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: I've never met anyone like that.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: And they're gone. And I have no one left. Without my cats, I am utterly and completely alone.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: Angela, you still have your son.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: I guess.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Attention, everyone. May I have your attention? There are four new deadly weapons in this office. [kicking and punching] Basher, Thrasher, Crasher and—

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Smasher!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Smasher? No, where'd you get that? Fireball. This morning after hours of combat with some of the city's best teenagers I earned my black belt in Goju Ryu martial arts.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I had to find a new dojo after sensei Ira and I parted ways. My new sensei, sensei Billy, thought I had more than enough training to take the test. Turns out, sensei Ira was a bit of a shyster. Sensei Billy says most students don't spend $150,000 over 20 years to get their black belt.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: I would like to invite you all to my black belt ceremony, right here in the office at lunch, lunch not provided.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Fireball!

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Ah! [throws punch] That's how it's done.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: That's pretty good. I feel safe.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Hey, Erin. Is Andy in?

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Oh, is Andy in? Sorry, I thought you said "is Indian" and was like, "Is Indian what?" Is Indian food good? Is Indian jewelry pretty? Is Indian hair an expensive kind of wig? Yes, to all three, by the way.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Lately, I've been having a lot of trouble keeping track of Andy's calendar. His student film audition schedule is crazy hectic.

scenes.speaker: Erin
scenes.line: Yes, there's Andy! Andy is in. I'm a good receptionist, I know he's in.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: David Walrus, in his native habitat.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Hey, Andy. Can we go in your office and talk?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: This isn't going to be an easy conversation. I told Andy that he was on very thin ice when he snuck away from three months to the Caribbean. Then last week he used company money to buy a top-of-the-line photo printer. In his words, "The kind that's good for head shots." And yesterday, he asked me to pay for cheek implants. Claimed it's gonna boost office morale. Now, he's a good guy. But honestly, at some point, the ice gets too thin and you fall through. And that is when you get fired.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Andy—

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I'm gonna stop you right there. David, this documentary is going to air in two weeks. I feel like it's a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to pursue my dream.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Uh-huh, but—

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Every minute that I spend here is time not spent making audition videos for reality dating, cooking or singing shows. I got a real shot here. And I'll never be able to forgive myself if I blew it because I was too focused on my stupid paper company job. No offense.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: So you think you've been too focused on your job?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: At my last head shot sitting, I was so distracted wondEring what I was missing at work that I came across totally manic. And I was going for zany.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: So you—you want to quit Dunder Mifflin to pursue acting?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Well, no, actually. I see no reason to limit myself to just acting. I am pursuing fame of any kind. Could be singing, could be dancing. I don't—it just… I owe it to myself and my future fans.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Uh, well, I guess I can't stand in the way of a man's dream. And it seems like you have the gift.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Thank you, David.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: There's probably no way I can talk you into staying at this point, can I?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Nope. I have made up my mind. I'm really sorry.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Well, good luck.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Thank you. Not gonna need it.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Well that kind of worked out.

scenes.speaker: Creed
scenes.line: I think just anybody could be a star. My postman, the night janitor here, but Andy? No, definitely not. Charisma black hole.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh, Clark. I'm actually here today. Surprise! So I was wondEring if I could maybe have my desk back.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Right. Yeah. But, you know, I've actually been working pretty hard here on a daily basis. So, I kind of feel like I've earned this. I mean, you know?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: You totally have. You have earned this. But maybe I could be with my wife. Kind of the whole reason that I'm here.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Right. Well, I'm here to sell paper.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Wow.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: All right, Jim, look, I just got made junior salesman. Right? And—and Wallace is here today. And I don't him to just think of me as a customer service rep that sits in the annex. I mean, you can get that, right? Right? And what do you need more face time with Wallace for? You trying to get a second second job here?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: it's okay. You can sit in the annex.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: What?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I'll come visit you.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Okay. The annex it is. I'll be sitting at your desk if that's okay with you.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: That's fine with me. But be careful, it is very easy to get lost in Pete's beautiful, dead eyes.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Everyone, a little breaking news for ya. Just had a little chat with David Wallace. And, um, I'm taking a leave of absence from Dunder Mifflin, forever.

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: I can't say we didn't see it coming. But it's a sad day when anybody is fired. We're so sorry, Andy.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Uh, uh, uh, uh, Andy was not fired.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I wasn't fired. What are you talking about? I'm fired up, yes. Guys, I'm—I'm leaving to pursue my lifelong dream of being famous.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Oh, Andy.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yeah, so, I'll see you on the red carpet. See, that's how it works.

scenes.speaker: Phyllis
scenes.line: Andy sings beautifully. And he's really good at dancing. He's a good speaker. But there's just something there you don't want to look at.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey, how am I doing as your desk mate, by the way? You probably miss Clark.

scenes.speaker: Pete
scenes.line: Yeah, a little bit.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh, wow. But, um—Oh, I get that.

scenes.speaker: Pete
scenes.line: Oh, no, no, no. No it's cool.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I get it.

scenes.speaker: Pete
scenes.line: It's cool, man. I'm sure you and I will have our own thing.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Yeah. Definitely. Go Phillies, right. You don't watch baseball. I keep forgetting that.

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: I just think you're going into this a little fast.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: I'm 38, Darryl, how much slower should I go?

scenes.speaker: Darryl
scenes.line: Show business is cold. Let's say you get a job, which you probably won't. They're not gonna cut you any slack. You're meant for a job with lots and lots of slack.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: All right. I get it.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: The male is a funny species. We don't just tell each other how we feel, that's chick stuff. So instead of saying, "Hey, Andy, I love you, man. I don't want you to leave." You say something like, "Hey, Andy, you're making the worst mistake of your life. You're not talented." Well… right back at you, Darryl.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: [hugs Darryl] I'm gonna miss you too. Mmm!

scenes.speaker: Stanley
scenes.line: Andy's from the generation that thinks they should all be famous. What happened to the generation that knew you shut up, did your work, and died quietly from a heart attack?

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Could Andy make it as an entertainer? I don't know. You know who's really funny? This bird, in the park, that can't fly right. I'd pay to see him. But I don't have to cause the park is free!

scenes.speaker: Sensei Billy
scenes.line: I will now perform the ceremonial changing of the belts.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: He will now perform the ceremonial changing of the belts!

scenes.speaker: Sensei Billy
scenes.line: It's not a large room, I think they heard me.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Take my belt, master. I now submit to you every part of myself. [thrusts hips at Ira]

scenes.speaker: Sensei Billy
scenes.line: That's really ok. I'm mostly focused on the belt here.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Just slip it off my—Slip it off my hips.

scenes.speaker: Sensei Billy
scenes.line: Hold it—Take a step back. Take a step back. [they bow, then Dwight thrusts again] Okay, okay. I can't—I can't do this if you're gonna be thrusting like that, okay? I think we're gonna have to cut this off.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: He will now perform the ceremonial cutting-off-of-the-belt.

scenes.speaker: Angela
scenes.line: Dwight has been practicing karate for years. When we were dating, I would help him with his strength training. He would strap me to his chest in a baby Bjorn made for fat children and do lunges across the farm. It felt like I was flying.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: There it is. [everyone applauds]

scenes.speaker: Sensei Billy
scenes.line: Congratulations.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: We did it, we did it. I love you.

scenes.speaker: Sensei Billy
scenes.line: Okay.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Thanks. I will now perform my final kata forms. You're gonna watch me right?

scenes.speaker: Sensei Billy
scenes.line: Yes, I will. [Dwight starts doing karate]

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Sensei, you're not watching.

scenes.speaker: Sensei Billy
scenes.line: Yeah, I'm watching. Just do it.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Watching?

scenes.speaker: Sensei Billy
scenes.line: I'm watching.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Watch this part, okay?

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Sensei, do you generally do house calls like this?

scenes.speaker: Sensei Billy
scenes.line: Uh, you can just call me Billy. And no. No, but Dwight insisted. He wanted to receive his black belt in the place he loves most in the world.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: He said that? He's an odd guy, isn't he?

scenes.speaker: Sensei Billy
scenes.line: Yes. Irritating, also yes. But I gotta hand it to him, he's one of the most tenacious and determined men I've ever met. [Dwight finishes his routines and everyone applauds]

scenes.speaker: Esther
scenes.line: Oh! I'm am so proud of you, Schru-berry blue.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I really felt like I almost lost her, and—and nothing is worth that.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Well, I gotta tell you, Jim, a lot of guys in my circle? They wouldn't even change their golf schedule to shore up their marriage let alone their professional goals.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: Dude, there is no way that Jim is just back here to hang out with Pam.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: You did not just say that! You don't know Pam. She is really cool.

scenes.speaker: Clark
scenes.line: All I'm saying is, forget about my chair. He wants the manager's chair. And I thought you wanted that job.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Yeah, I did. But I made too many mistakes. It's out of my reach now. Besides, I think Jim would be a fine manager. I'd be happy to see Jim as manager.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: So, the reason that I called you in here is because Andy is moving on.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Again.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Again! And I'm looking for a new manager. And with his performance this year, I have been considEring Dwight. Am I crazy?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Not at all. It should be Dwight.

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: You sure?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: You're gonna want to invest in a lot more liability insurance, but, uh—

scenes.speaker: David Wallace
scenes.line: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey, if there is someone out there who loves paper more than Dwight, I definitely don't want to meet that person.

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: Andy, we just wondered if we could have a word.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: It's now or never.

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: Well, we just had a quick question about this decision of yours. You know, to leave a stable job and pursue a career in the entertainment business. In your late 30s. With no savings to fall back on. And no real connections in that business, which can be competitive.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Yeah, sure. What's your question?

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Our question is—it seems dumb.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Well, it's better than sticking around here and half-assing it, right?

scenes.speaker: Nellie
scenes.line: Of course. But what if you were to stay here, you know, and "full-ass" it? Um, really give it a go. Be the greatest manager in the history of this branch and in that way achieve the fame and immortality that you seek. Hmm?

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Nah. I like my plan better.

scenes.speaker: Kevin
scenes.line: Well, Andy, your plan sucks, okay? Nobody is going to hire you ever. You're too character-y to be a lead and you're not fat enough to be a great character actor.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: What?

scenes.speaker: Oscar
scenes.line: No, I don't think that he can make it as an actor. But, he also can't make it as an employee in an office, so why not go nuts with it?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey, are you still in charge of office supplies?

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Yes. Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I seem to have sticky not emergency where I grab it on the wrong end, and this happens.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Oh, boy. Um—

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: If you could help me out, that would be—

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: I could give you some beginner stickies?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Anything would help.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Here you go.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Oh, also, while you're at it, if you did have a salt packet, three tacks and some aspirin, that would be great. Oh, wow. You have that.

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: Mm-hmm.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Wow, that's—

scenes.speaker: Pam
scenes.line: It's all yours.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: You come so prepared. Aspirin.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: You wanna get rid of a headache, you sit on something sharp. Any sensei will tell you that.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: Hey, congratulations on that black belt, man. It's really great.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Thank you. So I saw you talking to Wallace earlier. Is he going to offer you the manager's job?

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: No. He was maybe thinking of you for it.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Yeah, right. I'm afraid that ship has sailed.

scenes.speaker: Jim
scenes.line: I wouldn't be too sure about that. Just saying.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Hello.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Well, hello.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Big day for you.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Big day for you.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Thank you.

scenes.speaker: Andy
scenes.line: Love the belt.

scenes.speaker: Dwight
scenes.line: Oh, yes.
